This cycle is unusual in a way worth recording: one of the source advisories (CVE-2026-48124, a workspace-controlled agent-harness hook configuration that triggered unsandboxed execution) names **Nexus-Hub's own distribution channel** as the attack surface, since the installer's entire job is shipping `.claude` hook configs to exactly the affected platforms. **1.1** authored `catalog/skills/security-operations/agentic-endpoint-hardening/SKILL.md` (244 lines, well under the 500-line norm): the config-write-then-executed model stated as three steps (a write that is legal and in scope, a trust step where a component outside the sandbox reads the file as its own config, and an execute step at host privilege on a trigger the agent no longer controls), a six-form escape taxonomy whose final column is *why each form passes inspection*, nine control layers each marked enforced / advisory / guidance-only, a privileged-local-daemon enumeration section, a seven-question platform audit checklist, nine Common Rationalizations, ten binary Verification items, and a Limits and Honest Boundaries section that states plainly what the catalog's own guardrails cannot do. Two structural decisions carry the phase. First, layers 4 and 5 are marked **guidance-only** rather than claimed as controls, because whether a vendor's language extension or version-control integration runs sandboxed is that vendor's architecture and no hook or permission file can change it; the correct action is to put them to the vendor as questions and record the answer as accepted risk. Second, the skill states that a pattern denylist is defense-in-depth and NOT a boundary, which is the source's own thesis applied honestly to the guardrails Phases 2 and 4 will ship. **The load-bearing deliverable is the normative execution-trigger surface list, and implementing it surfaced a real defect in the plan.** The plan lists the paths as one flat set including `core.hooksPath` and `core.fsmonitor`, and sub-task 2.1 asks `escalation-trigger.sh` to cover them, but that hook only ever receives a file path (`CLAUDE_FILE_PATH`) and can never match a git config key, so the flat form makes Phase 2.1 unimplementable as literally written. The list is therefore defined in three groups keyed by matching input: group A file paths and group C interpreter paths (matched against a write or edit target, so `escalation-trigger` owns them) and group B command-string patterns (matched against a shell command, so `git-guardrails` owns them), with `.git/config` added to group A as the mechanical consequence of `core.hooksPath` being agent-writable. A separate "project extension candidates" subsection lists commonly-present surfaces (`.vscode/settings.json`, `.devcontainer/*`, package-manifest lifecycle scripts) deliberately OUTSIDE the normative set, so promoting one is a conscious decision rather than silent scope drift. **1.2** authored `references/standards.md`, which carries the attribution debt out of the shipped body: the vendor, its framework, and its commercial product are named there and in the policy matrix and nowhere else, while the skill body describes component classes rather than product versions so it stays accurate as vendors patch. The optional framework fields were declared (`mitre_attack: [T1546, T1059, T1611]`, `d3fend_techniques: [D3-FA, D3-FH, D3-PA]`, `nist_csf: [PR.PS, DE.CM]`) but only after cross-checking every identifier against existing verified in-repo usage with live source URLs, rather than asserting them from memory, since a wrong framework ID in a security artifact is a real defect; D3-FH (File Hashing) turned out to already be an established catalog mapping and is precisely the countermeasure Phase 3's provenance ledger must implement, so the mapping pre-names a later control instead of decorating this one. **1.3** registered the skill by hand in the three registry files (no catalog rebuild, which would rewrite the whole tree), and added a seven-row matrix section covering every candidate (AC1 and AC7 `skill-native`, AC2 / AC4 / AC5 `re-full`, AC3 `re-partial`, AC6 mixed) plus two `drop-outright` rows for the vendor's commercial endpoint product (a third-party data processor watching the endpoint, on the MCP Registry Policy hard-no list) and for its framework adopted verbatim. Catalog counts move to **270 skills**, verified consistent across all four surfaces programmatically along with zero duplicate names and exact per-category and per-priority agreement. **1.4 hit the one genuine problem of the phase and it was instructive**: the routing gate FAILED on a 50% near-collision against `ai-agent-governance`, caused *by following the authoring guidance correctly*, since AGENTS.md requires a SKIP clause naming look-alike skills and doing so imports their vocabulary into the token set that the pairwise detector then flags. The detector cannot distinguish "mentioned to exclude" from "overlaps with". The routing result settled it: all six positives outrank every competitor (the runner scores against every other skill) and the `neg-service-governance` case routes away, so routing is empirically correct in both directions and the pair was allowlisted with that evidence recorded as its reason. Adding a reciprocal SKIP clause to `ai-agent-governance` would be the better fix and matches the `technical-documentation` precedent, but its missing clause is a pre-existing gap this phase did not create, so it is tracked as DF-1 rather than silently fixed or silently dropped. **Gates**: all 13 validators pass individually (`make` is unavailable on this Windows host), bundle audit 0 errors, routing gate PASS, compression gate PASS, catalog security scan clean, ShellCheck 0, and a mechanical markdown style self-check PASS on all four touched Markdown files. Discoverability was verified end-to-end rather than inferred from counts: the skill-server catalog loads 270, `get_skill` returns the record with the right category, and the frontmatter parses as real YAML with `summary_l0` at 12 words and `overview_l1` at 146. **A test-baseline finding worth the effort**: the repo-wide suites show 103 failures on this host, and rather than assume they were pre-existing, a detached worktree at clean `develop` was used to prove it, reproducing identical counts (`catalog/hooks/tests` 99 failed / 361 passed / 36 skipped, plus 1 in `tests/validators` and 3 in `tests/installer`, every one a `bash.EXE` exit-127 path-resolution failure that never reaches an assertion). Aggregate 2129 passed, 103 pre-existing environmental failures, 0 introduced, matching the v3.15.5 advisory exactly. That constraint is escalated to **HO-1** rather than filed as a mere advisory, because Phase 2 ADDS hook tests and its stability gate requires them to pass, so a verification route (CI, a POSIX shell with a resolvable path, or a path-normalizing harness fix) has to be chosen before Phase 2 starts. CI needed no edit: the existing `validate` job already covers skill validation, the routing gate, and registry integrity, and already carries path filters, concurrency cancel-in-progress, pip caching, and cost-gated matrix legs. On Claude Code the effort knob is a user action, so `/effort max` was surfaced rather than switched. **The headline outcome is a correction, not a feature.** Before writing any Phase 3 code I tested the plan's central safety claim, that `check_base_template_parity.py` makes the hard rail physical so "a model-named line in a shared `base-*.md` fails the build". It is FALSE. Three fixture cases: (A) the same model-named line added to all five `base-*.md` inside an invariant section PASSES; (B) a model-named line in one file in a non-invariant section PASSES; (C) the control, a divergent invariant section, is correctly CAUGHT. The guard compares the five templates to EACH OTHER, so lockstep is precisely what it verifies, and case A is not a corner case: it is exactly what a well-behaved auto-apply engine respecting the lockstep rule would produce. The plan's Definition of Done ("a model-specific finding provably cannot reach a shared body (parity guard proves it)") therefore cannot be satisfied by the guard it names. **3.1 classifier**: built `scripts/apply_prompting_edits.py` (bundled) with four routes. Scope must be EXACTLY `model-agnostic-candidate` to be eligible; missing, empty, unrecognized, and even differently-cased values route to profile-only, so ambiguity always resolves to model-specific. Only six shared-body surfaces are targetable (skill description / trigger phrase / rationalization / verification, command body, base-template line), so the feature cannot touch installers, hooks, `data/`, READMEs, or CI. **The hard rail was implemented in the engine, where it can actually bind**: an edit may not INTRODUCE a model identifier into a shared body regardless of its declared scope, detected by diffing identifiers in the edit's new text against those already in its old text, so rewording or removing an existing mention stays allowed while smuggling a new name in does not. Documented with the evidence in `references/edit-routing.md`. **3.2 apply loop**: creates or checks out `feat/tune-prompting-<stamp>` from the integration branch (stamp caller-supplied, never generated internally, since a workflow runtime has no clock) and asserts HEAD is that branch and is not main/master/develop BEFORE touching a file. Each eligible edit is snapshotted, applied, and guarded against the full suite; all-pass keeps it, any-fail restores the snapshot and quarantines the edit with the failing guard's name and output, and the run continues rather than aborting. Edits stay uncommitted unless `--commit` is passed, and every run ends by stating the branch is for human merge. **A second plan correction**: the plan specified `git checkout -- <file>` for the revert, which is wrong when two eligible edits target the same file, since it reverts to HEAD and would silently discard an earlier SURVIVING edit along with the failing one. An in-memory snapshot restores exactly the failed edit, and `test_a_failing_second_edit_does_not_destroy_a_surviving_first_edit` guards it. **3.3 gap report**: deterministic from one run's results, with applied / quarantined / profile-only / rejected sections, a branch diff summary, and paste-ready known-gaps entries per quarantined edit and per unverified model. **3.4 tests**: 68 tests, 83% branch coverage on the engine. The hard-rail proof ships as a PAIR: one test pins the parity guard's real permissive behavior (so the false premise cannot quietly return, and so the test fails loudly if the guard ever gains content checks), and its partner proves the engine blocks the exact edit the guard misses. Two of the three initial failures were the tests doing their job: the `base-*.md` glob picked up non-lockstep files like `base-google-shared.md` (fixed by importing the guard's own `LOCKSTEP_FILES`), and a model-id regex missed the `deepseek-v3` letter-then-digit shape. The third was a fixture that lacked a genuinely repeated anchor. **A gap was closed rather than deferred**: MT-4 originally recorded that the default guard suite is never executed (tests inject fake guards for speed); its realistic half is now covered by a near-free test asserting each default guard names a `.py` script that exists, so a renamed gate fails at test time instead of silently quarantining every edit on a live run. **Residual, stated plainly and recorded as DF-2**: the engine's rail binds the engine, so the accurate claim is "this feature cannot autonomously write model-specific content into a shared body", NOT "model-specific content cannot exist in a shared body". A human hand-edit bypasses it. A catalog-wide leakage gate was considered and deliberately not added: the catalog already carries 6 model mentions across the `base-*.md` set and 10 SKILL.md files, several legitimate (`model-routing` documents tiers by name), so it would fail on day one and triaging those is a separate decision. It would need no installer edit (the `DEV_ONLY_SCRIPTS` allowlist covers repo-internal guards). **Gates**: all 12 validate gates exit 0, `tests/skills` is 179 passed / 3 skipped, the routing gate stays green, and the skill validator reports 0 errors / 0 warnings. SKILL.md is 159 lines. **CI / installer**: no edit needed, same reasoning as Phase 2. **Known gaps**: DF-2 and MT-4 added; NI-2, DF-1, MT-1, MT-2, MT-3, NI-3 carry. Phase 6.4 must reword the Definition-of-Done item that names the parity guard, or explicitly accept the DF-2 residual. Phases 4-6 pending.

## [2026-07-27] - v3.15.5 model-prompting-research Phase 2: research engine and skill scaffold

Implemented Phase 2 on `feat/model-prompting-research` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 6 is the terminal gate). This phase builds the web-research half: the skill that houses the capability, the fan-out that reads each vendor's own documentation, the verification bar every claim must clear, and the budget that bounds it. **Model-routing pre-flight**: same picker sentinel as Phase 1 (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), so there was no fresher roster to re-score against and the session's Opus-class model already matched the plan's recommendation. **2.1 skill scaffold**: authored `SKILL.md` at 131 lines (well inside the 500-line norm) with every Tier-1 field inside budget (description 243/250 chars, `summary_l0` 13/15 words, `overview_l1` 148/150 words). The body fences the skill off from its two same-category near-neighbours explicitly (`model-routing` picks a model, `prompt-engineering` tunes one prompt) and carries the scope hard rail as a table, the degradation ladder, the budget section, a bundled-resources table, seven Common Rationalizations each citing a concrete failure mode, and an eight-item binary Verification checklist. Procedure detail was pushed to a new `references/research-runbook.md` per the three-tier norm rather than inflating the body. **2.2 research fan-out**: added `assets/research-workflow.js`, a Dynamic-Workflow TEMPLATE to adapt (never run verbatim), pipelining per model: search and actually FETCH the vendor's own primary sources (official prompting docs, cookbook, model card, changelog), extract discrete testable claims, then refute each claim with three independent skeptics weighing source authority, currency, and actionability. A claim survives only when a primary source supports it AND a majority fail to refute it, and `confidence` follows the margin, so a barely-surviving claim is not recorded with the same weight as a unanimous one. Scope may be tightened by a verifier but never loosened, because loosening is the direction that makes a claim eligible for a shared body. The three mandatory rules are inline, including an explicit offline rung that writes nothing and re-stamps nothing. **2.3 budget and kill switch**: a 60k-output-token default per-model cap with a one-branch reserve checked BEFORE each branch starts, so the run stops starting branches at the ceiling instead of dying mid-verification; since writes happen per model, a capped run leaves a valid partial layer plus a logged shortfall. **Deterministic planner and writer**: added the bundled `scripts/write_model_prompting_profile.py`. This is an in-spirit realization rather than a named sub-task, and it exists because Phase 2.4's acceptance ("the claim schema written by the synthesis step, against the Phase 1 validator") needs a deterministic writer to assert against, and because workflow scripts have no filesystem access so the caller must scout the work-list anyway. `plan` computes which models still need research (unprofiled, claimless, or wholly-unverified, which correctly still flags the Phase 1 seed); `write` validates and merges verified claims, re-stamps the roster and hash, regenerates the Markdown mirrors, and refuses the ENTIRE write on any malformed claim so a bad research result fails loudly instead of quietly degrading the layer. Same precedent as v3.15.4's `visual_qa_score.py`. **2.4 tests**: 51 tests in `tests/skills/test_model_prompting_research.py`, 91% branch coverage on the writer (measured with the same `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` plumbing Phase 1 needed, since the CLI is exercised as a subprocess). The load-bearing assertion is a cross-check: whatever the writer produces must pass the repo-level structural gate, so the bundled writer and the repo validator cannot drift apart. **The routing eval earned its keep immediately.** Shipped `evals/trigger-cases.json` (4 positives, 5 near-miss negatives drawn from the SKIP clause), matching the v3.15.3 standard for a new skill, and it FAILED on first run against my own description: the SKIP clause read "SKIP picking a model", and "picking" stems to the same token as the "pick the cheapest model" near-miss, so the weakest positive (0.57) missed the strongest negative (0.50) by less than the 1.15x margin. The fence I wrote to prevent mis-routing was pulling the look-alike closer, which is invisible on re-reading the prose because it lives in the scorer's token space. Reworded to "choosing a model" and added "conventions"; the gate now passes across all 269 skills. Two other defects were caught and fixed during stabilization: the template documented the no-clock rule using the literal `Date.now()` syntax, which tripped the test forbidding that call (reworded rather than weakening a strict test), and a test helper passed `models` both positionally and via kwargs. **CI**: no edit needed. `ci.yml` already runs `pytest tests/skills -v`, and its `validate` job already triggers on `catalog/**` with concurrency and caching. No installer edit either: the bundled script rides the recursive skill-folder copy, and only repo-level `scripts/*.py` need registration. **Working-tree note**: three untracked docs files unrelated to this work appeared mid-session (`v3.15.7-comparison-raptor-loop-hunt.md`, `v3.17.0-comparison-interface-craft-skills.md`, `v3.17.0-agent-autonomy-toggle.md`), so this phase staged its files explicitly rather than with `git add -A`. **Gates**: all 12 validate gates exit 0, the orphan-bundle audit reports 0 unreferenced files for the new bundle, `tests/skills` is 117 passed / 3 skipped, and `tests/validators` is 363 passed with only the pre-existing Windows-host failure. **Known gaps**: NI-1 RESOLVED (the bundle is distributable now that `SKILL.md` exists); NI-3 added (269 skills on disk vs 268 in `data/`, registered in Phase 4.3); MT-3 added (the fan-out itself is agent behavior and is not unit-run; the deterministic ends and the template's rules are). NI-2, DF-1, MT-1, MT-2 carry unchanged. Phases 3-6 pending.

## [2026-07-27] - v3.15.5 model-prompting-research Phase 1: profile-layer contract and validators

Implemented Phase 1 of the model-prompting-research plan on a new branch `feat/model-prompting-research` cut from `develop` at v3.15.4 (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 6 is the terminal refactor + known-gaps + CI/CD gate, so no release-readiness workflow ran). This is the foundation phase: it establishes the per-model prompting profile layer as a real, schema-validated data spine that every later phase reads and writes, rather than an ad-hoc format invented mid-research. **Model-routing pre-flight**: the plan recommends a strong reasoning tier at high effort; `detect-platform` returned `claude-code` and `enumerate-models` returned the picker sentinel (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), so there was no fresher roster to re-score against and the session's Opus-class model already matched the recommendation. **1.1 the layer**: created `catalog/skills/ai-development/model-prompting-research/` carrying the authoritative machine index `assets/profiles-index.json` (schema 1.0.0), the contract doc `references/schema.md`, and one seed mirror `references/models/claude-opus-5.md`. The index fixes `meta` (a sorted, unique `roster`; a `roster_hash` defined as `sha256` of the sorted roster joined by newlines; a `roster_source` provenance tag; `platform`; `last_verified`) and per-model claim objects (`claim`, `source_url`, `confidence`, `scope`, optional `note`). Because live enumeration was unavailable, the roster was read from the Claude Code model picker and tagged `roster_source: picker`, and the seed claim is tagged `confidence: unverified` with a TODO rather than being dressed up as verified: writing a "verified" claim with an invented citation would be fabrication, and the whole feature exists to make claims earn their status through an adversarial-verify pass. The seed is also scoped `model-specific`, which demonstrates the ambiguous-defaults-to-model-specific safe default and keeps it out of shared bodies by construction. **1.2 the hard gate**: added `scripts/verify_model_prompting_profiles.py` (stdlib-only, offline) and wired it into the `make validate` target and the CI `validate` job. It checks the three top-level keys, the whole `meta` block, roster sortedness / uniqueness / hash self-consistency, every claim's shape with allowed `confidence` and `scope` values, and a BOTH-directions match between index models and `references/models/*.md`; it rejects unknown keys at every level so a `sources_url` typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored. It is STRUCTURAL ONLY by design: it never reads the clock and never enumerates a roster. It also discovers the bundle at the flattened `skills/<name>/` installed layout as well as the in-repo catalog path, so the installed copy is usable. **1.3 the advisory checker**: added `scripts/check_model_prompting_freshness.py`, which compares the recorded roster against a live roster passed on argv (the caller enumerates; the script itself makes no network call) and reports IN SYNC, DRIFTED (added, removed, or a roster whose hash was not re-stamped), or UNKNOWN. It exits 0 on every path unless the explicit `--strict` flag is passed, and it is deliberately absent from `make validate` and CI: gating freshness would let a vendor shipping a model on a Tuesday wedge every release, which is exactly the coupling this design avoids. It imports `find_bundle` and `roster_hash` from the validator so the two scripts can never disagree about where the layer lives or how a roster hashes. **1.4 installer registration** (an ask-first area, approved before editing): registered both scripts in BOTH installers next to the existing `generate_report.py` precedent, then verified them for real by extracting the actual `install_templates` (bash) and `Install-Templates` (PowerShell) function bodies out of the installers and running each against a throwaway HOME. Both scripts land byte-identically under `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/` on both hosts, the installed validator runs standalone, and the repo's generalized guard `test_installers_copy_every_scripts_dir_py_file` passes. A name-level diff of the two copy blocks shows the only delta is `generate_release_changelog.ps1`, a legitimately PowerShell-only sibling, so shared-script parity holds. **1.5 tests, gates, CI**: 62 new tests across `tests/validators/test_verify_model_prompting_profiles.py` and `tests/validators/test_check_model_prompting_freshness.py`, subprocess-invoked via the shared `runner` fixture to match the established validator-test pattern. They cover the shipped seed, bundle discovery including the flattened layout, one parametrized case per documented structural rule, the wrong-JSON-shape guards a hand-edit would produce, bidirectional mirror matching, the two deliberate non-checks (roster coverage and freshness), all three drift verdicts, and the non-blocking contract itself (every advisory path exits 0; only `--strict` propagates). Measured coverage required explicit plumbing because the tests spawn subprocesses: with `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` plus `coverage combine` and branch coverage on, the validator is at 94%, the freshness checker at 97%, and the pair at 97% against the 80% gate. All `make validate` gates exit 0 (run individually, since `make` is unavailable on this Windows host), ShellCheck exits 0 on `installer.sh` and `install.sh`, and `installer.ps1` AST-parses. **Baseline discipline**: the repo shows 103 pre-existing test failures on this Windows host, so a detached worktree at `develop` (`b613b251`) was used to prove they are not regressions; the counts are byte-identical (`catalog/hooks/tests` 99 failed / 361 passed / 36 skipped, `test_session_query_extract` 1, `test_branch_flag` 3). Phase 1 introduced zero new failures. Note also that the two pytest trees must run as SEPARATE invocations, as `ci.yml` documents; combining them makes pytest adopt a nested `pyproject.toml` as rootdir and produces a large misleading failure count. **CI**: added the validator as a step in the existing `validate` job rather than creating a separately path-filtered job (recorded as DF-1). That job already runs on any non-docs change and already carries concurrency cancel-in-progress and pip caching, so a dedicated job for two fast stdlib scripts would add a cold runner instead of saving minutes; the same call was made at v3.15.1 QG-1, v3.15.2 DF-1, and v3.15.4 Phase 6.3. The new pytests ride the existing `tests/validators` step. **Incidental cleanup**: an aborted full-installer dry run left `extensions/claude-usage-monitor/package-lock.json` modified by a transitive npm bump; it was reverted, so the commit carries only Phase 1 files. **Known gaps**: NI-1 (the bundle is not distributed until Phase 2 adds `SKILL.md`, which is the intended intermediate state, since `find_skill_dirs` discovers a skill only by that file), NI-2 (three of four rostered models are UNVERIFIED and the seed claim is unverified, both resolved by the Phase 2 research run), DF-1 (the CI-job placement deviation above), MT-1 (nothing asserts the `make validate` and CI wiring, a pre-existing class of gap), and MT-2 (subprocess coverage is not measured in CI for the whole `tests/validators` tree). Docs-layout audit: the `docs/v3/v3.15/` tree is canonical (`comparisons/`, `development/`, `plans/`, `known-gaps.md`) with no empty dirs, duplicates, or scratch docs, so no cleanup report file was created, matching the v3.15.0-.4 precedent. Phases 2-6 pending.

This is the plan's centerpiece: it replaces the single-pass Step 9 with a genuine iterative loop that renders the output, grades each SEGMENT against its source and the measurable Phase 1-4 rubric, adversarially verifies, synthesizes fixes, and re-renders until the page-level bar passes or a cap / budget is hit, degrading gracefully when a headless browser or the workflow runtime is absent. Implementing the phase is single-agent authoring (the fan-out is the SUBJECT I author, a template, not the METHOD), so no Dynamic Workflow was spawned. **5.1 rubric reference**: authored `references/visual-qa-rubric.md` - the per-segment grading rubric assembling metrics from Phases 1-4 (full-width band >= ~95% at 1920px; image sizing / crop / dead-space; annotation-overlay fidelity vs the source; imagery integration into starved sections; readability / layout integrity), split into STRUCTURAL (deterministic, scorer-checkable) and AGENT-VISION (screenshot judgment) kinds, with a per-segment score schema (criterion -> pass/fail/n-a + severity + kind + evidence) and a binary page-level pass bar (no open high-severity finding; n/a criteria and a correctly-degraded low-confidence annotated figure do not block). **5.2 fan-out template**: added `assets/visual-qa-workflow.js`, a Dynamic-Workflow TEMPLATE (adapt, not run verbatim) following the AGENTS.md workflow-as-skill-bundle pattern: `export const meta`, then a `pipeline()` over segments that grades each against the rubric + source (StructuredOutput `FINDINGS_SCHEMA`) and, without a barrier, adversarially verifies each high-severity finding with an independent skeptic (`VERDICT_SCHEMA`, majority-refute kills it), then synthesizes a confirmed-fix list, rebuilds, and re-grades in a capped loop. It encodes the THREE mandatory rules inline: graceful degradation (Dynamic Workflows -> isolated subagents -> single sequential agent; headless render -> the structural scorer), scope-first token caution (a 5-15x multiplier, calibrate on one segment, confirm before scale), and skill-native (no outbound call / dependency / credential, LOCAL render), cross-linking `[[agent-orchestration-primitives]]` + `[[ai-billing-safeguards]]`. **5.5a scorer**: shipped `scripts/visual_qa_score.py`, the deterministic STRUCTURAL scorer (stdlib-only, no network, headless-optional) that scores a generated `.html` against the structural rubric subset (full-width band via the injected `--page-max`/`--gutter` clamp heuristic; the `max-height: 80vh` + `object-fit: contain` image caps; annotated-overlay well-formedness, a `.fig-annotated` with zero `.fig-region` is the dropped-overlay defect; the imagery-integration count against a supplied expectation; offline-cleanliness + well-formedness) and returns per-criterion findings + the binary pass bar. It is the structural-review degradation path AND the concrete realization of the Phase-1 `measure_widest_band` "gate seed". n/a criteria (full-width when aspect != full, imagery without an expectation, annotation without a `.fig-annotated`) never block. **5.3 Step 9 rewrite**: rewrote SKILL.md Step 9 into the render -> segment-and-grade -> adversarially-verify -> synthesize-fixes -> re-render iterative loop with the full degradation ladder (browser vs structural scorer; Dynamic Workflows vs subagents vs single agent) and the scope-first / budget caution, and updated the Bundled Resources list with the rubric, the scorer, and the workflow template. **5.4 verification + rationalizations**: added binary Verification items (full-width band metric, image sizing, annotation-overlay fidelity, imagery-integration gate, loop-ran-and-converged-or-degraded) and four Common Rationalizations rows (one-render-pass-is-enough, grade-whole-page-not-per-segment, skip-verification-because-expensive, skip-QA-without-a-browser), each tied to one of the four observed defects. **5.5b tests**: `tests/skills/test_presentify_visual_qa.py` (10 cases, dependency-free): the scorer flags each seeded structural defect (narrow full-width, missing image caps, dropped overlay, zero imagery on a consented expectation, a non-offline page) and passes a clean fixture and the n/a cases; the CLI exit codes (0 pass / 1 fail / 2 usage) hold; the workflow template carries the three mandatory rules + cross-links; the rubric lists all five criteria + the pass bar + the structural/agent-vision split. **CI**: no edit - the scorer is under the bundle `scripts/**` path filter (and ruff-linted by the presentify-extractor "Lint the bundled scripts" step), and the new test under `tests/skills/**` (both wired in Phase 2). **Gates**: ruff clean on the scorer + test; orphan-bundle audit 0 errors (the rubric, scorer, and workflow template are all referenced from SKILL.md); unicode 0 errors; SKILL.md 229 lines (within the 800 soft cap); full `tests/skills` suite 65 pass / 3 skip (the 3 skips are the headless-render checks from Phases 1-3). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is authoritative. **Scope note**: `scripts/visual_qa_score.py` (5.5a) is the deterministic realization the plan's 5.5 test acceptance ("the rubric scorer flags a seeded defective fixture on each criterion") requires and that Phase 1 pre-named the "gate seed"; the AGENT-VISION grading and the Dynamic-Workflow fan-out stay behavioral (documented + template-asserted, not unit-run). **Known gaps**: MT-3 added (the loop's agent-vision grading, fan-out, and e2e sample-deck smoke are behavioral; the structural scorer is the unit-tested backbone; the e2e is a browser-gated / release-time check). MT-1/MT-2, DF-1/DF-2/DF-3, and BG-1 carry from prior phases, untouched. Phases 6-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 4: reliable stock/mix imagery integration

Implemented Phase 4 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan on `feat/presentify-visual-fidelity` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal gate). Made a stock/mix imagery choice reliably put relevant, license-verified images into image-starved sections, so "mix" never silently produces zero images. This phase is pipeline WIRING (command + skill + reference prose) plus tests; the fetch helper (`scripts/fetch_stock_media.py`) is complete since v3.13/v3.14 and was NOT changed. **4.1 up-front consent**: folded the build-time-network / generation CONSENT into the up-front batched design round in both `catalog/commands/presentify.md` and SKILL.md Step 2. When the resolved imagery tier is `stock`, `mix` / `auto`, or `ai`, consent is now captured with the four design choices (not as a separate mid-run prompt), and a consented run is EXPECTED to attempt integration in Step 6 (silence is a bug, not a default). Preserved every invariant: the default `procedural` tier and every non-interactive run stay fully offline and never fetch; the consent gate stays load-bearing (`fetch_stock_media.py` performs no network without `--consent`, degrading with a recorded reason); a recalled memory / saved preference never pre-answers the consent. **4.2 starved-section detection**: defined an image-starved-section detection pass in SKILL.md Step 6 (concise) and `references/interactive-features.md` Tier 2 (full): after the structure is drafted, identify each section that carries NO source visual AND would be materially clearer with one (a concrete subject); derive SHORT relevance keywords from the section TOPIC (never the raw source document text, which keeps the compiling-content trap closed); run `fetch_stock_media.py --consent` per starved section (Openverse-first, then Wikimedia, Pexels when configured); take ONE highly-relevant, license-verified asset and place it per the Phase 2 sizing rules with relevance-and-restraint (a loosely-related photo is worse than none). **4.3 integration gate**: added a SKILL.md Verification item and a Tier 2 rubric criterion (feeding Phase 5): a consented `stock` / `mix` / `ai` run MUST integrate at least one relevant, license-verified asset into each image-starved section OR record a per-section reason; a consented run that integrated ZERO assets with no reason FAILS. The offline + license-safety gates are unchanged. **4.4 setup-media (VERIFIED, no change)**: confirmed `nexus-hub setup-media` already exists and stores the Pexels key at `~/.nexus-hub/config/media.env` at mode 0600 - it is wired in `scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py` (`cmd_setup_media` dispatches to `scripts/setup_media_keys.py`), listed in `--help`, present in both installers, and tested by `tests/skills/test_media_key_setup.py`; the first-time-video note in the command/skill already points at it. So this was a verification, NOT an "Ask first" installer addition, and no installer edit was made. **4.5 tests**: `tests/skills/test_presentify_stock_fetch.py` (14 cases) exercises the fetcher's enforcement layer with the network functions monkeypatched (no real request, no `requests` dependency, so it runs in both the deps-light `ci.yml` tests job and the presentify-extractor workflow): the consent gate (no `--consent` = no network + degrade code 3, with a boom-if-called guard proving no network), a consented Openverse run integrating + crediting a base64-embedded asset (offline `data:` URI, CC0 provenance), the free-for-commercial-use allow-list rejecting NonCommercial / NoDerivatives (parametrized `is_commercial_cc` + `accept_candidate`), and degrade-always-carries-a-reason (so the integration gate never sees silent zero-integration). CI: no edit - the fetcher is under the bundle path filter and the new test under `tests/skills/**` (both wired in Phase 2); the setup-media test's 0600 assertion is already posix-guarded. **Gates**: ruff clean on the new test; orphan audit 0 errors; unicode 0 errors; SKILL.md 217 lines (within the 800 soft cap); full `tests/skills` suite 55 pass / 3 skip (the 3 skips are the headless-render checks from Phases 1-3). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is authoritative. **Known gaps**: MT-2 added (the agent-side per-section detection + placement is LLM-native, not deterministically unit-testable; the fetcher enforcement is unit-tested and the end-to-end integration is graded by the Phase 5 visual-QA loop). DF-1/DF-2/DF-3 and BG-1 carry from prior phases, untouched. Phases 5-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 3: annotated-figure overlay recreation

Implemented Phase 3 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan on `feat/presentify-visual-fidelity` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal gate). When a source figure is a base image carrying author-added annotations (map regions, colored zones, callout labels, leader lines), those annotations are now recreated as a registered interactive overlay on the extracted base image, instead of being demoted to a textual list beside a flat map. **3.1 protocol (reference)**: `references/figure-reconstruction.md` part 1 records an `annotated: true` signal alongside the base `classification`, and part 5 is rewritten from a binary (full SVG rebuild OR flat enhanced-original) into a THREE-way decision that adds the OVERLAY-RECREATION path: keep the base image at native resolution; recreate each annotation in a registered overlay layer normalized to the base image with PERCENTAGE coords (so it scales); make it interactive (hover/focus highlight, click-toggle legend, keyboard focus, a lightbox that moves base + overlay together); and carry the provenance badge + view-original toggle. The side-text list is kept as an ACCESSIBLE COMPLEMENT, never the replacement (the exact defect being fixed). **3.2 gate + accounting (reference)**: part 4 gates overlays on confidence (high/medium recreate; low ships the enhanced original + textual complement with NO fabricated regions), part 6 adds the overlay to the model round-trip, and the coverage-reconciliation output format gains an `[overlay-reconstructed]` line plus the resolution-list update. **3.3 extractor**: `scripts/extract_content.py` now captures PPTX overlay shapes drawn over a picture as an `annotations` array on that image block. `_iter_pptx_shapes` was extended to carry the enclosing group name, and the `_extract_pptx` inner loop became a two-pass walk: pass 1 finds picture placed-rectangles; pass 2 assigns any non-picture shape whose CENTER lies inside a picture AND whose area is smaller than it as an annotation (image-relative bbox, text, solid fill/line hex colors best-effort, group name) and CONSUMES it so it is not also emitted as a stray text block; pass 3 builds blocks in document order and attaches the annotations to the image block. A shape beside (not over) a picture stays normal content. `content-model.md` documents the new `annotations` field (image-relative bbox rationale) and `extraction-runbook.md` documents the PPTX capture + the flattened-PDF agent-vision path. **Extractor regression proof**: the committed extractor and the new extractor BOTH score 41 PASS / 4 FAIL on `verify_phase1.py`, where the 4 FAILs are environmental (no `rapidocr-onnxruntime` locally, so scanned-page OCR degrades) and all 8 PPTX checks pass - so the two-pass restructure changed nothing for the existing fixtures. **3.4 builder + tests**: the deterministic baseline builder was extended to recreate the overlay from the `annotations` metadata (`build_presentation.py` `_render_annotated_figure` + `assets/presentation-template.html` overlay CSS), because it is the only deterministic producer of "authored HTML" the phase's end-to-end test can assert against. It renders a `.fig-annotated` figure: the base image, a `.fig-overlay` layer of percentage-positioned `.fig-region` elements (each with its label, fill via a `--region-color` custom property, `tabindex` + `role`/`aria-label`), a `.fig-legend`, a provenance badge, and a CSS-ONLY view-original toggle (a hashed-id checkbox + `<label for>` driving `.fig-toggle:checked ~ .fig-figure .fig-overlay { display: none }`, no JS). Offline (the self-check passes; hex colors and percentage coords trip no fetch guard). `tests/skills/test_presentify_annotations.py` (5 cases): the extractor captures the two over-map shapes as annotations (0..1 bbox, labels, fill) and leaves the sidebar text as a paragraph; the end-to-end annotated-map PPTX -> extractor -> builder -> HTML contains a registered overlay (one `.fig-region` per source region, the labels, a legend, a view-original toggle); the dependency-free builder test asserts the region percentage coords + provenance + offline; the no-annotations fixture emits NO fabricated regions (the low-confidence/flattened degrade); and a headless-optional toggle test skips-with-note without a browser. **CI**: no edit needed - `presentify-extractor.yml` already runs the whole `tests/skills/` dir under a `tests/skills/**` path filter (Phase 2), so the new test file is covered; concurrency + pip cache present; no headless job. **Gates**: ruff clean on the extractor + builder + test; orphan audit 0 errors; unicode 0 errors; full `tests/skills` suite 40 pass / 3 skip (the 3 skips are the headless-render checks). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is authoritative. **Scope note**: the builder-overlay rendering (`3.4a`) is not one of the plan's named sub-tasks (which are reference + extractor + tests), but the plan's 3.4 acceptance ("assert the authored HTML contains a registered overlay layer") requires a deterministic HTML producer, so the builder consuming the extractor's `annotations` is the in-spirit realization that makes Phase 3 end-to-end testable. **Known gaps**: DF-3 added (the overlay-detection heuristic - center-inside plus smaller-than-picture - would capture full-slide-background body text; the LLM-native path applies judgment; documented in the runbook gotchas). DF-1/DF-2 and BG-1 carry from Phases 1-2, untouched. Phases 4-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 2: image sizing and placement discipline

Implemented Phase 2 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan on `feat/presentify-visual-fidelity` (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal gate). Gave every extracted image a prominence-appropriate, bounded box with no meaningful-content crop and no dead space at 100% zoom, and named the inverse-of-contact-sheet failure (a secondary image ballooned to hero scale) as a defect. Command + skill + references + docs behavior only; no `base-*.md` lockstep, no installer edit, no new outbound call / dependency / credential. **2.1 measurable rules**: extended `references/interactive-features.md` "Prominence preservation" with four image-box rules, each carrying an observable metric the Phase 5 QA gate grades: a hero height cap (~80vh, so rendered-height/viewport-height stays <= ~0.8); a secondary cap that forbids a low-`page_fraction` image from being enlarged past its section's hero (the explicit inverse of the contact-sheet defect); an object-fit / crop policy (`object-fit: contain` plus a matched background for anything whose content `cover` would clip, `cover` reserved for decorative backdrops, with cropping a chart axis / labeled region / face called a defect and the metric being rendered-vs-native aspect ratio within ~2 percent); and a no-oversized-tile rule for galleries. Added a dead-space ceiling (~30% whitespace within an image band) to "Spacing and density". **2.2 extractor signals (CONFIRMED, no code change)**: verified `scripts/extract_content.py` already emits `page_fraction` and native `width`/`height` for image blocks on BOTH formats the rules depend on - PPTX picture shapes (`_pptx_image_block`, fraction = shape area / slide area) and PDF embedded rasters (fraction = bbox area / page area) - and that `references/content-model.md` already documents these v3 prominence fields; nothing was missing, so no extractor or schema edit was made and the new prominence test is the confirmation artifact. Empirically confirmed by building a python-pptx deck (`shape-picture page_fraction=0.142 width=400 height=267`) and a reportlab text+image PDF (`embedded-raster page_fraction=0.124 width=600 height=400`); a Pillow one-page image-only PDF is correctly classified `scanned-page` (no page geometry, so no `page_fraction`, by design). **2.3 template caps**: `assets/presentation-template.html` `figure img` now carries `max-height: 80vh` + `object-fit: contain` + a matched `background` (aspect preserved via `height: auto` + `max-width`, so no crop and no distortion), and a new token-driven `.gallery` grid caps each tile (a minimum tile width via `minmax` plus `max-height: 40vh` + `object-fit: contain`) so no secondary image balloons. Token-driven and offline (rebuild greps clean; self-check rc=0). **2.4 tests + CI**: added `tests/skills/test_presentify_extractor_prominence.py` (PPTX via python-pptx, PDF via reportlab, both `importorskip`-guarded so they run in the `presentify-extractor` workflow and skip in the deps-light `ci.yml` tests job) asserting populated `page_fraction` + native dimensions; extended `tests/skills/test_presentify_layout.py` with a browser-free image-cap assertion (max-height, object-fit, `.gallery`) and a headless-optional rendered image-box check (skip-with-note without a browser). Broadened `presentify-extractor.yml`'s path filter to `tests/skills/**` and pointed its pytest step at the whole `tests/skills/` dir (that runner installs the heavy extractor libs, so the prominence tests execute there; concurrency + pip cache already present). **Gates**: ruff clean on the builder + both test files; orphan audit 0 errors; unicode 0 errors; workflow-security pass; CI YAML parses; full `tests/skills` suite 36 pass / 2 skip (the 2 skips are the by-design headless-render checks; the extractor prominence tests actually ran and passed locally). `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is the authoritative gate. **Known gaps**: two new documented, non-blocking deferrals - DF-1 (the baseline builder still stacks images and does not emit the new `.gallery` grouping or classify hero-vs-secondary from `page_fraction`; the gallery styles are latent for the LLM-native path, which is the primary target per the reference) and DF-2 (a PDF embedded raster's `page_fraction` is null when pdfplumber's per-page image-bbox count does not match the extracted raster count, the intentional geometry-alignment guard; native dimensions still rank, and PPTX + PDF rasterized-regions always carry the fraction). BG-1 (the Phase 1 builder color-var mismatch) remains open and untouched. Phases 3-7 pending.

## [2026-07-24] - v3.15.4 presentify-visual-fidelity Phase 1: full-width canvas contract

Implemented Phase 1 of the presentify visual-fidelity plan (`is_final_phase = false`; Phase 7 is the terminal refactor gate). Made "full-width" a concrete, measurable edge-to-edge canvas across both the LLM-native authoring path and the deterministic baseline builder, with the body reading measure kept per-element. Command + skill + references + docs behavior only - no `base-*.md` five-platform lockstep, no installer edit (the bundle is folder-auto-copied), no new outbound call / dependency / credential. **1.1 reference contract**: replaced the prose "Full-width" bullet in `references/interactive-features.md` ("Output aspect (the canvas)") with an enforceable contract - page shell spanning the viewport via named `--gutter` tokens (not a centered `max-width` column); full-bleed top-level bands; the 45-85ch `--measure` scoped PER LONG-FORM-PROSE ELEMENT only (never the wrapper, headings, hero text, charts, tables, or image bands); and the success metric the verification and the Phase 5 gate use (at 1920px the widest top-level content band reaches at least ~95% of the viewport after gutters, with no global zoom / `transform: scale()`) - plus a one-line "failure to avoid" note (the narrow-centered-column-only-right-at-200%-zoom defect). Kept standard / portrait / other unchanged. **1.2 SKILL.md**: tightened Step 6's "Use the viewport width on purpose" and "Spacing, density, and aspect" bullets to cite the contract by name and state the binary full-width rule, and added a distinct Common Rationalizations row rebutting "the user chose full-width, but I'll keep one tidy centered column so it's safe" (a centered column with empty margins is a defect at full-width, not caution). SKILL.md stays well under the 800-line soft cap. **1.3 builder + template**: added `--layout {full|standard|portrait}` (default standard) to `build_presentation.py`; it injects a `--page-max`/`--gutter` pair into a new `NEXUS_ASPECT` marker block (mirroring the existing `NEXUS_THEME` mechanism, so no `[data-aspect]`-selector specificity conflict) and stamps `data-aspect` on the root `<html>`. `assets/presentation-template.html` now drives the canvas from those vars (`--slide-max` -> `--page-max`; `.slide` horizontal padding -> `--gutter`; `.slide__body` max-width -> `--page-max`), widens a full-width chart to its band, gates the >=1700px projector-padding widening to non-full aspects so full-width stays edge-to-edge, and keeps `--measure` scoped to prose. `full` = page-max 100% + small gutters (~96.7% band at 1920px); `standard` = the historical 1180px centered column (byte-identical to today's look); `portrait` = a 46rem reading column. **1.3 DEVIATION (root-cause fix)**: while verifying the builder I found a PRE-EXISTING bug - the title-substitution regex `<title>.*?</title>` (DOTALL) matched the header comment's literal "<title>" mention and spanned to the real `</title>`, deleting the comment close, `<html>`, `<head>`, and the `<meta>` tags on EVERY build (the baseline builder had been emitting headless, malformed HTML, unnoticed because no test checked builder output structure and `assert_no_external` strips comments first). Confirmed pre-existing by building from the committed template. Fixed the root cause (`<title>[^<]*</title>`, which cannot span across other tags) because Phase 1.3 requires a valid `<html data-aspect="...">` with an intact head; logged inline as a `# DEVIATION:`. **1.4 tests + CI**: `tests/skills/test_presentify_layout.py` (11 pass / 1 skip) asserts the injected `--page-max`/`--gutter`/`data-aspect` per layout, offline-cleanliness, head integrity (the TITLE_RE regression guard), and a browser-free CSS heuristic proving the >=95% full-width / <95% standard metric; it also ships the headless-optional `measure_widest_band` helper (the Phase 5 gate seed) whose true-render check skips-with-note when no browser is present. Broadened the `presentify-extractor.yml` path filter from `scripts/**` to the whole bundle + the new test, added `pytest`, and wired in the layout suite (concurrency cancel-in-progress + pip cache already present; no headless-render job added - that is gated to a later phase per the plan). **Gates**: ruff clean on the builder + test; `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` 0 errors; `validate_unicode_safety.py` 0 errors; `validate_workflow_security.py` pass; the CI YAML parses; full `tests/skills` suite 33 pass / 1 skip. `make` is unavailable on this Windows host, so validators ran individually; CI is the authoritative full-suite gate. **Known gaps**: BG-1 (a PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope builder color-var mismatch - `theme_to_css` emits `--color-background`/`--color-foreground` while the template consumes `--color-bg`/`--color-fg`, so built output loses theme colors; recorded, not fixed, per scope discipline) and MT-1 (the rendered-width check skips without a headless browser; the metric is covered browser-free by the CSS heuristic, and a gated headless-render job is deferred to Phase 5). Phases 2-7 pending.

CLI: `--to-interop` / `--to-internal`, `--skill-name`, `-o`, else stdout. Registered by explicit name in BOTH installers (sibling of aggregate_benchmark/skill_eval_viewer/optimize_skill_description); documented in `references/schemas.md` (a new interop section with the field mapping + the align-vs-adapter decision rationale, described generically with no external tool named) and referenced from the skill's SKILL.md via a new "Behavioral-eval schema interop" section. ## [2026-07-23] - v3.15.2 adoption-awesome-llm-apps Phase 2: unfilled-placeholder lint

Implemented Phase 2 of the awesome-llm-apps adoption plan on `feat/adoption-awesome-llm-apps` - a bounded regex fold-in to the existing skill validator so a scaffolded-but-unfinished skill cannot pass validation silently. **2.1 (detection)**: added `validate_placeholders` to `scripts/validate_skills.py` (plus the module regex `PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN` and two helpers `_strip_inline_code` / `_body_after_frontmatter`). A placeholder is a multi-word lowercase angle-bracket span - two or more single-space-separated lowercase words, hyphens allowed, e.g. `<what this skill does>` - matched by `<[a-z]+(?: [a-z-]+)+>`. It is a HARD ERROR in both the `description` frontmatter field and the SKILL.md body prose. The shape is deliberately tight so the real catalog stays at zero false positives: single-word CLI notation (`<path>`, `<name>`, `<category>`) has no interior space and is not matched; HTML tags (`<div>`, `<br/>`, `<a href="x">`) carry `=`/`"`/`/` and are excluded; uppercase template tokens (`<MAJOR>`, so `docs/v<MAJOR>/` is safe) are excluded; comparison operators (`x < y and y > z`) are excluded (a space follows `<`); and fenced code blocks + inline-code spans are skipped, with CommonMark-aware fence tracking mirrored from `scan_text_for_secrets` (a shorter inner fence cannot close a longer outer one, so a ` ```bash ` example inside a ` ````markdown ` block stays content). The description check strips inline code too, so a backticked example in a description is exempt. Wired into BOTH `validate_skill_dir` (full mode) and the `--bundles-only` branch that `make validate` and CI run, so the lint is enforced everywhere the strict-YAML gate is. **2.2 (triage)**: the first run over all 267 skills produced ZERO findings - no genuine unfilled scaffolds and no false positives - so no SKILL.md needed fixing (a positive/negative control confirmed the regex is not inert: it matches real placeholders and rejects every look-alike). **2.3 (tests + CI)**: added 14 cases to `tests/validators/test_validate_skills.py` (description hit, body hit, the CLI-notation / HTML / uppercase-token / comparison-operator negatives, the fenced / inline-code / backticked-description exemptions, a nested-fence guard using a 4-backtick outer fence, `_body_after_frontmatter` with and without frontmatter, and two end-to-end `--bundles-only` CLI tests - a scaffold skill that must exit 1 and a clean skill that must exit 0); new-code line coverage 100% in-process (the full-file 66% is the pre-existing subprocess-only `main()`, unchanged). Full `tests/validators` suite 272 passed; `--bundles-only` and `--quality` both PASS (0 errors) on the real catalog. NO CI edit needed - the check runs inside CI's existing `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` step and the tests run via the existing `pytest tests/validators` step; path filters and caching are unchanged (no redundant job). AGENTS.md documents the new lint alongside the orphan-bundle detection block. No installer, `base-*.md`, catalog-registry, or hook change. Phases 3-6 pending.

## [2026-07-23] - v3.15.2 adoption-awesome-llm-apps Phase 1: catalog-wide trigger-and-routing eval

Implemented Phase 1 of the awesome-llm-apps adoption plan on a fresh `feat/adoption-awesome-llm-apps` branch (cut off `develop`). The phase ships the catalog's first deterministic, model-free routing-safety gate: a skill-description near-collision detector. **1.1 (detector)**: new `scripts/run_trigger_evals.py` (Python stdlib only - `json`/`os`/`re`/`sys`/`argparse` - no third-party imports, no outbound call, no new dependency; the frontmatter parser is mirrored from `validate_skills.py` so the script is self-contained at its installed location). It tokenizes every skill's `description` (lowercase, split on non-alphanumerics, drop a stopword set that includes the "pushy-description" scaffolding vocabulary plus tokens under 3 chars, light suffix-stem ing/es/ed/s with a floor guard), then scores every pair with a containment metric `|A n B| / min(|A|, |B|)` - deliberately not Jaccard, so a smaller skill's vocabulary being subsumed by a larger one's still fires - and flags any pair at or above a configurable threshold (default 0.5). It supports `--threshold`, `--json`, `--allowlist`, and a `--gate`/`--strict` mode; default is WARNING-ONLY (always exit 0) so first-run findings are triaged before it becomes a merge gate. Generic descriptive names throughout per the reverse-engineering attribution rule (no external repo/product/author named). **1.2 (triage)**: the first run over all 267 skills surfaced 39 near-collisions. 38 are by-design category siblings (parallel `<lang>-cleanup` / `<lang>-expert` / `init-<lang>-project` / framework-expert / `*-generation` / mobile-platform / compliance-regulation pairs, and two matched pairs that already carry mutual SKIP clauses), routed apart by a domain noun that is the user's actual trigger. The one genuine collision was `technical-documentation` (a broad doc skill that advertised "ADRs" and had NO SKIP clause) colliding with the single-artifact `architecture-decision-record` and `project-constitution` skills; it was FIXED by sharpening `technical-documentation`'s description to defer to both via an explicit SKIP clause (kept under the 250-char ceiling), with the `data/skills.json` `description` mirror updated to match (`summary_l0` and `SKILL_INDEX.md` untouched - the detector reads only `description`). **1.3 (allowlist)**: `scripts/run_trigger_evals.allowlist.json` (modeled on `validate_skills.allowlist.json`) records the 39 intentional near-neighbor pairs, each with a one-line justification; the runner downgrades them to informational lines, and `--gate` now reports zero un-allowlisted collisions. **1.4 (registration)**: registered warning-first in BOTH installers (`installer.sh` + `installer.ps1`, next to the eval-loop dispatcher scripts, copying the script and its allowlist to `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/`), the `Makefile` (a `trigger-evals` target plus a warning-only step inside `validate`), and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (a warning-only step in the `validate` job). **1.5 (tests + CI)**: `tests/validators/test_run_trigger_evals.py` (25 tests: tokenizer/stemmer, containment metric, threshold floor, allowlist downgrade, warning-only vs `--gate` exit codes, a colliding fixture pair the detector must catch and a distinct pair it must not, plus in-process `main()` coverage and a real-catalog zero-un-allowlisted guard) - 96% line coverage on the new script; CI auto-runs them via the existing `pytest tests/validators` step. Full `tests/validators` suite 258 passed; shellcheck on `installer.sh` clean; `skills.json` valid (267 skills). CI/CD is already optimized (concurrency cancel-in-progress, pip caching, cost-gated matrix legs), so the eval rides the existing `validate` job as a sub-second step rather than a separately-path-filtered job (DF-1). Promotion from warning-only to a hard `--gate` is deferred to Phase 6. No `base-*.md`, catalog-command, or hook change. Phases 2-6 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 5: token-savings benchmark + map-health lint

Implemented Phase 5 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - the measurement + health phase that validates the measured half of the definition of done. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. **5.1 token-savings benchmark** (`contextmap/benchmark.py` + committed `benchmark_baseline.json`, patterned on `nexus-context-compressor/evals`): measures the compiled map's token count against a SIMULATED manual-exploration cost - the sum of per-file tokens times a documented revisit multiplier (an AI re-reads files while exploring) plus a per-entity discovery overhead for each route / model / component / env var. The reduction ratio is `1 - map_cost / manual_cost`; the estimation constants are the tool's own heuristic. The map cost is computed WITHOUT writing `.nexus/` (a new `estimate_map_tokens` in the generator renders in memory) and each repo indexes into a throwaway directory, so benchmarking never mutates the repo it measures. A key honest finding: the tiny per-framework `contextmap` fixtures show NEGATIVE savings (a map is not worth its fixed overhead on a 2-file repo), so the benchmark corpus is three realistic committed sample repos (`shop_api`, `blog_ts`, `tasks_py`) that show 44-55% reduction, plus a run on Nexus-Hub itself: a ~22k-token map replaces ~1.9M tokens of manual exploration (~99% reduction across 443 files). `benchmark_baseline.json` records a per-repo floor (a margin below the measured ratio) so a regression - the map silently losing its savings - fails `--check`; `--update-baseline` re-baselines intentionally. **5.2 map-health lint** (`contextmap/maphealth.py`): deterministic checks for orphan articles (not linked from the index), missing backlinks (article not linking `../CONTEXT-MAP.md`), and staleness (the map's embedded source fingerprint vs a freshly-recomputed one - I extracted the fingerprint into a shared `current_source_hash` so the lint and the generator agree exactly). Exposed as the `map_health` MCP tool and `nexus-hub map --lint` (exit 1 when unhealthy). **Decision**: the lint ships as extension code, NOT a new catalog skill - the richer semantic checks stay in the LLM-native `documentation-consistency` skill - so no `data/` registry files were touched (Phases 1-5 remain entirely extension-only). **5.3 tests**: `test_context_map_measurement.py` (19) covers the benchmark (positive reduction, corpus-meets-baseline, seeded-regression gate, side-effect-free, CLI `--json`/`--check`/`--repo`/missing-corpus, `measured_baseline` floors) and the lint (healthy, seeded orphan/backlink/stale, no-map, CLI exit codes, the MCP handler). **Gates**: full extension suite 285 passed / 1 skipped (+19 Phase 5 tests), new-code coverage 94% (contextmap; benchmark.py lifted to 90% after CLI tests), all new/modified code ruff-clean. The benchmark + lint run in CI via the existing pytest job (no CI edit needed). Known-gaps: both DoD axes now hold; MT-2 added (`--update-baseline` write path untested by design). Phases 6-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 3: ORM schema + components + events

Implemented Phase 3 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - the framework-extraction II pass (schema + components + events), the plan's hardest phase (ORM relation resolution). Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. Consistent with Phase 2, everything is post-graph source parsing inside `contextmap/` (no new extraction-time resolvers). **3.1 schema** (`schema.py`): ORM models with fields, PK/FK/unique flags, and relations across SQLAlchemy (`Column`/`mapped_column` + `relationship()`), Django ORM (`models.XField` + ForeignKey/OneToOne/ManyToMany), and Prisma (`.prisma` DSL `model` blocks). Class-based ORMs are located from the `class` nodes already in the graph and parsed from their source span (a helper joins multi-line field defs until parens balance); Prisma is parsed from the `.prisma` files. Detection keys on ORM-specific tokens (`models.Model`/`models.X(`, `Column(`/`relationship(`), so a plain class (or a Django `Meta`) is never mistaken for a model - the fixtures include a decoy class to lock that. Relations carry name + target + best-effort kind (Django FK->many-to-one, M2M->many-to-many; Prisma `[]`->one-to-many else many-to-one; SQLAlchemy relationship()->relation). **3.2 components + events** (`components.py`, `events.py`): React components are detected in `.tsx`/`.jsx` as exported PascalCase function/const declarations (JSX-file scoping makes that a reliable signal, so a plain helper or a hook is not misreported), with props unioned from the destructured parameter AND the resolved prop type (a `}: Props` annotation or a `React.FC<Props>` generic resolved to its `interface`/`type` in the same file). Events detect declaration-strong background-work surfaces only (Celery task decorators, BullMQ `new Queue/Worker`, Kafka, `new EventEmitter`), deferring FP-prone invocation-only patterns (`.delay(`/`.emit(`/`.publish(`). **Map**: Data Models / Components / Events sections + a `database` article with per-model field/relation detail; `GENERATOR_VERSION` 2 -> 3; the source fingerprint now also covers `.prisma` files (a schema change invalidates the no-op). **3.3 accuracy** (`accuracy.py` extended + `schema_app`/`frontend_app` fixtures): `evaluate()` now scores only the sections a fixture declares (so the Phase 2 route fixtures are untouched) and adds models / relations / components / events; a dedicated `test_relation_resolution` asserts 100% relation recall with zero FP across Django, SQLAlchemy, and Prisma. Two component-props bugs were found and fixed via the fixtures: a single-line `type X = {...}` only yielded its first member (fixed by splitting on member separators), and a `React.FC<CardProps>` component whose arrow only destructures a subset now unions in the full declared prop type. **Gates**: full extension suite 257 passed / 1 skipped (+12 Phase 3 tests), new-code coverage 95% (contextmap), all new/modified code ruff-clean. CI needs no edit (path-filtered `code-search.yml` + always-on `tests` job auto-discover the new tests/fixtures). Known-gaps: DF-3 expanded to record the deferred ORMs (TypeORM/Drizzle/ActiveRecord/GORM), component libs (Vue/Svelte), and event patterns as explicit coverage. Phases 4-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 2: framework routes + env audit + middleware

Implemented Phase 2 of the CodeSight-adoption plan on `feat/adoption-codesight` - framework-aware route extraction, an env-var audit, and middleware detection, all feeding the compiled context map and gated by an extraction-accuracy harness. Extension-only; no catalog registry, installer, or `base-*.md` changes. **Architecture (reuse-first)**: rather than adding new extraction-time resolvers, Phase 2 reads the `route` nodes the EXISTING FastAPI / Flask / Django / Express resolvers already emit (built in v2.2.0-v2.3.0) and enriches them in a read-only post-graph layer. **2.1 routes** (`contextmap/routes.py` + `behavior.py`): parses each route node into framework / method / path / URL params (unioning `{x}`, `<conv:x>`, `:x`, and `(?P<x>)` syntaxes), resolves the handler via the `decorates` / `references` edge, and infers coarse behavior tags (auth / db / cache / payment / ai / queue / email) from the handler's source. A key refinement: when no handler edge resolves (an Express inline arrow handler has no separate node), tags are inferred from the route node's OWN source span, so inline handlers are still tagged - the FastAPI decorator span (body lives elsewhere) uses the edge-based handler slice instead, and unioning both covers both styles without adding false positives. Behavior tokens are deliberately distinctive (library/API surface names, word-boundary-anchored) so a generic verb does not trigger a tag. **2.2 env + middleware** (`env.py`, `middleware.py`): the env audit scans indexed source for real env-access forms (`os.environ[...]`, `os.getenv(...)`, `process.env.X`, `import.meta.env`) and classifies each required vs has-default (a default at the call site, or an `.env.example` declaration, means not-required), and merges NAMES from `.env.example`-style files (never the real `.env`, never a value); middleware detection finds `app.use(...)` / `add_middleware(...)` / Django `MIDDLEWARE=[...]` registrations and categorizes each (auth / rate-limit / cors / validation / logging / error-handling / other) by a conservative name match. Both reject look-alikes (a plain `dict["X"]` is not an env var). **Map**: the generator gained Routes / Environment / Middleware sections + a `context/routes.md` article + an Overview `Frameworks:` line (resolving the frameworks half of Phase 1's DF-1); `GENERATOR_VERSION` bumped 1 -> 2 (format change invalidates old maps) and the source fingerprint now covers `.env.example` files so a change to one invalidates the no-op. **2.3 accuracy harness** (`accuracy.py` + `tests/fixtures/contextmap/{fastapi,express,django}_app` with hand-counted `truth.json`): per-section recall + a HARD zero-false-positive gate; `test_context_map_accuracy.py` enforces both. The harness immediately earned its keep - it flagged a "false positive" on the Django fixture (`ANY admin/`) that was actually a ground-truth omission on my part (`path("admin/", include(...))` binds both `admin/` and the include), which I corrected. **Gates**: full extension suite 245 passed / 1 skipped (+23 Phase 2 tests), new-code coverage 95% (contextmap package), all new/modified code ruff-clean. CI needs no edit - the path-filtered `code-search.yml` and the always-on `tests` job both auto-discover the new tests and fixtures. Known-gaps ([docs/releases/v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md](v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md)): DF-1 frameworks half resolved (most-imported still Phase 4), DF-3 added (additional route frameworks Hono/Fastify/Next/NestJS/Gin/Rails/Spring/Laravel + ORMs deferred as explicit coverage, per the plan's incremental posture). Phases 3-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.1 adoption-codesight Phase 1: compiled context-map generator + `nexus-hub map`

Implemented Phase 1 of the v3.15.1 CodeSight-adoption plan on a fresh `feat/adoption-codesight` branch (cut off `develop`, chosen over the current `feat/platform-parity-all-gaps` branch which holds a different, complete v3.15.0 feature set). The whole phase is extension-only, inside `extensions/nexus-code-search/`: it compiles the tree-sitter AST graph the extension already builds (`codegraph.db`: files / nodes / edges) into a deterministic, committed `.nexus/CONTEXT-MAP.md` plus a `.nexus/context/` article set, so an AI reads a cheap cold-start map once instead of re-exploring files every session. **1.1 (generator)**: new `contextmap/` package - `model.py` (rendering-free content model + a SHA-256 source fingerprint over the sorted `(path, content_hash)` rows), `tokens.py` (a `count_tokens` that prefers tiktoken/cl100k_base but falls back to a stdlib heuristic, so no new dependency and the zero-outbound posture holds), and `generator.py` (reads the graph, groups files by top-level module, counts significant symbols, and renders the map + an `index.md` + one article per module). Three load-bearing guarantees, each test-locked: **neutral path** (every write is confined to `<root>/.nexus/` via an `is_relative_to` guard; AI-config files are never touched), **deterministic** (no wall-clock timestamp in the output, so the MCP tool and the CLI are byte-identical for the same graph), and **content-hash incremental** (the source fingerprint is embedded in the map; an unchanged graph is a no-op unless `force`). The token-count header every output file carries is measured over the document EXCLUDING its own metadata line, dodging the circular-count problem. The "Most-Imported Files" section and an Overview frameworks line are explicit Phase-1 placeholders (Phase 4 / Phase 2 respectively; DF-1). **1.2 (surfaces)**: added the `generate_context_map` MCP tool to `server.py` (tool def + dispatch + handler + instructions) and wired a `nexus-hub map [root] [--force] [--json]` verb into `scripts/nexus_hub_cli.py` - verified the dispatcher wiring first, and because the map logic lives entirely in the extension and `nexus_hub_cli.py` is already installer-copied, NO installer edit was needed (the ask-first gate was not tripped); the verb forwards verbatim to `nexus_code_search.contextmap.cli`, mirroring the `nexus_hub_affected.py` late-import + pip-hint precedent. **1.3 (tests + CI)**: `tests/test_context_map.py` (22 tests: sections, per-file token-header accuracy, neutral-path, no-op vs force vs graph-change, tool-vs-CLI byte-identity, empty-graph, missing-graph exit codes, and the tiktoken-preference + fallback paths) and a new path-filtered `.github/workflows/code-search.yml` (scoped to `extensions/nexus-code-search/**`, pip-cached, concurrency cancel-in-progress). **Gates**: full extension suite green (222 passed, 1 pre-existing skip), new-code coverage 97%, all new/modified code ruff-clean (the one ruff finding is a PRE-EXISTING unused `json` import in `nexus_hub_cli.py`, left out of scope and logged as WN-1), workflow-security + IOC validators exit 0. Known-gaps recorded in [docs/releases/v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md](v3/v3.15/known-gaps.md): DF-1 (placeholders), DF-2 (extension version not bumped), WN-1, MT-1 (repo-level dispatch not auto-tested), QG-1 (extension tests run in both ci.yml and code-search.yml - Phase 7 CI-optimization to de-dupe), QG-2 (three plans share v3.15.0 - reconcile before release). No catalog registry files, installers, or `base-*.md` templates touched. Phases 2-7 pending.

## [2026-07-21] - v3.15.0 Phase 3: OpenCode parity (agents surface; plugins/hooks out of scope)

Implemented Phase 3 (OpenCode parity) of the v3.15.0 platform-parity plan on `feat/platform-parity-all-gaps`. A small, verification-led phase. **3.1 (agents surface)**: added `agents_subdir: "agents"` to `OpenCodeIntegration.config` - a config-only change, because the base `_mirror_catalog` already turns `agents_subdir` into a verbatim `catalog/agents/*.md` -> `<root>/agents/` tree copy (the same machinery that ships skills/commands/rules). A Cursor-DF-1-style direct re-read of `opencode.ai/docs/agents/` (2026-07-21) confirmed the format before wiring: OpenCode reads `.md` + YAML frontmatter from `~/.config/opencode/agents/` (global) and `.opencode/agents/` (project), the filename is the agent id, and the `mode` field is OPTIONAL defaulting to `all`. So the catalog's 23 personas (which carry `name`/`description`/`tools` frontmatter, no `mode`) load as-is: OpenCode uses `description` + the filename, defaults the mode, and ignores the non-native `name`/`tools` keys - exactly how Cursor consumes the same files. ## [2026-07-20] - v3.14.7: usage-monitor status-bar icon spacing

Small cosmetic follow-up to v3.14.6, driven by the user noticing (in the shipped v3.14.6 extensions) that the status-bar icon sat glued to the usage text - `icon47% (current)...` with no gap. Root cause: VS Code collapses consecutive plain spaces in a status-bar label, so the single separating space in `${ICON} ${label}...` did not survive rendering. Fix (both extensions, lockstep): each `statusBarManager.ts` now defines a module-level `const ICON_GAP = "\u2002"` (an en-space, U+2002, which does NOT collapse) and places it between the icon and the label in every `statusText` branch - Codex's no-data path (`${CODEX_ICON}${ICON_GAP}${label}--${staleLabel}`) and data path, and Claude's compact and full paths. Written as the ASCII `\u2002` escape (not a literal en-space char) to keep the source ASCII-clean and avoid the invisible-character fragility that `validate_unicode_safety` guards against. The test friction was purely tooling: the Edit tool and bash heredocs kept rendering my `\u2002` intent as either a literal en-space or a normal space, so I used Python (`chr(0x2002)` to search, `chr(92)+"u2002"` for the replacement text) to write the exact escape deterministically, verified via `repr()` and `line.isascii()`. Both extensions' `statusBarManager.test.ts` expected strings updated from `"$(icon) ..."` to `"$(icon)\u2002..."` (4 occurrences Codex, 2 Claude). Extension versions bumped Claude 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3, Codex 0.2.3 -> 0.2.4; user verified the gap renders correctly in the live host before release. Verification: both type-clean (`tsc` exit 0), Vitest green (Codex 43, Claude 5), both VSIXes packaged. Platform read-contract reaffirmed (not re-verified) - v3.14.7 touched no platform read-paths, so the 2026-07-19 full re-verification holds; freshness marker re-stamped to 3.14.7. Catalog counts unchanged (267 skills, 16 commands, 28 hooks).

## [2026-07-20] - v3.14.6: Codex auto-fetch fix, inline settings, installer-log overhaul

Post-v3.14.5 fix release driven by user testing of the shipped v3.14.5 extensions. **Codex auto-fetch root-caused and fixed**: the monitor showed "No Usage Data" even though the token + endpoint were fine. Probing `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` live (with the user's `~/.codex/auth.json` token, on their machine) returned HTTP 200 - the failure was a mapper schema mismatch. Our `locateWindows` looked for `rate_limits` (plural) with `primary`/`secondary`; the real response nests the windows under `rate_limit` (singular) as `primary_window`/`secondary_window`, and the user's Team plan exposes a single 7-day (weekly) window (`limit_window_seconds: 604800`, `secondary_window: null`). Rewrote the mapper to the verified schema and made it classify each window by its own duration (so a weekly-only window maps to weekly, not mislabeled "current session"); retired the "undocumented endpoint" caveat (DF-2). **Manual entry removed** (per user): the command, dashboard button, and prompts are gone now that auto-fetch works; the empty state is an honest fetch-failure diagnostic. **Both extensions: settings moved inline** - the status-bar gear item is removed and the dashboard's gear now toggles a Settings section rendered under the dashboard (state-persisted across re-renders via `vscode.getState`, unified fonts/headings), replacing the standalone settings webview;
