## [2026-06-09] - v3.2.0 adoption-headroom Phase 4: Runtime integration + retire rtk (nexus-context-compressor)

Implemented Phase 4 (of 7) of the v3.2.0 `adoption-headroom` plan on `feat/adoption-headroom` (switched from `develop`, where the session opened with only stale gitignored `.pyc` artifacts of the compressor and no tracked source -- the Phase 1-3 source lives on the feature branch). Subtasks T012-T015 closed. This phase wires the deterministic engine (Phases 1-3) into a live session and supersedes the external `rtk` recommendation; it is local-first and zero new outbound.

Enabling work (the runtime seam): added `compress_output(text, *, persist=True, store=None, config=None) -> RouteResult` to `__init__.py` -- the single-blob entry both the hook (via the CLI) and the MCP tool call. It runs `ContentRouter`, opens the default CCR store when `persist` so drops stay reversible, and adds two integration-boundary guarantees the raw `route()` lacks: **never expand** (a sub-threshold JSON array that would grow when reserialized is returned verbatim -- a real defect caught in stabilization where `[1,2,3]` went 7 -> 14 tokens) and **never lose output** (a missing/unwritable cache dir degrades to non-persisting compression instead of raising). Rewired `compress(messages)` to route each message's content -- no longer the Phase 1 no-op, resolving DF-v32hr-7 -- and because `route()` no-ops on prose, the all-prose scaffold identity test stays green with `transforms_applied == []`. Added `cli.py` (`compress` reads stdin, `retrieve` resolves a marker, `serve` launches the MCP server; `compress` is fail-open, returning the input unchanged on any error) and repointed `__main__.py` at it while preserving the bare-invocation identity print.

T012 shipped `catalog/hooks/compress-output.sh`, a PreToolUse Bash hook that is opt-in / default-off (inert unless `NEXUS_CONTEXT_COMPRESS=1`, mirroring git-guardrails' protected-branch guard). When enabled, gated on `jq` and on the engine importing cleanly (so output is never piped into a missing compressor), it emits a `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput` rewriting the command to `{ <ORIG> ; } | python -m nexus_context_compressor compress; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` -- piping stdout through the engine while preserving the original exit status (verified end-to-end on both a passing and a failing command) and leaving stderr untouched. Registered in `catalog/hooks/settings.json` (PreToolUse Bash, after the guards) and copied by both installers alongside git-guardrails. Windows uses CLAUDE.md-injected instructions (hooks need a Unix shell), exactly as the prior rtk integration documented. pytest suite at `catalog/hooks/tests/test_compress_output_hook.py` (inert paths run everywhere; rewrite-path tests run with `jq` + an importable engine, skip gracefully otherwise). A first-draft `set -e` + grep-fallback bug (a no-command payload made `grep` exit 1, killing the hook) was fixed by dropping the grep fallback and gating the whole hook on `jq` up front.

T013 added the internal MCP server (`server.py`) exposing `context_compress(payload, persist)` and `context_retrieve(marker)` over stdio, modeled on `nexus-web-fetch`. Unlike that MCP-only package, `mcp` is an optional `[mcp]` extra here and is imported lazily inside `run_server`, so the module -- and its pure `do_compress` / `do_retrieve` handlers + `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS` -- import and test without it (the engine stays usable air-gapped). Registered in `catalog/mcp-configs/mcp-servers.json` (`re-full`, full 5-question audit), with a reverse-engineering matrix row (`docs/policy/mcp-reverse-engineering-matrix.md`, new "New in v3.2.0" section). Both installers now install the compressor with the `[mcp]` extra and auto-register `nexus-context-compressor` (`python -m nexus_context_compressor serve`) in the `mcpServers` merge block -- the installer's own Phase-1 comment had pre-committed this to T013. ShellCheck caught `SC1087` on the install line (`"$dest[mcp]"` is array-subscript syntax to bash) -- fixed to `"${dest}[mcp]"`. Also closed a CI gap: the compressor extension suite was never CI-gated (a Phase 1-3 oversight), so added the install + test step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

T014 rewrote `guides/reference/RTK_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION.md` to lead with the internal engine (no Rust, local-first, reversible) -- platform table, enable/Windows paths, a "Migrating from rtk" section, and the preserved cross-platform output-minimization guidance -- and updated the one rtk reference line in `templates/ai-instructions/base-claude.md`. The supersession is honest about scope rather than overclaiming parity: the deterministic engine compresses **structured** output (JSON arrays, code) today and passes free-text/logs through (the optional Phase 6 ML module), so the guide documents that boundary and leads the reversible CCR store as the real differentiator over (lossy) rtk. The `context-optimization` SKILL.md rtk content is deliberately left for Phase 7's T021 cross-link (DF-v32hr-11).

## [2026-06-09] - v3.2.0 adoption-headroom Phase 1: Foundation + SmartCrusher (nexus-context-compressor)

Implemented Phase 1 (of 7) of the v3.2.0 `adoption-headroom` plan on the new `feat/adoption-headroom` branch (created off the post-teach `develop` merge `8523281`): stood up the internal, local-first `extensions/nexus-context-compressor` package and shipped its first deterministic strategy, `SmartCrusher`. Subtasks T001-T004 closed. This is the reverse-engineer-first internal build that will replace the external `rtk` context-compression binary; Phase 1 is pure standard library plus a single declared dependency (`tiktoken`) that the code never hard-requires at runtime.

T001 scaffolded the package modeled structurally on `extensions/nexus-skill-scanner` (src/ layout, hatchling build, frozen dataclasses, a `tests/conftest.py` that puts `src/` on `sys.path`): `pyproject.toml` (Python 3.10+, `tiktoken` the only required dep, optional `ml`/`code`/`dev` extras), `nexus_context_compressor/__init__.py` exposing `compress(messages, model=...) -> CompressResult` as a Phase-1 no-op pipeline (messages pass through unchanged; metrics report an identity transform), a `types.py` `CompressResult` dataclass (messages + tokens_before/after + `ratio`/`reduction` properties), a `tokens.py` counter that prefers tiktoken's `cl100k_base` proxy and degrades to a deterministic stdlib regex estimate when tiktoken or its cached vocab is unavailable (so the package never requires an outbound call -- the tiktoken vocab fetch is a static asset carrying no user data, mirroring the v3.0.0 OSV.dev / Phase 6 ML-weights offline-first precedent), a `transforms/` subpackage marker, a `__main__.py`, a README, and a scaffold test.

T002 traced the installer distribution mechanism and found the plan's stated assumption wrong: `extensions/` is NOT copied recursively as a folder -- each internal package (`nexus-skill-server`, `nexus-code-search`, `nexus-web-fetch`) has its own explicit `cp -r` + editable `pip install -e` block inside `install_mcp_server`. So the new package would NOT auto-distribute. Per the maintainer's choice (ask-first installer gate), added a matching copy + editable-install block for `nexus-context-compressor` into the shared `mcp-server-venv` in BOTH `scripts/installer.sh` (after the web-fetch block) and `scripts/installer.ps1` (modeled on the web-fetch sibling), with NO MCP-server registration yet -- the compress/retrieve MCP tool is Phase 4 (T013), so the "three internal servers" registration comment is unchanged. `bash -n` + ShellCheck (`-S error`) on installer.sh and a PowerShell tokenizer parse on installer.ps1 are both clean.

T003 implemented `transforms/smart_crusher.py`: a deterministic, dependency-free JSON-array dedup. The load-bearing heuristic, `_distinctiveness_scores`, was chosen after researching how production engines (the headroom source, and Claude Code / Codex compaction) do this -- the key finding being that adjacent-only comparison fails on non-adjacent repetition (`A,B,A,B`), so the score blends GLOBAL uniqueness (content seen anywhere earlier scores 0 -> drop candidate) with ADJACENT change magnitude (a novel record scored by how many fields it changed vs its predecessor, making `variance_threshold=2.0` meaningful as a near-duplicate cutoff). Positional anchors always keep the first and last record; `_select_keep_indices` keeps anchors + records clearing the threshold, capped at `max_items_after_crush` (the cap dominates the positional rule -- the research confirmed headroom's "30%/15%/55%" is a split of the kept budget K, not the array). `_assemble` walks the array emitting kept records interleaved with one `{"_ccr_dropped": "<<ccr:HASH N_rows>>"}` marker per dropped run; the hash is a stable truncated SHA-256 over the canonical (sort_keys) serialization of the dropped span (no randomness/uuid/clock). A `SmartCrusherConfig` dataclass carries the plan's defaults (`min_items_to_analyze=5`, `max_items_after_crush=15`, `variance_threshold=2.0`); a `CrushResult` carries kept records + `CCRSpan` dropped spans (the Phase 2 CCR store's input) + a lossless-accounting `kept_count`. A thin top-level `smart_crusher.py` shim re-exports the strategy and provides the `python -m nexus_context_compressor.smart_crusher` entry the stability gate names verbatim (the implementation lives under `transforms/`, where Phase 3's strategies will also live), resolving a path inconsistency between the gate command and T003's file-location prompt.

T004 wrote 13 SmartCrusher tests (plus 6 scaffold tests, 19 total, all passing) covering every stability-gate assertion -- 1000 identical lines -> 2 kept + 1 marker (<=3); a 12-record high-variance array preserved verbatim; CCR marker hashes stable across runs; `CrushResult` metrics correct -- plus a lossless-accounting invariant (`kept_count + sum(dropped span counts) == original_count`, proving nothing is silently lost), non-adjacent `A,B,A,B` dedup, the budget cap, mixed-type records, determinism, the marker regex format, and the `--demo` CLI. Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on the Windows host, so the gate was emulated by invoking each validator directly -- ALL GREEN. The documented gate command `python -m nexus_context_compressor.smart_crusher --demo` crushes the built-in 100-item array to 5 kept + 4 markers (<=15). `make validate` equivalent green: catalog JSON parses (skills.json unchanged at 251 -- this phase adds an extension, not a skill), `validate_skills.py --bundles-only` PASS, `check_version_sync.py` consistent at canonical 3.1.1 (the new pyproject carries its inception version 3.2.0, which the guard does not scan -- mirroring nexus-skill-scanner's 3.0.0), and unicode-safety / no-personal-paths / supply-chain-iocs / workflow-security all exit 0 with zero warnings in the new package. `make lint` (ShellCheck) WAS applicable this phase (installer edits) and is clean. The new package's `__pycache__`/`.pytest_cache` are already gitignored. No deviations beyond the two plan inconsistencies handled in-flight (installer auto-copy assumption -> explicit block per maintainer choice; gate module path -> top-level shim); all quality gates passed (GO). Known-gaps: 3 new DF (DF-v32hr-1 fuzzy near-duplicate fingerprinting, DF-v32hr-2 information-theoretic auto-sizing, DF-v32hr-3 explicit error/outlier preservation -- all intentionally out of scope for the v1 deterministic port, referenced from the SmartCrusher docstring), 0 resolved; 6 open total (3 DF + the 3 carried-over teach WN). ## [2026-06-08] - v3.1.0 adoption-claude-red Phase 2: Scanner allowlist prerequisite gate (producer-catalog security-skill cap)

Implemented Phase 2 (of 5) of the v3.1.0 `adoption-claude-red` plan on the `feat/adoption-claude-red` branch: tuned the `nexus-skill-scanner` so authorized red-team payloads inside `catalog/skills/security/` skill bodies are capped below the HIGH/CRITICAL CI gate, without weakening detection of genuinely malicious skills. Subtasks T005-T006 closed. This is the prerequisite gate for the payload-bearing Phase 3-4 fold-ins (web AppSec + JWT/OAuth attack methodology). The change is a self-contained policy layer plus regression tests; no new dependency, credential, or outbound call (the scanner stays stdlib-only).

Root-cause analysis came first. The scanner already had two layers that keep a pure-markdown skill below the gate: text patterns are hard-capped at MEDIUM and suppressed inside fences (`text_patterns.py`), and the behavioral AST analyzer only parses real `.py` files, never markdown fenced examples (`behavioral_ast.py`). The one residual HIGH path on a markdown skill body is the secret analyzer: high-confidence credential formats (`Bearer <token>`, `sk-...`, `AKIA...`, `ghp_...`) are flagged HIGH even inside a fence by design (`scripts/validate_skills.py` `scan_text_for_secrets` -- "a genuinely leaked key must never be suppressed"). A JWT/OAuth attack-methodology skill (Phase 4) that shows a fenced example token would therefore trip `--fail-on high`. That is the precise gap Phase 2 addresses.

T005 added `extensions/nexus-skill-scanner/src/nexus_skill_scanner/allowlist.py` -- a documented policy layer, not a detection change. Every analyzer still reports the real detection class and severity; the allowlist lowers a finding to MEDIUM at exactly one choke point (`scanner.scan_file`, the single place that knows both the file path and the repo root) and only when ALL three scoping rules hold: (1) trusted producer catalog -- the scan is rooted at a real Nexus-Hub checkout AND the host file resolves under `<repo_root>/catalog/skills/security/` (a third-party `/skills import` scan has no Nexus-Hub root, so it is never allowlisted); (2) prose/fenced context only -- the host file is a Markdown skill body (`.md`/`.markdown`), so bundled executable scripts (`.py`, `.sh`, `.ps1`) are never capped and a payload that actually runs is detected at full severity; (3) not a never-relax class -- data exfiltration (2), excessive agency (5), dynamic code execution (12), taint-to-sink injection (13), and signature/live-malware (14) keep their real severity even inside a security skill body. The cap only ever lowers (HIGH/CRITICAL -> MEDIUM), never raises, so a currently-clean catalog stays clean. The helpers are exported from the package `__init__.py` and the scoping rule + rationale is documented in a new "Security-category allowlist" subsection of the package `README.md`. A scoping-interpretation decision was made deliberately: "fenced/prose contexts" is read as the whole markdown skill body (prose + fenced), consistent with the existing text-analyzer prose-capping discipline, rather than a fence-line-precise check -- the trade-off (a real leaked credential in a security-skill body is downgraded to MEDIUM, still emitted and visible, only within the reviewed producer catalog's security category) is documented in the module docstring and README.

T006 added `extensions/nexus-skill-scanner/tests/test_allowlist.py` (15 tests) and two launcher-subprocess regressions in `tests/validators/test_scan_skill_security.py`. The four plan assertions are proven: (a) the planted-malicious fixture still scores CRITICAL; (b) the known-clean fixture still scores LOW; (c) a representative authorized-payload security skill (a fenced example Bearer token) scores below HIGH -- the secret is still detected, just capped to MEDIUM; (d) the same payload in a non-security category and as a third-party (no-repo-root) scan is NOT allowlisted and still scores HIGH. The headline safety test plants a malicious bundled `.py` script (exec + credential exfiltration) under `catalog/skills/security/` and confirms it still scores CRITICAL -- proving the markdown-only cap did not open a blind spot for executable payloads in the security category. High-confidence tokens are assembled at runtime (`"Bearer " + "A"*64`) so the test sources carry no credential literal and do not trip the repo's own secret-scan. The new tests are already wired into both `make test` (the scanner suite runs at Makefile:42, validators at the CI `tests` job) and CI (`ci.yml:126` scanner, `ci.yml:102` validators), so no CI edit was needed.

Stabilization: `make` is unavailable on the Windows host, so the gate was emulated directly. 87 scanner-package tests + 136 repo-level validator tests pass; `allowlist.py` is at 100% line coverage (package TOTAL 90%); the catalog scanner gate (`scan_skill_security.py catalog/skills catalog/mcp-configs --fail-on high`) exits 0 (only pre-existing LOW MCP moving-ref findings); `skills.json` valid (250 skills), bundle audit PASS, `check_version_sync.py` green (no version surface touched). `ruff check` is clean on all new/changed code; the only finding is a pre-existing unused `import pytest` in the validator test file (F401 at HEAD line 16, not introduced here), left untouched per the no-out-of-scope-cleanup rule and recorded as WN-v31cr-4 -- the repo has no ruff hook (lint gate is ShellCheck-only). `ruff format` was intentionally not applied: the entire scanner package is non-ruff-format-clean by convention (15 of 18 files would reformat), so the new files match the established package style rather than becoming a lone outlier. No deviations from the plan; no bugs; all four quality gates passed (GO). Known-gaps: 1 new WN (WN-v31cr-4), 0 resolved; 4 WN open total. Next: Phase 3 (fold web AppSec attacker-perspective methodology -- SSRF/SSTI/XXE/deserialization/request-smuggling/IDOR -- into `advanced-attack-patterns` and `business-logic-abuse`, now that the allowlist exists to cap their fenced payloads).

Subtasks T001-T004 closed. Pure catalog content (2 new SKILL.md + 1 references/standards.md) plus registry + count-prose edits; no new code, dependency, credential, or outbound call. The phase deliberately precedes the Phase 2 scanner-allowlist tuning, so payloads were kept minimal and fenced to stay below the HIGH gate without relying on an allowlist that does not yet exist.

T001 created `catalog/skills/security/ai-attack-patterns/SKILL.md` (160 lines): offensive AI-security methodology (direct/indirect prompt injection, jailbreaking, RAG/knowledge-base poisoning, tool/agent abuse, unsafe-output handling), re-authored generically per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule (no Claude-Red / SnailSploit / Sahar Shlichov references). Data-exfiltration-via-injection is described conceptually (with the reserved `attacker.example` placeholder) rather than as a runnable payload, framing the skill as feeding defensive review rather than standalone offensive engagement.

T002 created `catalog/skills/security/pentest-reporting/SKILL.md` (169 lines): pentest report-writing methodology (report + finding anatomy, consistent CVSS base/temporal/environmental scoring, reproducible redacted evidence capture, risk-led executive summary, prioritized remediation, a retest-to-closure workflow, and a markdown report skeleton). No payloads -- pure report methodology, so scanner collision is near-zero (0 findings).

## [2026-06-05] - v3.1.0 adoption-dynamic-workflows Phase 1: Workflow-bundle convention (skill-native)

Implemented Phase 1 (of 3) of the v3.1.0 `adoption-dynamic-workflows` plan: the workflow-as-skill-bundle distribution convention plus one reference graceful-degrading Dynamic-Workflow template. Subtasks T001-T003 closed. Pure catalog content and prose (one `.js` template + two markdown edits); no new code path, dependency, credential, or outbound call. The phase establishes how a skill ships a Dynamic-Workflow `.js` file as a Tier-3 bundled resource (referenced from SKILL.md as a template to adapt, not a script to run) so later phases can pilot it on high-value read-only fan-out skills. Work was done on the `feat/adoption-dynamic-workflows` feature branch, fast-forwarded to `develop` first (it was two commits behind the branching-governance merge with no unique commits of its own).

T001 extended the "Per-skill Bundled Resources" subsection of `AGENTS.md` with a new "Workflow templates (Dynamic Workflows)" block. It states the three mandatory rules a bundled workflow template must satisfy: (a) graceful degradation -- the template must fall back to isolated subagents (small surface) or a single sequential agent (smallest surface) because Dynamic Workflows is a plan-gated research-preview capability that may be absent, and the skill must not hard-depend on the runtime; (b) the scope-first token caution carried inline (calibrate on one folder first, review the plan on first trigger, confirm before full scale) with a cross-link to `[[ai-billing-safeguards]]` for hard budget controls; (c) skill-native -- no outbound call, dependency, or credential. It points at `agent-orchestration-primitives` as the decision guide and notes the orphan-bundle audit applies unchanged (the `.js` must be referenced from SKILL.md).

T002 authored the reference template at `catalog/skills/orchestration/agent-orchestration-primitives/assets/example-fanout-workflow.js` -- a read-only fan-out-and-synthesize example (audit every file under a directory, then merge the findings) that opens with the required pure-literal `export const meta = {...}` block and a three-phase Discover -> Audit -> Synthesize shape using `phase()` / `agent()` / `pipeline()` / `log()` / `args`. Inline comments mark every adaptation point as a TEMPLATE TO ADAPT, carry the required graceful-degradation note and scope-first token caution as header banners, and explain the no-filesystem-access constraint (the work-list arrives via `args` on the scope-first path, or a discovery agent on the fallback path). It uses a `schema` on the per-file agent so findings return validated rather than text-parsed, and filters `pipeline()` nulls before flattening. The asset is referenced from the skill's SKILL.md Step 7 (the orchestration-patterns section) as a copy-adaptable starting point, so it is not an orphan bundle.

T003 stabilized. `make` is unavailable on the Windows host (WN-v31-1), so `make validate` was emulated by invoking each validator directly: the orphan-bundle audit passed (0 errors -- `example-fanout-workflow.js` is correctly recognized as referenced; the only warning is a pre-existing `demo-capture` `__pycache__/*.pyc` file, gitignored-but-on-disk, unrelated to this phase), all four JSON catalogs (`skills.json` 247 skills, `bundles.json`, `workflows.json`, `templates.json`) load, and no-personal-paths / unicode-safety / supply-chain / workflow-security / `check_version_sync.py` (green at 3.0.0 -- no version surface was touched) all exit 0. The new `.js` template and both markdown edits were verified ASCII-clean (0 non-ASCII chars; the AGENTS.md em-dashes / box-drawing glyphs the unicode scanner reports are all pre-existing, none in the inserted block). No `data/` registry edits were needed -- this adds an asset to an existing skill, not a new skill -- and that was confirmed. CI needs no edit: the `validate` job runs the same validators on the ubuntu runner. New known-gap: WN-v31-1 (local make partial, covered by CI). Summary: 1 open (1 WN), 0 resolved. Next: Phase 2 (pilot the convention on `multi-agent-code-review` and `deep-research-compilation`).

## [2026-06-04] - v3.0.0 command-consolidation-skill-security Phase 9: Ingested known-gaps (Swift/Kotlin extractors, heading cleanup, NI-v24-1)

Implemented Phase 9 (of 10) of the v3.0.0 `command-consolidation-skill-security` plan: the three actionable v2.4.0 known-gaps ingested into this plan. Subtasks T040-T043 closed. The phase adds two code-search language extractors, removes a cosmetic checklist redundancy across 71 skills, and closes a deliberate convention decision. The only new code is two Python extractors + two grammar dependencies; the skill edits are pure deletions; no new credential or outbound call.

T040 (DF-v24-7) shipped the recommended mobile extractor batch -- Swift and Kotlin -- raising code-search language coverage from 10 to 12. Both `extensions/nexus-code-search/.../extraction/languages/swift.py` and `kotlin.py` follow the established two-pass extractor idiom (walk declarations + build the index, then walk calls and resolve in-file name matches), match the sibling extractors' compact style, and emit the grammar-appropriate node/edge subset: Swift handles the grammar's single `class_declaration` (discriminated by the leading `class`/`struct`/`enum`/`actor` keyword), `protocol_declaration`, initializers, properties, enum cases, dotted `import` declarations, and `extends` (class) vs `implements` (protocol conformance); Kotlin handles `class`/`interface`/`enum class` (one `class_declaration` discriminated by keyword + `enum_class_body`), `object` singletons, enum entries (whose name lives in an `identifier` child, not a `name` field), package namespaces, top-level constants vs class properties, and `extends`/`implements` from delegation specifiers. The two grammars (`tree-sitter-swift` 0.7.x, `tree-sitter-kotlin` 1.1.x) version their package independently of the core's `<0.26` ceiling, so they were probed and verified ABI-compatible with the installed core 0.25.2 before pinning (`>=0.7,<0.8` / `>=1.1,<2`, with a `pyproject.toml` comment explaining the divergence). Registered `.swift` / `.kt` / `.kts` in `LANGUAGE_EXTRACTORS`. Each ships an eval fixture (`swift_app`, `kotlin_app`) clearing the 80% recall gate -- both land at 100% recall / 100% precision, and the full eval is 100%/100% across all 14 fixtures -- plus unit tests (8 Swift, 6 Kotlin). A bug surfaced during augmentation: the Swift `_descendants` helper used a LIFO stack that reversed sibling order, so `import os.log` picked `log` instead of the top module `os`; fixed by pushing children reversed for a true pre-order walk (now covered by a dedicated test). New-module coverage: swift 90%, kotlin 91%.

T041 (WN-v24-2) consolidated the 71 skills that carried BOTH `## Quality Checklist` and `## Verification` down to the single canonical `## Verification` binary checklist. A dry-run dedup showed the two sections' content is genuinely different in kind (Quality Checklist = looser, often-subjective best-practice/coverage items; Verification = the rigorous observable-artifact gate authored in v2.4.0), so folding would have bloated Verification and violated its binary-observable contract. The faithful resolution per T041's primary instruction was to remove the superseded `## Quality Checklist` section (its design guidance already lives in each skill's Instructions / Best Practices body), making these files consistent with the correctly-remediated Verification-only skills. The removal was surgical: a line-based pass with blank-line-hygiene normalization produced 911 deletions and 0 additions, touching only the QC headings and their items (verified via `git diff --numstat`; the pre-existing in-code-block double-blank-lines were confirmed in HEAD and left untouched). `validate_skills.py --quality` stays at 0 warnings across all 247 skills.

T042 (NI-v24-1) confirmed and recorded the convention-based decision to keep `validate_solution_frontmatter.py` as a single cross-platform `.py` validator with no `.ps1` sibling. ## [2026-06-04] - v3.0.0 command-consolidation-skill-security Phase 7: scanner optional modules (re-partial)

Implemented Phase 7 (of 10) of the v3.0.0 `command-consolidation-skill-security` plan: the two optional, default-off `nexus-skill-scanner` modules that complete its detection surface -- the class-14 signature engine and the live portion of class 4, the OSV.dev dependency-vulnerability lookup. Subtasks T033-T035 closed. This phase was recovered from an interrupted prior session: a network drop lost the conversation but left the working tree intact (the opt-in wiring in `pyproject.toml` / `analyzers/__init__.py` / `cli.py` / `scanner.py`, plus `dependencies.py`, `signatures.py`, the bundled `data/`, and `test_dependencies.py`). Recovery found T034 complete (16 tests green) and T033 functionally complete but missing its test file, plus a stale scanner `README.md`; this session closed both gaps and ran the post-phase sequence. The Phase 7 gate is behavioral: both modules degrade gracefully, the default scan stays byte-identical to Phase 6, and no new default outbound call is introduced -- the only network surface in all of v3.0.0 is the opt-in `--osv` query, which sends only a `{ecosystem, package, version}` tuple and ships an offline fallback.

T033 (signatures) is a self-contained pure-Python rule engine rather than a wrapper over the native `yara-python` binding -- a deliberate, user-endorsed DEVIATION from the plan's "lazy optional dependency" wording. It parses a small subset of the YARA grammar (named literal/regex strings with `any of them` / `all of them` / `N of them` / `$a and/or/not $b` conditions, evaluated by a recursive-descent parser that degrades a malformed condition to the safe `any of them` default rather than raising), runs the bundled rules fence-aware (a payload inside a Markdown fence is suppressed exactly as the text analyzers suppress theirs), and reports itself `skipped` when no rules can be loaded. The `pyproject.toml` change deletes the `yara = ["yara-python>=4.3"]` optional extra, keeping the scanner stdlib-only top to bottom: this sits one tier higher on the MCP Registry Policy decision tree (reverse-engineer into a local internal, not a vendor wrapper) and matches the no-external-dependency direction for this phase. Twelve re-authored rules ship across `cryptominers.yar` (stratum / XMRig / browser-miner), `exploits.yar` (bash-`/dev/tcp`, netcat, python-pty reverse shells + a PowerShell download cradle), and `webshells.yar` (PHP eval/obfuscated/system, JSP `Runtime.exec`, ASP `Eval(Request)`); no signature text is copied from any external rule set (Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule). The graceful-degrade contract is preserved but re-pointed -- "simulate YARA absent" becomes "simulate the bundled rules unavailable" -- and asserted at both the analyzer and `Scanner` levels.

T034 (OSV.dev) was recovered and verified: `dependencies.py` extracts pinned coordinates from `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` / `package.json`, matches them against a bundled 5-advisory offline DB (`data/osv_offline.json`), and -- only under `--osv` -- supplements with a live OSV.dev query via stdlib `urllib`, degrading to the offline result on any network/parse failure (`network_degraded` set, analyzer surfaces a skip note). The live call sends only the coordinate tuple. Its 16 tests cover constraint matching, manifest extraction, offline match, an injected-fetcher live merge (never a real network call), the coordinate-only privacy assertion, network-failure degrade, and the default-OFF wiring.

T035 stabilized. The new `tests/test_signatures.py` adds 18 tests (condition grammar, rule parsing incl. malformed-string skip and nocase, bundled-rule load, reverse-shell -> CRITICAL, cryptominer detect, clean -> none, fence-suppress vs prose-match, graceful degrade, default-off, scanner integration, and a monkeypatched scanner skip-note surfacing), bringing the package suite to 72 passed (was 54). Coverage: `signatures.py` 92%, `dependencies.py` 90%, total 90% (above the 80% gate). `ruff check` (0.9.4) is clean on the changed files. The scanner `README.md` was synced to document `--yara` and to drop the now-false "`--osv` reported as skipped until Phase 7" line. CI needs no edit: the `tests` job already pip-installs the scanner editable and runs `pytest extensions/nexus-skill-scanner/tests/`, so the new file auto-discovers, and no new env var or dependency was introduced (the `yara-python` extra was removed, not added). `make` is unavailable on the Windows host (WN-v30-4), so `make validate` was emulated directly: `skills.json` OK (247 skills), bundle audit PASS (1 pre-existing warning in `catalog/skills`, unrelated to `extensions/`), supply-chain / workflow-security / `check_version_sync.py` all exit 0 (version-sync green at 2.4.0 across all six surfaces -- the v3.0.0 bump is Phase 10's `/update release`). New known-gaps: DF-v30-3 (minimal starter content -- 12 rules + 5-advisory seed -- grows per release) and WN-v30-4 (local make partial, covered by CI); DF-v30-1's "class 14 + OSV are Phase 7, not gaps" note is now discharged. Next: Phase 8 (the 41 deprecation shims, the command-migration doc, and the count/template reconciliation).

## [2026-06-03] - v3.0.0 command-consolidation-skill-security Phase 6: nexus-skill-scanner engine (re-full)

Implemented Phase 6 (of 10) of the v3.0.0 `command-consolidation-skill-security` plan: the local internal static skill-security scanner that backs the `/skills scan` and `/review skill-scan` scopes and gates the catalog in CI. Subtasks T026-T032 closed. This is the `re-full` core from the SkillSpector comparison: a deterministic, stdlib-only engine that reads a skill's `SKILL.md`, its bundled scripts, and any MCP config and emits findings across the 15 static detection classes (1-13, 15-16) with a severity-banded risk score and framework-ID tags. Zero new outbound calls, no LLM client, no API key -- the semantic-adjudication stage is the Phase 2 `skill-security-scan` skill, run by the user's own agent. Per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule the package uses generic naming throughout and never references the upstream project.

T026 scaffolded `extensions/nexus-skill-scanner/` as a plain-Python package following the existing internal-MCP idiom (`src/nexus_skill_scanner/` + `tests/` + hatchling `pyproject.toml`, editable-installable, no LangGraph -- rejected per comparison N1). T027 implemented the analyzers: a fence-aware text-pattern analyzer (classes 1, 2-text, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) whose Markdown matches inside fenced code blocks are suppressed and whose prose patterns are all capped at MEDIUM; a Python-AST behavioral analyzer (class 12 -- `exec`/`eval`/`compile` builtins CRITICAL, dynamic import / subprocess / reflective-load MEDIUM, reflection LOW, with import-alias and from-import resolution so `import subprocess as sp; sp.run(...)` is caught and `re.compile` is NOT mistaken for the `compile` builtin), the executable portion of class 2 (an `os.environ` read plus a network egress call in the same script = HIGH credential exfiltration), and class 13 taint tracking (a tainted source reaching a code-exec sink = HIGH); and an MCP-config analyzer (classes 15-16 -- hardcoded credential and `curl|bash` command HIGH, over-broad scope / filesystem-root MEDIUM, moving package ref LOW, hidden override instructions in a description MEDIUM). All patterns are re-authored from public security knowledge. T028 implemented severity-point scoring (CRIT +50 / HIGH +25 / MED +10 / LOW +5, with a 1.3x executable-script multiplier), the four bands (0-20 LOW, 21-50 MED, 51-80 HIGH, 81-100 CRIT), framework-ID tagging of every finding (MITRE ATT&CK / ATLAS / D3FEND / NIST CSF, mirroring `references/detection-classes.md`), and the four emitters (terminal / JSON / Markdown / SARIF v2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning).

T030 subsumed the three fragmented validators behavior-preservingly: rather than re-author (and risk drifting from) their patterns, the scanner loads `validate_skills.py`, `scan_supply_chain_iocs.py`, and `validate_workflow_security.py` by path via `importlib` and routes their findings through the unified schema. The originals are left byte-for-byte unchanged -- their `make validate` entry points and entire pytest suites stay green -- so the unification is behavior-preserving by construction (the scanner literally calls their detection functions). Reusing `validate_skills.scan_text_for_secrets` directly preserves the v2.4.0 fence-aware secret nuance (BG-v23-1) with zero risk of divergence. When run outside a Nexus-Hub checkout the secret analyzer falls back to a compact re-authored pattern set; the repo-oriented supply-chain and workflow analyzers no-op. T029 added the thin `scripts/scan_skill_security.py` launcher (locates the bundled package whether pip-installed or in a repo / `~/.nexus-hub` checkout), registered it as an explicit-name copy step in BOTH installers (lockstep with the `check_version_sync.py` block; single cross-platform `.py`, no `.ps1` sibling per NI-v24-1), and added a `make scan` target. T031 added the planted-malicious fixture (prompt-injection prose + an `exec`/`compile`/exfiltration script -- scores CRITICAL) and the known-clean fixture (all dangerous-looking constructs inside fences -- scores LOW), the package test suite (38 tests: end-to-end gate, per-analyzer units, emitters, subsumption behavior-preservation), the repo-level `tests/validators/test_scan_skill_security.py` (drives the launcher end to end and dogfoods the catalog gate), and the CI catalog gate (`scan catalog/skills catalog/mcp-configs --fail-on high` in the validate job, plus the editable install + package suite in the tests job).

T032 stabilized. The engine scores the malicious fixture CRITICAL (exec/compile drive it) and the clean fixture LOW (0 findings -- every fenced `exec`/`eval`/`password`/"ignore previous instructions" suppressed), proving the fence-awareness is the difference. The catalog scan over 532 files produces ZERO HIGH/CRITICAL findings (12 MEDIUM + 2 LOW: security skills discussing injection/XSS in prose, skill-authoring skills describing SKILL.md edits, one legitimate `subprocess.run`, and the supabase `@latest` pin -- all the expected producer-catalog matches the semantic skill filters, none of which trips the per-finding HIGH gate), so the CI gate passes by construction. The two installer copy blocks reuse the exact `safe_copy ... true` / `Safe-Copy ... -Confirm:$true` sibling pattern, so they are ShellCheck-clean by construction (ShellCheck deferred to CI per WN-v30-3). `make`/`ruff` are unavailable on the Windows host (WN-v30-1/WN-v30-3), so the gate was emulated directly: 38 package tests + 134 repo validator tests green (including the three subsumed validators' original suites -- zero regression), `py_compile` clean on every new module, version-sync / supply-chain / workflow-security / bundle-audit all exit 0, editable install + console + module entry points verified, and the catalog/malicious/clean gate exit codes confirmed (0 / 1 / 0). New known-gaps: DF-v30-1 (pattern set is the highest-signal subset, grows per release; class 14 YARA + OSV are Phase 7), DF-v30-2 (taint tracking is a conservative module-scoped heuristic), WN-v30-3 (local lint partial, covered by CI). Next: Phase 7 (the optional, default-off YARA signature module and the offline-first opt-in OSV.dev dependency lookup).

## [2026-06-02] - v3.0.0 command-consolidation-skill-security Phase 1: Foundation -- version-sync guard + command scaffolding

Implemented Phase 1 (of 10) of the v3.0.0 `command-consolidation-skill-security` plan: the systemic fix for the v2.4.0-class version-drift CI failure plus the scaffolding the command consolidation (Phases 3-5) builds on. Subtasks T001-T004 closed. Pure local content (one stdlib validator, one style guide, build/CI/installer wiring, two invisible doc markers); no new outbound call, no new credential, no new runtime dependency.

T001 added `scripts/check_version_sync.py`, a stdlib-only version-drift guard. It reads the canonical version from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and asserts every other version-carrying surface matches it: `data/marketplace.json` (`plugin.version`), `scripts/installer.sh` (`NEXUS_HUB_VERSION="X.Y.Z"`), `scripts/installer.ps1` (`$script:NexusHubVersion = "X.Y.Z"`), the latest `CHANGELOG.md` `## [X.Y.Z]` heading, and a new `<!-- nexus-hub-version: X.Y.Z -->` marker in `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Surface semantics are deliberate: an absent surface file is skipped (so the guard works on partial trees), a present-but-version-less structured surface (installer/marketplace/changelog) is a finding, a present-but-marker-less README/AGENTS is skipped (the marker is an optional anchor), and a present-but-mismatched version is a drift finding. It accepts `--root` (for fixture trees), `--json` (CI), and `--verbose`; exit 0 in sync, 1 on drift, 2 when the canonical file is missing. Because the README/AGENTS prose carries many historical version references (`v2.0.0`, `v2.1.0`, ...) and no single canonical "current version" line, scanning free prose would false-positive heavily; the chosen fix is a machine-readable HTML-comment marker (invisible when rendered, ASCII-only) added to both files, which the guard asserts and which gives `/update version` (Phase 4) a precise bump anchor. The validator ships as a single cross-platform `.py` with no `.ps1` sibling, consistent with the five existing top-level `.py`-only validators (the NI-v24-1 convention). `tests/validators/test_check_version_sync.py` adds 13 cases (in-sync pass, each drift class - installer.sh / installer.ps1 / marketplace / changelog / README marker, multi-surface drift, partial-tree tolerance, missing-marker skip, unparseable-structured finding, missing-canonical usage error, and both JSON-output states); in-process coverage of the script is 93%.

T002 wired the guard everywhere it must run and distribute. The `make validate` target and the CI `validate` job both invoke `check_version_sync.py` (so a version drift now fails the build), and the script is registered as an explicit-name copy step in BOTH installers (after the `validate_solution_frontmatter.py` block, lockstep `safe_copy` / `Safe-Copy` to `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/`). The existing `test_installer_smoke.py` already asserts the two installer constants against plugin.json; this guard generalizes that to every surface as a build-failing gate, with no conflict.

T003 created `catalog/style-guides/command-scope-mechanism.md`: the distributable, author-facing version of the design doc's Section 4 scope contract (parse `$ARGUMENTS` -> recognized scope token skips the menu; else a numbered menu with a recommended default; `full`/`all` runs every focused scope in order; delegate to the retained skill), plus the optional dynamic-workflow fan-out with graceful-degradation guidance, a copy-paste thin-command skeleton template the later phases reuse, and an authoring checklist. Placed under `catalog/style-guides/` (NOT `catalog/commands/`, so it does not surface as a slash command) and auto-installs to `~/.nexus-hub/style-guides/`.

T004 stabilized. `make` and `shellcheck` are unavailable on the Windows host, so `make validate` was emulated by invoking each validator directly: all green, with `check_version_sync.py` reporting all six surfaces matched at 2.4.0. The targeted suite (`tests/validators` incl. the 13 new cases, `tests/installer`, `catalog/hooks/tests/test_installer_smoke.py`, `test_platform_parity.py`) is **228 passed / 0 failed**, confirming the installer copy-block additions regress nothing. `ruff check` is clean on both new Python files and `ruff format` was applied to `check_version_sync.py` (88-char wraps only). The ShellCheck pass on the new `installer.sh` block is deferred to the CI ubuntu job (recorded as WN-v30-1, low / covered-by-CI); the block reuses the exact pattern of its 15 siblings. A `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG section was added (safe: the guard matches only semver headings, so `[Unreleased]` is skipped and `[2.4.0]` stays canonical), and `docs/v3/v3.0/known-gaps.md` was initialized. Next: Phase 2 (skill-native adoptions -- the `agent-orchestration-primitives` and `skill-security-scan` skills, plus the `multi-agent-coordinator` enrichment).

It teaches: write each measured result to its own file immediately (never batch-flush), verify the write by reading it back (a truncated JSON write looks like progress on resume and is worse than no write), re-read state from disk at every phase boundary (never trust in-memory state across context compaction), keep an append-only `run-log.jsonl`, and write per-experiment `started` / `done` crash-recovery markers so a resume reruns only the interrupted experiment and never recomputes a completed one. T006 (ingested BG-v23-1) made the secret scanner fenced-code-aware. `scan_for_secrets` now delegates to `scan_text_for_secrets`, which tracks Markdown fenced code blocks with CommonMark semantics: an opening fence may carry an info string, but a closing fence must use the same character, be at least as long, and carry no info string. This correctly handles nested examples (a Markdown code block that itself shows a nested shell snippet, exactly the case in `user-documentation/SKILL.md`) that a naive toggle inverted. Inside a Markdown fence the low-confidence "Generic secret assignment" pattern is suppressed (documentation examples); high-confidence credential patterns (real API-key / token formats) are still flagged everywhere, so a genuinely leaked key in a code block is still caught. Result: 0 generic-secret false positives across the catalog (was 7); the unfenced case still fails. 5 new pytest cases added.

## [2026-05-30] - v2.3.0 adoption-superpowers Phase 5: flaky-test tooling cluster (P2)

Implemented Phase 5 of the v2.3.0 `adoption-superpowers` plan: shipping the two flaky-test tooling items the comparison's Section 5a flagged as superpowers tooling that Nexus-Hub's `flaky-test-detector` describes but does not bundle -- a test-pollution bisector and a reusable `waitFor` condition-based-waiting helper. Subtasks T018-T020 closed. This is a `re-full` phase: both artifacts are local code reverse-engineered into a project-agnostic form, so the change adds zero new runtime dependencies, zero outbound calls, and zero new credentials. Both ship as per-skill bundled resources auto-copied by the installer's recursive `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy`, so no `scripts/installer.{sh,ps1}` copy-step edit is needed; no `data/` registry file was touched (no new skill).

T018 added `catalog/skills/tests-generation/flaky-test-detector/scripts/find-polluter.sh` and its parity sibling `find-polluter.ps1`: a project-agnostic bisector that runs each test file in isolation, removes a watched pollution artifact before each run, and reports the first file whose isolated run re-creates it. The bash interface is `--watch <artifact>` / `--tests <glob>` / `-- <test-cmd...>` with a `{}` per-file placeholder (appended if absent), and the post-`--` command is executed as an argv array (no `eval`, honoring the bash security rules); the PowerShell sibling is `-Watch` / `-Tests` / `-TestCommand "<cmd>"` (the command string is split on whitespace into exe + args, with `{}` substituted as a single token so a file path with spaces survives). Both carry an unsafe-path guard on the watched pattern (refusing `/`, `.`, `..`, `~`, `$HOME`, `$PWD`, `*`), tolerate a failing test during bisection (only pollution matters), print the polluter to stdout for scriptability with logs on stderr, and exit 0 on a successful scan / 2 on a usage-IO error.

T019 added `catalog/skills/tests-generation/flaky-test-detector/assets/condition-based-waiting-example.ts`: a copy-in `waitFor(probe, description, timeoutMs = 5000, intervalMs = 25)` polling helper (matching the signature the Phase-3 `references/condition-based-waiting.md` already shows) plus `waitForEvent` / `waitForCount` / `waitForState`. It has zero runtime dependencies (only `setTimeout`), explicit return types, and heavy WHY comments encoding the flakiness footguns it avoids -- always an outer deadline, a small non-zero poll interval, swallow probe errors during polling and surface them only in the timeout message, and assert AFTER `waitFor` returns rather than inside the probe. A bisector block was added to `flaky-test-detector/SKILL.md` Step 3 naming both `find-polluter` scripts with a bash and a PowerShell invocation example, so the orphan-bundle audit stays clean; the `.ts` basename was already referenced from Step 2 and the Phase-3 reference.

T020 stabilized. The `make validate` equivalent was run directly (make unavailable on the Windows host): orphan-bundle audit PASS 0/0 across 237 skills, JSON catalogs OK (skills.json 231, untouched), and the no-personal-paths / unicode-safety / supply-chain-iocs / workflow-security validators all exit 0 with the four new/edited files ASCII-clean. `bash -n` on the script is clean. `.sh`/`.ps1` parity was CONFIRMED by running both siblings live against a throwaway fixture with identical results across 5 cases each (polluter detection, no-polluter, append-mode, unsafe-watch guard, no-match guard). The smoke test caught one real bug, fixed in-phase: a literal (metacharacter-free) `--watch` value always matched under `nullglob` in the `.sh` because a non-pattern word is not subject to globbing, so `artifact_exists` / `remove_artifact` / the test-glob expansion now test real on-disk existence with `-e` (the `.ps1` was unaffected -- it uses existence-based `Test-Path`). No new open gap was recorded: ShellCheck is unavailable on the host so the script was verified via `bash -n` + the live cross-OS smoke, and per-skill-script ShellCheck coverage in CI is already tracked under the transferred QG-v23-1; the `.ts` is a by-design copy-in example needing no test. Next: Phase 6 (final) -- the visual-brainstorm-server deferral record, AGENTS/CHANGELOG counts, and the final validation sweep, which (being the final phase) also triggers the release-readiness workflow.

## [2026-05-30] - v2.3.0 adoption-superpowers Phase 4: eval-harness trigger techniques (P1)

Implemented Phase 4 of the v2.3.0 `adoption-superpowers` plan: adding the three trigger-testing techniques superpowers' harness has that Nexus-Hub's `skill-eval-loop` lacked -- premature-action detection, multi-turn conversation triggering, and cheap-model fragility testing (comparison Section 8). Subtasks T014-T017 closed. This is a `re-full` phase: all three techniques are local code that reuses the eval harness's existing CLI dispatcher, so the change adds zero new runtime dependencies, zero outbound calls, and zero new credentials -- the harness drives the user's already-configured model CLI exactly as before. No `data/` registry file was touched (no new skill).

T014 added premature-action detection to `scripts/optimize_skill_description.py`. `extract_tool_invocations()` walks a CLI stream-json transcript (the same stream the superpowers harness greps for `"name":"Skill"`) and returns the ordered tool-use names, tolerating both newline-delimited events and a single JSON array; `detect_premature_action()` applies one rule over that list -- the first `Skill` invocation clears the run, and any non-allowlisted tool (anything other than `Skill` / `TodoWrite`) seen before it sets the flag, including the case where the skill never loads but a real tool ran. The flag is surfaced per-eval in the benchmark output: `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py` now passes `premature_action` through from the with_skill `grading.json` into `benchmark.json` (eval-level + the with_skill condition), defaulting False for the without_skill baseline that has no skill to load.

T015 added the multi-turn and cheap-model modes. For multi-turn, `evaluate_multi_turn()` replays an eval's ordered `turns` list through the dispatcher and records per-turn triggering, and the pure helpers `first_trigger_turn()` / `multi_turn_passes()` assert the skill FIRST triggers exactly at the designated `trigger_turn` (triggering early or never both fail) -- catching skills that fire on a cold prompt but not deep in a brainstorm-then-plan-then-execute flow. For cheap-model fragility, `invoke_cli()` was split into a pure `build_cli_command()` (so the new `--model` flag threading and the no-cross-CLI-bleed parity invariant are both testable without spawning a subprocess) and a `--model <name>` flag was threaded through `estimate_trigger_rate` / `run_iteration` / `_passes` / `render_dry_run`; a per-eval `model` field overrides the global flag. The `evals.json` schema (documented in `skill-eval-loop/references/schemas.md`) gained the optional `turns` / `trigger_turn` / `model` fields, and the grading/benchmark schema gained `premature_action`; both modes are opt-in so existing single-turn, default-model eval sets are unaffected.

T016 created `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/references/trigger-testing.md` documenting all three techniques (what each catches, how to author an eval that exercises it, how to read the new output fields, when to use each), cross-referencing the comparison Section 8 for provenance, and linked it from `skill-eval-loop/SKILL.md` (a new "Trigger-testing techniques" body section plus a Reference-files entry) so the orphan-bundle audit stays clean. `agents/grader.md` was updated to record `premature_action` from the optional `outputs/stream.jsonl` transcript using the documented rule.

T017 added 23 pytest cases to `catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py` (suite 14 -> 37 passed): premature-action detection over fixture stream-json including tool-ordering and the single-array fallback; the multi-turn pure-logic (`is_multi_turn` / `first_trigger_turn` / `multi_turn_passes`); `build_cli_command` argv assertions confirming `--model` threads into all four CLI branches and is omitted by default; a dry-run model-surfacing test; and a benchmark `premature_action` pass-through test. The existing CLI-adapter parity test stays green after the `build_cli_command` extraction, and a dry-run smoke (exit 0, train/test split + `test_trigger_rate` selection metric unchanged) confirms existing optimizer behavior is preserved. `make` is unavailable on this Windows host so pytest + validators were invoked directly: orphan-bundle audit PASS 0/0 across 237 skills, unicode-safety `--strict` 0 findings on the six changed files, no-personal-paths 0. CI already runs `pytest catalog/hooks/tests/` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 94) so the new cases are gated with no CI edit. The 73 failures elsewhere in `catalog/hooks/tests/` are pre-existing bash-hook-on-Windows environmental failures in five unrelated test files (same cross-OS class as DF-v23-6, green on Linux CI), not regressions from this phase. One new low-priority gap was recorded (DF-v23-8: a live end-to-end run of the three new modes is deferred to the Phase 6 final validation, alongside the DF-v23-7 live `skill-eval-loop` run; only dry-run + pure-logic + fixture-stream tests were done this phase). Next: Phase 5 (flaky-test tooling cluster -- the `find-polluter` bisector and the `waitFor` helper).

Its core is a six-step gate function (name the claim, identify the single proving command, run it fresh this turn, read the full output + exit code, confirm the output supports the claim, then claim while quoting the evidence), backed by a claim-to-evidence table (tests pass / linter clean / build succeeds / type check / bug fixed / requirements met / feature works / change in place) and a nine-row Common Rationalizations table. ## [2026-05-29] - v2.3.0 adoption-ecc-cybersec-skills Phase 9: live-environment verification (P1, FINAL)

Implemented Phase 9 (the final phase) of the v2.3.0 `adoption-ecc-cybersec-skills` plan, closing the last four v2.2.0 carryover gaps (WN-2, WN-3, WN-4 Antigravity CLI assumptions; WN-8 cross-OS installer smoke). Subtasks T032-T036 closed. The plan framed these as live-environment verifications that T036 explicitly allowed resolving via documentation or re-deferring with a dated reason if Google had not shipped a verifiable channel. By 2026-05-29 (the Gemini-CLI-to-Antigravity-CLI cutover is 2026-06-18) Google's Antigravity CLI documentation is public, so WN-2/WN-3/WN-4 were verified against primary docs + official codelabs rather than a live install; WN-8 was re-run on Windows and cross-checked against CI's Linux run. The pre-implementation review surfaced that the v2.2.0 probe had INFERRED the Antigravity conventions by analogy to Gemini CLI, and the docs contradicted several of them, so the path-rewrite scope was taken to the user up front (the user chose the full rewrite including the global-dir restructure).

T032 (WN-2): the Antigravity CLI binary name was CORRECTED from the inferred `antigravity` to `agy` (the official docs page is titled "Using AGY CLI"; the binary installs to `~/.local/bin/agy`; corroborated by multiple practitioner guides). This was a silent-failure bug: the diff-review hook detects the binary with `command -v` and fails open, so the wrong name made the entire Antigravity pre-commit review a no-op on every machine rather than erroring. Fixed the binary detection + invocation in `catalog/hooks/antigravity-cli-diff-review.sh`/`.ps1` (the product-named filename was kept, consistent with its siblings and its registration in both installers). T033 (WN-3): the workflow file format was CONFIRMED as Markdown under `.agents/workflows/` (the inferred value was right), reconciled in `test_antigravity_commands.py`. T034 (WN-4): YAML frontmatter is honored and a workflow's name derives from its filename -- DOCUMENTED; the existing verbatim `catalog/commands/*.md` mirror is compatible, so no `_write_antigravity_commands` variant was needed.

Verification surfaced bonus path corrections beyond the binary name: the per-project dir is `.agents/` (plural, per official codelab) not `.agent/`, the instruction file is `AGENTS.md` not `AGENT.md`, and the global CLI footprint is `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` not `~/.agent/`. These were applied across `scripts/lib/integrations/antigravity.py` (`workspace_dir=.agents`, `global_dir=~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, `instruction_file=AGENTS.md`), both installers' legacy mirror paths in lockstep, the `base-antigravity-20.md`/`base-antigravity-cli.md` templates, AGENTS.md, README.md, and the three antigravity integration test files (20 tests pass; `installer.ps1 -PrintConfig antigravity2` now shows the `.agents/` tree). The integration writes its instruction file to `.agents/AGENTS.md` rather than the project root: `agy` reads a root `AGENTS.md`, but that file is already managed by the `codex` integration through the single shared `## Nexus-Hub` marker, so pointing two integrations at it would clobber the block (a real install-time regression isolated tests would not catch). Whether `agy` requires a root `AGENTS.md` (needing a per-integration marker scheme) is one of four residuals recorded as WN-v23-5.

T035 (WN-8): the cross-OS smoke was re-run. Windows is empirically green -- 936 pytest cases (catalog/hooks 392+3 skipped, integrations+installer 260, validators 44, skill-server 43, code-search 168+1 skipped, web-fetch 29), eval recall 100% / precision 96.2% reproducing `docs/archive/v2/v2.3/eval-baseline.md`, and installer.ps1 -Help/-PrintConfig probes for claude/antigravity2/gemini-cli exit 0 with the negative case exiting 1. T028 (WN-6) taught `python.py` and `typescript.py` to emit `instantiates` (a call / `new` expression whose resolved target is a class, replacing the plain `calls` edge) and `overrides` (a method shadowing a same-named parent method, via a new `_resolve_overrides` pass that walks the in-file `extends` chain transitively with a cycle guard). `INSTANTIATES` was added to `traverser._IMPACT_KINDS` so re-typing a constructor call from `calls` does not silently drop it from `code_impact`. T029 (WN-7) wrapped the default FTS query as `name : (<query>)` in `traverser.search_fts` (new `_scope_to_name` helper), with an `all_columns` opt-out threaded through `GraphQueryManager.search` and surfaced on the `code_search` MCP tool as `all_fields`. The precision shortfall was a column-matching artifact: a query like `AdminUser` previously matched the class plus every node embedding it in `qualified_name` (its method `is_admin`, parameter `self`). Name-scoping raised aggregate eval precision from 63.3% to 96.2% with recall held at 100%.

T030 (DF-002) shipped four new extractors (`go.py`, `rust.py`, `java.py`, `csharp.py`) registered in `LANGUAGE_EXTRACTORS` for `.go`/`.rs`/`.java`/`.cs`/`.csx`, each following the `python.py` pattern. Go emits structs / interfaces / receiver-keyed methods / fields and `instantiates` from composite literals; Rust emits structs / enums / traits / impl-block methods, `implements` from `impl Trait for Type`, and `instantiates` from struct literals; Java and C# emit the full OOP edge set (`extends` / `implements` / `overrides` / `instantiates`), with C# resolving its single syntactic `base_list` into `extends` vs `implements` by the resolved target's kind. The new extractors deliberately omit `parameter` nodes to avoid re-introducing the FTS noise T029 just removed. Four tree-sitter grammar deps (go 0.25, rust 0.24, java/c-sharp 0.23) were added to `pyproject.toml` under the shared `<0.26` ceiling; no installer edit was needed because both installers resolve them via `pip install -e` of the copied package, and T030 added no standalone `scripts/*.py`. Four eval fixtures (`go_app` / `rust_app` / `java_app` / `csharp_app`) were added, each clearing the 80% per-fixture recall gate at 100%.

T031 created `docs/archive/v2/v2.3/eval-baseline.md` (eight fixtures: 100% aggregate recall, 96.2% aggregate precision) and repointed the Makefile `eval` target there. Tests after the phase: nexus-code-search 168 passed / 1 skipped (+32 new -- 6 each for Go/Rust/Java/C#, 3 Python-edge, 2 TS-edge, 2 name-scope, 1 recall-gate), zero DeprecationWarnings; the `make validate` equivalent (skills.json 227 OK, bundle audit 0 orphans, four CI validators rc=0) is green; CI requires no workflow edit (the editable install resolves the new deps and auto-discovers the new tests). Two new low-priority gaps were recorded: DF-v23-4 (extractor coverage is partial -- 4 of ~18 languages, no new framework extractors, no parameter nodes for the new languages) and DF-v23-5 (a `code_search` precision residual where import-statement nodes named with the dotted import path are legitimately surfaced; python_app sits at 70%). The five carryover items moved to the Resolved table in `docs/archive/v2/v2.3/known-gaps.md`. Four new runtime dependencies, all local tree-sitter grammars; zero outbound network calls anywhere in the new extractors.

## [2026-05-29] - v2.3.0 adoption-ecc-cybersec-skills Phase 7: installer instruction-file parity (P1)

Implemented Phase 7 of the v2.3.0 `adoption-ecc-cybersec-skills` plan, closing the three v2.2.0 installer-parity carryover gaps (DF-001, MT-1, MT-2) so the legacy bash / PowerShell instruction-file rendering blocks could be removed. Subtasks T022 (placeholder threading + path/template reconciliation), T023 (body-parity test), T024 (Copilot marker-merge), and T025 (stabilization) all closed. The user selected the reconcile-then-remove path after the pre-implementation review surfaced that the legacy bash path and the Python registry had diverged in three ways -- placeholders, workspace path, and Gemini template -- so a naive call-swap would have regressed end-user output.

The Phase 1 review compared the bash `render_template` (today's end-user output) against the Python registry runner and found: (1) bash filled 15 `{{...}}` tokens + `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` + per-language coding snippets while the runner substituted only `{{PROJECT_NAME}}`; (2) bash wrote claude / codex workspace instruction files at the project root while the registry nested them under `.claude/` / `.codex/` (where the tools do not read them); (3) bash rendered `base-gemini.md` while the registry pointed at the orphan stub `base-gemini-ide.md`. A fourth difference -- the registry wraps the body in `<!-- NEXUS_HUB_START/END -->` markers for user-edit preservation while bash wrote raw -- is the deliberate v2.2.0 improvement, so parity is asserted at the managed-body level rather than whole-file.

T022 brought the runner to body parity. `MarkdownIntegration._render` now merges a built-in default placeholder map (mirroring the bash constant `sed` values), auto-loads `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` from `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, leaves unknown tokens literal exactly as the bash `sed` list does (so `{{AGENT_REGISTRY}}` and friends survive verbatim), and appends per-language coding-snippet fragments. `scripts/lib/integrations/runner.py` gained `--var KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--languages`, and `--instruction-only` on `install` (plus `--var` / `--languages` on `print-config`), and `InstallContext` gained `languages` and `instruction_only`. The path divergence was reconciled with a new `instruction_workspace_dir` config key (default = `workspace_dir`) set to `""` for claude and codex so CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md land at the project root while skills/ still mirror nested; the Gemini integration was repointed to the canonical `base-gemini.md`.

T024 (MT-1) refactored `CopilotIntegration.install_workspace` from its bespoke append-after-heading flow onto the canonical `merge_marker_section(..., legacy_header="## Nexus-Hub Harness")` primitive (matching Cursor), so the v2.1 legacy header migrates inline, re-installs settle to `unchanged`, and teardown removes only the marker block. The removal step replaced all six `render_template` / `Render-Template` instruction-file calls (claude / codex / gemini, global + workspace) with `invoke_registry_platform ... --instruction-only` / `Invoke-RegistryPlatform ... -InstructionOnly`, keeping the surrounding catalog-copy blocks, and deleted both dead render functions. Both installer helpers now thread their detected globals (PROJECT_NAME, PRIMARY_LANGUAGE, BUILD_CMD, OS_CONTEXT, ...) to the runner, which is now the single instruction-file renderer shared by bash and PowerShell -- a side benefit being it also fixed a latent literal-placeholder bug for the already-registry-driven platforms (cursor / opencode / antigravity / nexus-ai).

T023 (MT-2) added `test_instruction_body_parity_with_legacy_render` (claude / codex / gemini x global + workspace) to `tests/integrations/test_parity_with_legacy_installer.py`: it installs each integration in isolation with the full placeholder set, extracts the marker body, and asserts byte equality against an INDEPENDENT naive-`str.replace` reference render (the bash-semantics oracle), plus a no-literal-placeholder completeness check. Installing each integration in isolation keeps the assertion deterministic even though a real multi-platform install now has codex and cursor sharing the root AGENTS.md marker block (last-writer-wins over two near-identical templates -- cleaner than the prior bash behavior, which duplicated both bodies).

Tests after the phase: `tests/integrations` + `tests/installer` + `tests/validators` 304 passed / 0 failed (the single initial failure, a Copilot test asserting the old bespoke `kept` action, was a TEST-class issue updated to the canonical `unchanged`); `catalog/hooks/tests` 392 passed + 3 skipped; the `make validate` equivalent (JSON + bundle audit + quality pass + four CI validators) is green; ShellCheck `--severity=warning` on both installers is clean; `bash -n` and PowerShell `Parser::ParseFile` both pass. No new runtime dependencies, no new standalone scripts (so no installer copy-step registration needed), zero outbound calls. One new low-priority gap recorded: DF-v23-3 (`base-gemini-ide.md` is now orphaned as an instruction template; optional future cleanup). See `docs/archive/v2/v2.3/known-gaps.md`.

Implemented Phase 6 of the v2.3.0 `adoption-ecc-cybersec-skills` plan: a framework coverage-matrix generator over the Phase 1 mapping convention, plus two re-authored defensive security skill packs and their helper scripts. Subtasks T017 (coverage generator), T018 (defensive batch 1), T019 (defensive batch 2), T020 (helper scripts), and T021 (testing and stabilization) all closed. Bulk import of the source cybersecurity corpus stays explicitly rejected (plan appendix N5 / N6 / N7); this phase ships curated, re-authored content only.

`scripts/build_framework_coverage.py` reads the optional framework-mapping frontmatter fields introduced in Phase 1 (`mitre_attack` / `atlas_techniques` / `d3fend_techniques` / `nist_csf` / `nist_ai_rmf`) across `catalog/skills/` and emits a coverage matrix: a summary table (distinct controls + skill tags per framework) plus per-framework control-to-skill detail tables, in Markdown (default) or JSON (`--format json`), to stdout or a `--out <file>` artifact. It ships its own tolerant bracket-list parser (the existing `validate_skills.py` frontmatter reader leaves `[...]` as a raw string), accepts `--root` so it slots into the `tests/validators/conftest.py` subprocess harness, and is read-only / local / zero-outbound -- a catalog with no tagged skills produces a successful empty matrix rather than an error. After the new content landed the matrix spans 34 ATT&CK techniques, 6 D3FEND countermeasures, and 10 NIST CSF categories. It is registered as an explicit-name copy step in both installers and covered by 6 pytest cases in `tests/validators/test_build_framework_coverage.py`.

The maintainer approved a new `security-operations` skill category (the AGENTS.md "Ask first: creating a new skill category" gate), separating defensive operational skills from the application-security `security/` category. Fifteen skills were re-authored to Nexus-Hub format under it. Batch 1 (DFIR / threat hunting / incident response): `memory-forensics`, `hunting-credential-dumping`, `disk-artifact-forensics`, `siem-detection-engineering`, `log-threat-hunting`, `lateral-movement-detection`, `ransomware-incident-response`, `persistence-mechanism-hunting`, `endpoint-edr-detection`. Batch 2 (cloud / endpoint / phishing): `cloud-security-posture-detection`, `cloud-audit-log-detection`, `container-runtime-detection`, `phishing-analysis-and-defense`, `identity-threat-detection`, `malware-triage-analysis`. Each skill carries a pushy description (verbatim trigger phrases + a SKIP clause), MITRE ATT&CK / D3FEND / NIST CSF framework-mapping frontmatter, a `references/standards.md` companion documenting every mapped control ID (framework name, short title, rationale, public source URL), a Common Rationalizations table whose Reality column cites concrete failure modes, and a binary Verification checklist tied to observable artifacts. All content was re-authored from public MITRE / NIST framework knowledge -- no third-party SKILL.md text was copied and no source repository is named in the artifact (Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule) -- and the mandate filter was enforced: defensive / detection / forensics / incident-response only, with offensive and detection-evasion content excluded (the phishing and malware-triage skills explicitly state "defense only" and "never write malware"). The 15 skills were drafted by five parallel subagents working from a single rigorous spec with pre-assigned, verified framework IDs; the data-registry edits and helper scripts were authored centrally to keep the three counters consistent and avoid concurrent JSON edits.

Two skills ship a deterministic helper with `.sh` + `.ps1` parity per the AGENTS.md cross-platform rule. `memory-forensics/scripts/volatility-runner.sh|.ps1` is a thin, read-only wrapper around a locally-installed Volatility 3 (`vol`) that runs a fixed triage plugin set (process tree, hidden-process carve, module list, injection scan, network connections, handles, cmdline) against a memory image into a per-case output directory, hashing the image first for chain of custody; it requires Volatility 3 already installed, fetches no symbol packs over the network, and never executes carved samples. `log-threat-hunting/scripts/ioc-log-scan.sh|.ps1` is a local read-only IOC sweep that fixed-string-matches an indicator list against a log file and reports per-indicator counts and matching lines (comment and blank lines in the IOC list are ignored). Both bash scripts follow the project safety rules (`set -euo pipefail`, quoted expansions, `command -v` capability checks, per-item failure isolation), are shellcheck-clean at `--severity=warning`, are referenced from their parent SKILL.md so the orphan-bundle audit passes, and were functionally verified (the IOC sweep against a fixture log; the Volatility wrapper's missing-`vol` precondition path).

Two new known gaps were recorded: QG-v23-1 (the CI `shellcheck` job lints `catalog/hooks/*.sh` but not the new per-skill helper scripts under `catalog/skills/**/scripts/`; the one-line fix is proposed but not auto-applied per the "never silently rewrite CI" rule) and DF-v23-2 (the defensive skill bodies are concise and fully conformant but could optionally be deepened with platform-specific query examples in a future catalog-quality pass).
