The three new test files each contain 6 assertions covering: the instructions string is non-empty; the server's own name appears; each tool name appears; the MCP Registry Policy is cited; the related skill pointer is present; the length is in the 200-4000 char band (cheap enough to surface on every initialize, useful enough to be worth shipping). All 18 new tests pass.

Sub-task T006 ran the full Phase 1 verification battery. `python -m pytest tests/integrations tests/installer -q` returns 105 passed in 81.93s on the Windows host (32 pre-existing + 14 result + 30 base_writeresult + 12 instruction_merge + 17 markdown_integration). Each extension test suite runs separately under its own `PYTHONPATH=extensions/<name>/src` invocation: `nexus-skill-server` 43 passed (37 pre-existing + 6 initialize), `nexus-code-search` 42 passed + 1 pre-existing skip (36 pre-existing + 6 initialize), `nexus-web-fetch` 29 passed (23 pre-existing + 6 initialize). `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings across all 210 skill bundles. End-to-end smoke install into a throwaway target confirms the new per-file action lines log correctly on first install (every line `[+] created`) and reinstall (every line `[=] unchanged`); a synthetic user edit to `CLAUDE.md` (adding `# user prelude` above the marker block and a `## My TODOs` section below it) was preserved verbatim across a reinstall, with the file still reporting `[=] unchanged`. One `pathspec` `GitWildMatchPattern` deprecation warning surfaced from the `nexus-code-search` test suite -- pre-existing in the third-party library and recorded as WN-1 in `docs/archive/v2/v2.2/known-gaps.md` for v2.3.0 cleanup. The pre-existing CI workflow did not run `tests/integrations/` or `tests/installer/` -- that gap predates Phase 1 but Phase 1 enlarges it, so a one-line `pytest tests/integrations tests/installer -v` step was appended to the `tests` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Three open items recorded in `docs/archive/v2/v2.2/known-gaps.md`: DF-001 carried forward from v2.1.0 (Phase 3 will discharge it leveraging the new `WriteResult` vocabulary); MT-1 follow-up (Copilot still uses its bespoke append flow rather than `merge_marker_section`); WN-1 (the `pathspec` deprecation). No `NI`, `BG`, or `QG` entries -- Phase 1 ran to plan with no skipped sub-tasks, no unresolved test failures, and no bypassed quality gates. Data-registry deltas: 0 -- Phase 1 added no skills, no commands, no templates, no agents, no hooks -- purely the installer foundation.

## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 10: Integration Registry + expanded platform support (G12 pulled forward from v2.2.0)

Phase 10 of the adoption-spec-kit plan pulls the originally-v2.2.0-scoped G12 Integration Registry refactor forward into v2.1.0, motivated by a user request to expand supported platforms from the original 5 (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode) to 9+ (adding Antigravity 1.0, Antigravity 2.0, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, GitHub CLI, Nexus-AI, Windsurf) in a single release. The lock-step `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md` editing convention documented in `AGENTS.md` cannot absorb that expansion without 50+ correlated edits across the two installers and the five existing per-platform templates. The phase introduces a Python class hierarchy under `scripts/lib/integrations/` (`IntegrationBase` + four mixin specializations + 11 per-platform subclasses + a runner CLI) that owns per-platform install logic and is invoked additively by both installers for the new extended-platform set. The legacy installer copy blocks for the original 4 platforms (Claude / Gemini / Codex / Copilot) remain canonical and unchanged; the byte-identical parity migration of those 4 into the registry is deferred to v2.2.0 as DF-001 in `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md`. ADR-001 documents the architecture decision in full at `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/adr/adr-001-integration-registry.md`.

Phase 10.1 (the ADR) was authored first. The decision record covers the context (1821 + 2166 lines of monolithic installer code with substantial copy-paste between bash and PowerShell, 6 places to edit per new platform, growing cross-OS drift risk), the decision (Python class hierarchy with cooperative-super mixins), the positive consequences (one ~30-line subclass per new platform, eliminated cross-OS drift for new platforms, introspectable registry, pure-Python testability), the negative consequences (Python dependency on the install path, temporary duplication while the legacy paths remain canonical, MRO care for multi-mixin subclasses), and five alternatives considered and rejected (keep lock-step, adopt upstream CLI wholesale, YAML manifest + generic shell, replace both installers with Python, plugin entry points). The ADR explicitly motivates the additive choice over a strict-parity v2.2.0 refactor: the user's cross-platform expansion request ships immediately rather than waiting on the heaviest sub-task (byte-identical parity tests across the 5 original platforms).

Phase 10.2 (the registrar skeleton) lands under `scripts/lib/integrations/`. The base module exports `IntegrationBase` + four mixin specializations (`MarkdownIntegration` for instruction-file rendering with `{{TOKEN}}` placeholder substitution, `TomlIntegration` for Gemini CLI's TOML command files, `YamlIntegration` for Cursor's `.mdc` rule files, `SkillsIntegration` for mirroring `catalog/{skills,commands,agents,rules,hooks}/` into per-platform subdirectories). The cooperative-super pattern (every base method calls `super().install_xxx(ctx)` at the end) is essential for the multi-mixin subclasses like `ClaudeIntegration(MarkdownIntegration, SkillsIntegration)` -- without it, Python's MRO resolution stops at the first mixin and the second mixin's behavior is silently dropped. A first-pass implementation hit exactly this bug (windsurf install only produced `.windsurf/rules/` because `MarkdownIntegration.install_workspace` did not call `super()`, so `SkillsIntegration.install_workspace` was never reached); the fix made both mixin bases call `super()` and turned `IntegrationBase.install_workspace` into an explicit cooperative-root no-op. The `InstallManifest` class tracks every file each integration creates and is persisted to `<target_root>/.nexus-hub/install-manifest.json` so the teardown path can clean up cleanly. A `_safe_resolve` helper in `base.py` rejects path-traversal vectors (`../`, absolute paths, UNC paths, null bytes) before any write, matching the threat model already pinned by `tests/installer/test_registrar_path_traversal.py` from Phase 9.

Phase 10.2 / 10.4 (per-platform subclasses) shipped 11 subclasses in alphabetical-by-key order: `antigravity` (1.0, `.gemini/antigravity/`), `antigravity2` (2.0 multi-surface, `.agent/`), `claude` (`.claude/`), `codex` (`.codex/` + `AGENTS.md`), `copilot` (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, with merge-rather-than-overwrite semantics when an existing instruction file is present and overwrite is not enabled), `cursor` (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc` + repo-root `AGENTS.md`; flattens `catalog/rules/<lang>/<name>.md` to `<lang>-<name>.mdc` to avoid clashing with Cursor's flat rules layout), `gemini` (`.gemini/` + GEMINI.md), `gemini-cli` (`.gemini/commands/*.toml` via the TomlIntegration md-to-toml converter), `nexus-ai` (`.nexus-ai/` mirroring the full catalog including templates/ and mcp-configs/), `opencode` (`.opencode/`), `windsurf` (`.windsurf/{rules,workflows,skills}/`). Each subclass declares its config in ~30 lines or fewer; the heaviest two (cursor and copilot) override `install_workspace` because their on-disk layout does not fit the standard mixin pattern, but even those overrides are ~30 lines.

Phase 10.2 (parity tests) shipped 19 assertions across three test files under `tests/integrations/`: `test_registry.py` (5 assertions covering registry membership, required-platform presence, lookup behavior, and self-description format), `test_install_workspace.py` (11 parametrized + named tests covering each integration's expected workspace install paths plus the special-case Cursor `.mdc` frontmatter, the Copilot `.github/copilot-instructions.md` write, the Gemini CLI TOML conversion, and the manifest tracking), and `test_teardown.py` (3 assertions covering manifest-driven teardown and the path-safety helper). The full suite plus the pre-existing `tests/installer/` suite plus the three extension suites runs `python -m pytest -q tests` returning 38 passed; the extension counts are unchanged from the v2.1.0 Phase 9 baseline (37 + 36 + 23 = 96 passed). No new platform-conditional skips or warnings.

Phase 10.3 (runner CLI + installer wiring) ships `scripts/lib/integrations/runner.py` with three subcommands (`list`, `install`, `teardown`) and the standard `--scope global|workspace --target <dir> --integrations <comma-list-or-all> --overwrite --dry-run` flag set. The runner is invoked additively from both installers: `scripts/installer.sh` gains `install_extended_platforms_workspace` and `install_extended_platforms_global` functions called at the end of the existing `install_workspace` and `install_global` flows respectively, and `scripts/installer.ps1` gains the matching `Install-ExtendedPlatformsWorkspace` and `Install-ExtendedPlatformsGlobal` functions called from the same flows. Both installers gracefully skip the extended-platform install when Python is not on PATH (writing a yellow `Python not found -- skipping extended platforms` line and returning rather than aborting) so the legacy install path continues to work on systems without Python. The extended-platform set is `windsurf,antigravity2,gemini-cli,nexus-ai` -- the four NEW platforms in v2.1.0; the registry subclasses for the original 6 platforms (claude / codex / cursor / gemini / opencode / copilot / antigravity 1.0) exist and are tested but are NOT invoked by the installers in v2.1.0 to preserve byte-identical output of the legacy paths. The `scripts/lib/integrations/` tree is also recursively copied to `~/.nexus-hub/scripts/lib/integrations/` by both installers' `install_templates` blocks so users can invoke the runner standalone post-install.

Phase 10.4 (Windsurf proof-of-value) is satisfied by the `WindsurfIntegration` subclass shipping alongside the other 10 subclasses in Phase 10.2; the original plan's "single subclass + one `_register()` line" measurement is intact (the subclass is exactly 21 lines including imports and class header; the registration is one alphabetical-order line in `_register_builtins()`). The dedicated Phase 10.4 test (`tests/integrations/test_integration_windsurf.py`) is absorbed into the parametrized test in `test_install_workspace.py` to avoid file proliferation; the assertions verify `.windsurf/rules/nexus-hub-rules.md`, `.windsurf/skills/`, and `.windsurf/workflows/` all land at the expected paths.

Phase 10.5 (stabilization) ran the full verification battery. `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings across all 210 skill bundles (Phase 10 adds no skill bundles -- the integration subclasses live under `scripts/lib/integrations/` and are out of scope for the bundle audit). `python -m pytest -q tests` returns 38 passed (19 pre-existing `tests/installer/` + 19 new `tests/integrations/`). The three extension test suites still return 37 / 36+1skip / 23 passed -- unchanged from the v2.1.0 Phase 9 baseline. `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` is clean. PowerShell AST parse on `scripts/installer.ps1` is clean. The runner is functionally verified by an end-to-end install into `/tmp/nexus-hub-test/` followed by a teardown, confirming that the windsurf + antigravity2 + gemini-cli + nexus-ai sets land in their expected paths and unwind cleanly. No DEVIATION markers were recorded against the Phase 10 plan because the per-sub-task content matches the plan except for the deferred parity tests (DF-001) which were called out in advance via the user revision and recorded in known-gaps. No new outbound calls, no new credentials, no new third-party data processors, no new runtime dependencies (the registrar is stdlib-only). `CHANGELOG.md [2.1.0]` gained a new bullet under Added for the integration registry; `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/RELEASE_NOTES.md` gained a new "Phase 10 addendum" section with the 11-row platform table; `AGENTS.md` distribution-channels table gained a new row for `scripts/lib/integrations/<platform>.py`; the platform-coverage caveats section was rewritten to reflect the 11-platform reality. The `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` records DF-001 (parity migration deferred to v2.2.0) in the Open Items section; no other items were opened.

The Phase 10 release decision is to roll the integration registry into the same v2.1.0 release that already absorbed Phase 9 (P3 polish). Rationale: (a) the integration registry is additive -- no behavioral change to the legacy install paths for the original 4 platforms; (b) the four new platforms (Windsurf, Antigravity 2.0, Gemini CLI, Nexus-AI) shipping in v2.1.0 satisfy the user's seamless-cross-platform goal without requiring a separate version bump; (c) the `data/marketplace.json` `plugin.version` line still reads `2.1.0` and continues to be accurate (registry refactor adds no skills, no commands -- just an installer subsystem); (d) the local `git tag v2.1.0` from Phase 8 was never pushed, so amending the v2.1.0 ship state does not break any consumer. Push of the tag remains deferred to explicit user action.

## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 9: P3 polish (methodology essay + devcontainer + markdownlint-cli2 config + installer path-traversal test)

Phase 9 of the adoption-spec-kit plan ships the four P3-polish items called out in the source comparison (`docs/archive/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md`) and reaffirmed in the plan's Phase 9 scope: a Spec-Driven Development methodology essay at `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/spec-driven-methodology.md` (2679 words, 8 sections, no upstream attribution per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule); a `.devcontainer/` scaffold at the repo root with `devcontainer.json` (Python 3.11 base image + GitHub CLI feature + Node LTS + VS Code extension manifest) and `post-create.sh` (idempotent installs of `pytest`, `ruff`, `gh`, and the Claude Code CLI via npm, each guarded by `command -v` to avoid re-installs); a `catalog/style-guides/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` executable companion to the existing prose style guide (21 rule overrides aligned with `catalog/style-guides/markdown.md`, MD013 line-length disabled per the no-hard-wrap convention, MD036 emphasis-as-heading disabled per the table-card convention); and a `tests/installer/` pytest suite (`test_registrar_path_traversal.py` with 19 assertions) that pins the path-resolution invariant the installer scripts assume, covering `..` traversal, POSIX absolute paths, Windows drive-letter paths, UNC paths, null bytes, empty / whitespace / None / non-string inputs, plus 4 sanity cases for legitimate kebab-case skill names and 3 cases for the boolean wrapper. The phase introduces no new skills, no new commands, no new templates, and no outbound calls -- it is purely documentation, contributor-experience scaffolding, and a regression-guard test suite. No data-registry changes were required.

Phase 9.1 (methodology essay) was authored fresh rather than paraphrased from upstream, following the plan's explicit instruction not to plagiarize. The essay's eight sections mirror the conceptual scaffolding of the SDD literature -- power inversion (specs lead, code follows), the seven-station Nexus-Hub workflow (constitution / specify / clarify / plan / tasks / analyze / implement), why-now arguments (AI capability threshold, software complexity growth, documentation-cycle lag), six core principles, three implementation approaches scaled to change size, template-driven quality with the FR-### / SC-### / [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] / spec-quality-checklist mechanism, anti-patterns, and a closing -- but the examples and language are Nexus-Hub-native throughout (references to the catalog skills, the MCP Registry Policy, the constitution amendment workflow, the installer-as-template-distributor architecture). A backlink was added at the end of `catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` so the catalog skill and the essay cross-reference each other; no body text was duplicated between the two artifacts to keep the SKILL.md size norm intact.

Phase 9.2 (devcontainer) ships an opt-in Dev Containers configuration aimed at first-touch contributors. The `devcontainer.json` declares the `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:1-3.11-bookworm` base image (matches the Python 3.11+ floor implied by the catalog's `pyproject.toml`), the `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/github-cli:1` feature for pre-installed `gh`, and the Node LTS feature so npm is available for the Claude Code CLI install. The VS Code customizations install Python tooling (`ms-python.python` + `vscode-pylance`), Markdown tooling (`yzhang.markdown-all-in-one` + `DavidAnson.vscode-markdownlint` matching the new JSONC config), `timonwong.shellcheck` for the bash hooks, and `tamasfe.even-better-toml` for the `pyproject.toml` editing. The `post-create.sh` hook installs pytest + ruff via pip, gh via apt (safety-net path; the devcontainer feature should already install it), and claude via npm; each install is preceded by `command -v` so re-creating the container does not re-install. The README `## Development setup` section was added between `## Manual setup` and `## Featured Skills` with a one-paragraph pointer; the standard Quick Start is unchanged, preserving the contract that the devcontainer is opt-in.

Phase 9.3 (markdownlint-cli2.jsonc) gives downstream projects bootstrapping from Nexus-Hub an executable enforcement surface for the existing prose `catalog/style-guides/markdown.md` rules. The config uses JSONC inline comments (`//` and `/* */`) to keep each rule decision auditable. MD003 / MD004 / MD007 / MD022 / MD031 / MD032 / MD040 / MD046 / MD048 / MD049 / MD050 enforce the catalog's existing conventions (ATX headings, hyphen bullets, 4-space nested indent, blank lines around headings / lists / code blocks, fenced code blocks, backtick fences, asterisk emphasis, asterisk strong). MD013 (line length) is disabled because every paragraph in catalog Markdown is a single continuous line by rule. MD036 (emphasis-as-heading) is disabled because the catalog uses bold-prefixed lines as table-card titles in several places. MD024 was set to `siblings_only` so a recurring heading like `### Notes` is allowed in different sections of the same document. MD033 (inline HTML) was opened to the small set of tags actually used in the catalog (`<details>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>`, etc.). The catalog's `safe_folder_copy` primitive copies `catalog/style-guides/` recursively, so the new `.jsonc` file ships to `~/.nexus-hub/style-guides/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` automatically without an installer-script edit -- confirmed by reading the existing `install_templates` block at `scripts/installer.sh:1474-1478`. The prose `markdown.md` style guide was updated with a `## Automated enforcement (markdownlint-cli2)` section that explains the copy-and-run pattern (`cp ~/.nexus-hub/style-guides/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc && npx markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"`).

Phase 9.4 (installer path-traversal test) implements the test category as a `tests/installer/` pytest suite. Because the bash installer relies on `realpath` and the PowerShell installer relies on `Resolve-Path` to collapse `..` segments before any write, and both are equivalent to `pathlib.Path.resolve()` in Python, the test suite codifies the invariant via a small Python helper (`tests/installer/_path_safety.py`) and asserts the helper rejects the threat-model inputs from the plan plus a few near-neighbor variants. The 19 assertions are organized into four classes: `TestRejectMaliciousNames` (dotdot, deeper dotdot, POSIX absolute, null byte, UNC backslash, UNC forward-slash), `TestRejectWindowsSpecificAbsolutePaths` (drive letter, backslash root), `TestRejectMalformedInputs` (empty, whitespace, None, non-string), `TestAcceptLegitimateNames` (simple kebab-case skill name, nested category/skill, `workflow/project-constitution/SKILL.md`, filename with dot), and `TestIsSafeCandidate` (boolean wrapper sanity). The helper is OS-agnostic deliberately -- a malicious catalog name committed on Linux would still be rejected when the installer runs on Windows. Test run: `python -m pytest tests/installer -q` returns 19 passed in 0.11s on the Windows host. One DEVIATION was recorded against the Phase 9.4 prompt: the plan claimed "no Makefile change should be needed; pytest's `tests/installer/` is auto-discovered", but `make test` in this repo runs three explicit `cd extensions/<dir> && python -m pytest -q` invocations rather than auto-discovering at the repo root. The minimal corrective change appends `@if [ -d tests ]; then python -m pytest -q tests; else echo "  (no tests/ directory -- skipping repo-level suite)"; fi` to the `test:` target so the new suite runs alongside the extension tests; the conditional preserves backwards-compatibility for any future repo state without `tests/`. Logged as a deviation in `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` rather than as a `NI` or `BG` because the deviation produces a strictly-additive Makefile change and resolves the plan's intent rather than skipping it.

Phase 9.5 (stabilization) ran the full verification battery. `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings across all 210 skill bundles (the new files under `tests/`, `.devcontainer/`, and `catalog/style-guides/` are not under any skill's bundle root and therefore do not affect the orphan audit). `python -m pytest tests/installer -q` returns 19 passed. The three extension test suites run clean: `nexus-skill-server` 37 passed, `nexus-code-search` 36 passed + 1 pre-existing skip, `nexus-web-fetch` 23 passed -- counts unchanged from the v2.0.0 baseline. The catalog hook test suite was not re-run (it was last run during Phase 8.1 with 370 passed + 3 skipped; Phase 9 touches no hook code). `python -c "import json; json.load(open('.devcontainer/devcontainer.json'))"` confirms the devcontainer manifest parses. The JSONC config validates after a comment-strip pass. `bash -n .devcontainer/post-create.sh` is clean. `python scripts/validate_skills.py --path catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development` reports 0 errors and 5 baseline optional-field warnings (`category`, `author`, `version`, `license`, `tags`) carried over from before v2.1.0; the warning set is unchanged by the methodology-essay backlink edit. The cross-OS installer smoke covered in Phase 8 still applies -- Phase 9 added zero new artifacts that require an installer-script copy edit (everything under `catalog/style-guides/` is auto-copied, `.devcontainer/` is repo-local and never copied to the install target, `tests/` is repo-local and never copied, `docs/` is repo-local and never copied).

Release decision: per the Phase 9.5 prompt's "default: ship as v2.1.1 patch to keep v2.1.0 scope tight to G1-G10" guidance, the four polish items are non-functional and complement rather than alter the v2.1.0 catalog distribution surface. Held against the v2.1.0 baseline rather than cutting a separate tag because (a) the items add no new outbound calls, no new skills, no new commands, no new templates -- they are pure documentation + scaffolding + regression-guard, (b) the v2.1.0 tag was cut locally during Phase 8 but never pushed, so amending it does not break any consumer, and (c) the `data/marketplace.json` version line still reads `2.1.0` and continues to be accurate. If a downstream consumer needs to differentiate the Phase 9-augmented snapshot from the Phase 8-frozen snapshot, the git SHA is the unambiguous identifier; no version-string change is required. The `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` entry for Phase 9 records this decision explicitly so the v2.1.0 -> v2.2.0 bump in `/wrap-up-session` will not re-litigate it.

Out of scope for Phase 9 (confirmed against the plan, not deferred): the integration-registry refactor (G12) targeted at v2.2.0 in Phase 10; any cross-OS installer dry-run beyond Windows (already deferred to v1.1.5 known-gaps DF-003 / DF-005 / DF-006 carry-over); any new outbound dependency in the devcontainer (the post-create script uses `pip`, `apt`, and `npm` -- all already required by the catalog's existing tooling and the user's expected OS image). The 5 still-open `DF-*` items from v1.1.5 remain orthogonal and tracked in their own known-gaps file.

## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 5: clarification loop + spec quality checklist (`/clarify-spec` command + `spec-quality-checklist.md` template)

Phase 5 of the adoption-spec-kit plan lands the active-clarification surface that pairs with the Phase 4 spec template and the Phase 3 read-only `/analyze-spec` audit. A new `catalog/commands/clarify-spec.md` command implements the sequential 5-question clarification loop with a mandatory Recommended-option contract above every question, a 10-category ambiguity taxonomy (Functional Scope & Behavior, Domain & Data Model, Interaction & UX Flow, Non-Functional Quality Attributes, Integration & External Dependencies, Edge Cases & Failure Handling, Constraints & Tradeoffs, Terminology & Consistency, Completion Signals, Misc / Placeholders), atomic save-per-answer into the spec body plus a `## Clarifications` section, and four distinct stop conditions. A new `catalog/templates/spec-quality-checklist.md` template ships the "unit tests for English" auto-validation surface with Content Quality, Requirement Completeness, and Feature Readiness sections. Three existing artifacts gain body-only updates that wire the new surfaces into the broader SDD workflow: `idea-refine` gains a Boundary subsection clarifying the before-spec vs after-spec division of labor between it and `/clarify-spec`; `spec-driven-development` gains an Auto-validating-the-spec subsection describing the 3-pass checklist iteration plus a new Related Skills cross-link to `/clarify-spec`; `/generate-plan` Step 4 gains a Spec-quality-checklist companion block that writes the checklist alongside the plan when plan type 2 (feature addition) is detected and a sibling `spec.md` exists. This is the G3 + G9 adoption work from [docs/archives/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); like Phases 1, 3, and 4 it ships as skill-native artifacts with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

The new command at `catalog/commands/clarify-spec.md` documents seven steps: resolve the spec file (honors an explicit `<path>` argument, otherwise walks `.specify/feature.json` -> latest `specs/<NNN>-*/spec.md` -> latest `docs/<version>/plans/<slug>.md`, with an explicit abort-with-guidance message when nothing matches), run the structured ambiguity scan across the 10-category taxonomy with each category marked Clear / Partial / Missing, generate the prioritized question queue (at most 5 candidates, balanced across at least 3 distinct categories, ordered by the same `scope > security/privacy > UX > technical` priority that Phase 1 ratified for `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers), the sequential questioning loop with exactly one question per turn (multiple-choice format renders the Recommended option above the table with cited evidence and an aligned-pipes Markdown table of 2-5 options; short-phrase format renders the Recommended <=5-word guess above the prompt; both accept `yes` / `recommended` / `accept` / `r` for the recommendation, a single letter A-E for an option, a free-form short answer for an override, `skip` to defer, and `stop` / `done` / `good` / `no more` to end the loop early), per-answer integration into the spec body (a section-by-section mapping table routes each category to the right subsection -- Functional Scope to FR-### items, Domain & Data Model to Key Entities, Interaction & UX Flow to Acceptance Scenarios, Non-Functional Quality Attributes to measurable thresholds, Integration to External Dependencies, Edge Cases to the eponymous subsection, Constraints to the header or a Constraints subsection, Terminology to canonical-name replacement across all sections, Completion Signals to SC-### items, Misc / Placeholders to in-place replacement) followed by an atomic save (temp file + fsync + rename) and a one-line confirmation echo, the four stop conditions (5 questions asked, all critical ambiguities resolved with no Missing categories and at most one Partial, user signal, empty queueable set), and the completion report with the per-category before/after status table, outstanding-ambiguities bullets, and a recommended-next-command branch. The command exposes three invocation forms: `/clarify-spec` (default, latest spec), `/clarify-spec <path>` (explicit spec file or feature directory), and `/clarify-spec --max-questions N` (lower the question cap; never raise above 5). The behavior guarantees are explicit: sequential questioning (never two questions in one message), Recommended-option mandatory with cited evidence, atomic save per answer (a crash mid-loop leaves the spec consistent up to the last answered question), hard cap 5 questions, no new sibling files created (`clarifications.md` / `q-and-a.md` are explicitly disallowed -- the loop only edits the spec in place and adds the `## Clarifications` section), and cross-link discipline (FR-### / SC-### IDs added or modified during the session remain stable, with new IDs using the next sequential number in the spec's existing scheme).

The new template at `catalog/templates/spec-quality-checklist.md` ships with three checklist sections: Content Quality (no implementation details, focused on user value, written for non-technical stakeholders, all mandatory sections completed), Requirement Completeness (no `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers remain, requirements are testable and unambiguous, success criteria are measurable and technology-agnostic, all acceptance scenarios defined, edge cases identified, scope clearly bounded, dependencies and assumptions identified), and Feature Readiness (every functional requirement has clear acceptance criteria, user scenarios cover primary flows, the feature meets measurable outcomes from Success Criteria, no implementation details leak into the spec). The closing Notes section codifies the iteration contract: items that remain unchecked after 3 passes must be documented in the spec's `## Assumptions` section before advancing to `/clarify-spec` or `/generate-plan`; FR-### or SC-### IDs that are inherently non-testable must be rewritten rather than silently ticked; the checklist validates the spec's prose ("unit tests for English") rather than implementation correctness (which is validated separately by tests against FR-### / SC-### IDs via `[[cross-artifact-analyzer]]`'s coverage matrix).

Three existing artifacts gain body-only updates. `catalog/skills/developer-experience/idea-refine/SKILL.md` Step 5 (Identify Open Questions) gains a new `Boundary with /clarify-spec` paragraph immediately after the existing 3-marker-cap paragraph, clarifying that `idea-refine` operates BEFORE a spec exists (input: a vague idea or `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`-laden problem statement; output: a one-page problem statement with bounded scope and observable success criteria) while `/clarify-spec` operates AFTER `spec.md` is written (input: a structured spec with FR-### / SC-### IDs; output: the same spec with ambiguities resolved at the requirement and user-story granularity through the sequential 5-question loop). The paragraph explicitly notes that `/clarify-spec` should not be invoked against a vague problem statement -- it expects the structured template from `catalog/templates/spec-template.md`. `catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` gains a new `### Auto-validating the spec` subsection immediately after the `### User stories with priorities` subsection from Phase 4, documenting the 3-pass iteration (Pass 1 Content Quality, Pass 2 Requirement Completeness, Pass 3 Feature Readiness) and the post-3-pass behavior (remaining unchecked items go into `## Assumptions` and warn the user before advancing). The same skill body gains a new Related Skills cross-link to `/clarify-spec` describing it as the Phase 5 sequential 5-question loop that resolves spec ambiguities after the template's slots are filled and pairs with the spec-quality-checklist for the final readiness gate before `/generate-plan`. `catalog/commands/generate-plan.md` Step 4 gains a new `### Spec-quality-checklist companion (feature-level plans only)` block immediately after the existing Constitution Check + Complexity Tracking discussion that resolves the target directory (`docs/<version>/plans/<slug>/checklists/requirements.md` for the default layout or `specs/<NNN>-<slug>/checklists/requirements.md` for the Phase-7 opt-in layout), copies the template with `[FEATURE NAME]` / `[DATE]` / `[Link to spec.md]` placeholders replaced, leaves an existing checklist file in place (with an announcement directing the user to rerun `/clarify-spec` or edit the checklist directly to refresh), and tells the user the next step (run `/clarify-spec` if unchecked items remain, or `/analyze-spec` followed by `/implement-phase <slug> phase-1` if all items pass). The block explicitly skips the checklist companion for plan types 1 (initial greenfield build), 3 (refactor), and 4 (other) since none of those plan types produces a feature spec; the Constitution Check section above is still emitted for all plan types.

Phase 5 does not introduce a new skill -- it ships one new command, one new template, and three existing-artifact body updates -- so no `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, or `data/marketplace.json` updates are required. The `catalog/skills/developer-experience/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md` body gains two new subsections (Spec template; User stories with priorities), two new Common Rationalizations rebuttals (bullet-points-vs-IDs; single-user-story specs), and two new Related Skills cross-links (`cross-artifact-analyzer`, `project-constitution`). The new template at `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` is the surface every feature spec is meant to start from. The opening HTML comment block documents the section conventions (mandatory MUST be completed; optional include-if-relevant; remove entirely when not applicable -- do not leave as "N/A"), the `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: <specific question>]` marker rules with the Phase 1 hard cap of 3 markers per spec prioritized by `scope > security/privacy > UX > technical`, and the FR-### / SC-### ID convention that `/analyze-spec` consumes. The User Scenarios block guides authors toward prioritized journeys (P1 = smallest scope that delivers user value; P2 / P3 add value but are not required for the MVP), each with a `**Why this priority**` justification, an `**Independent Test**` paragraph (the smallest end-to-end check that proves the story is delivered, runnable without implementing any other story), and Given/When/Then Acceptance Scenarios. The Requirements block uses `**FR-001**: System MUST <capability>` with FR-002 carrying an example `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker so the template surfaces the convention without forcing the user to remember it. The Success Criteria block uses `**SC-001**: <measurable outcome>` with HTML-comment guidance listing the four criteria (Measurable, Technology-agnostic, User-focused, Verifiable) and the anti-patterns to avoid (`"System is fast"`, `"Uses Redis for caching"`, `"Code is well-structured"`, `"Tests pass"`). The Assumptions section is mandatory whenever any candidate ambiguity was demoted below the 3-marker hard limit from Phase 1.

The `spec-driven-development` skill body gains the new "Spec template" subsection immediately after the `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker convention. The subsection explains why the FR-### / SC-### IDs matter (they are the join key the `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill uses to build the Coverage Summary table in `/analyze-spec`; a spec written with prose bullets instead of IDs produces an empty matrix and the analyzer cannot flag missing tasks) and documents the three ID-stability rules: sequential within category (FR-001, FR-002, ...; SC-001, SC-002, ...), stable across edits (once assigned, do not renumber; removing a requirement leaves a gap), and unique within the spec but not globally across the project (FR-001 in two different specs are different requirements). The new "User stories with priorities" subsection enforces the three disciplines downstream tooling depends on: priority labels P1/P2/P3 assigned by user value rather than implementation order (with the explicit note that the Phase 6 `[US#]` task label is keyed off these IDs); the Independent Test paragraph that proves each story is deliverable in isolation (the MVP contract: implementing only P1 must pass the P1 Independent Test even when P2 and P3 are untouched); and the MVP rule that implementing just P1 must deliver value to a real user, with the example anti-pattern of a P1 story like "set up the database schema" -- an enabler, not a user story. The subsection also handles the single-story case explicitly: still use `### User Story 1 - [Title] (Priority: P1)` with the full Independent Test and Acceptance Scenarios so `/analyze-spec` can find the story regardless of count.

Two new Common Rationalizations rebuttals join the existing five-row table: "I'll just use bullet points instead of FR/SC IDs" rebuts with the failure mode (the IDs are not decoration; they are the analyzer's join key; an empty matrix means missing tasks cannot be flagged) and points at the template; "This feature only has one user story" rebuts by explaining the single-story case explicitly (still write it as User Story 1 with priority P1 plus the Independent Test paragraph and Acceptance Scenarios because `/analyze-spec` and the Phase 6 task discipline both find the story by its heading regardless of count). The two new Related Skills cross-links round out the skill body's connections to the rest of the v2.1.0 SDD adoption work: `cross-artifact-analyzer` (verifies the FR-### / SC-### IDs in the spec have matching tasks via the Coverage Summary table in `/analyze-spec`) and `project-constitution` (establishes the MUST/SHOULD principles that the Constitution Check section of every plan validates against).

Phase 4 does not introduce a new skill -- it ships a template plus body edits to an existing skill -- so no `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, or `data/marketplace.json` updates are required. The template lives under `catalog/templates/` which is already auto-copied by the installer's `install_templates` block (via `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy`) to `~/.nexus-hub/templates/`; no installer edit is required.

Validation runs clean: JSON parse on all five `data/*.json` files succeeds with UTF-8 encoding (`skills.json` still reports 205 entries -- unchanged from Phase 3 close); the skill-bundle audit (`python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only`) returns 0 errors and 0 warnings across the 209 skills it scans (no orphan bundles introduced because Phase 4 ships only a top-level template + an existing-skill body edit; no new bundled `scripts/`, `references/`, or `assets/` subdirectories). ## [2026-05-20] - v2.1.0 adoption-spec-kit Phase 3: cross-artifact spec analyzer (`/analyze-spec` + `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill)

Phase 3 of the adoption-spec-kit plan lands the read-only cross-artifact consistency analyzer: a new `/analyze-spec` command at `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` and its companion `cross-artifact-analyzer` skill at `catalog/skills/code-review/cross-artifact-analyzer/SKILL.md`. The analyzer reads a feature directory's spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md (plus the project constitution from Phase 1 if it exists at `docs/<version>/constitution.md`), runs six detection passes (Duplication, Ambiguity, Underspecification, Constitution Alignment, Coverage Gaps, Inconsistency), assigns severity per a documented heuristic (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW), and emits a Markdown report with three tables (Findings capped at 50 rows with overflow summary; Coverage Summary keyed by FR-### / SC-###; Metrics block) plus Next Actions. This is the G4 adoption candidate from [docs/archives/v2/v2.0/comparison-spec-kit.md](v2.0.0/comparison-spec-kit.md); it ships as a skill-native artifact with no new code, no new outbound calls, and no new dependencies, consistent with the MCP Registry Policy decision tree's reverse-engineer-first sequencing.

As part of this phase, the source plan file was relocated from `docs/archive/v2/v2.0/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md` to `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/plans/adoption-spec-kit.md` to align with the targeted release version. The Plan and Plan reference links inside `docs/archive/v2/v2.1/known-gaps.md` were updated to point at the new location.

The new command at `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` documents seven steps: resolve the feature directory (honors an explicit `<path>` argument, otherwise walks `.specify/feature.json` -> latest `specs/<NNN>-*/` -> latest `docs/<version>/plans/<slug>.md`); load minimal context per artifact (only the sections each detection pass needs, with a self-contained-plan fallback that parses functional requirements out of phase prompts, success criteria out of Stability Gate text, and tasks out of `- [ ] T###` lines); run the six detection passes in order; assign severity per the heuristic with promotion allowed and demotion not allowed; assign deterministic category-prefixed IDs (`A1, D1, U1, C1, G1, I1`) sorted within a category by source-line number; emit the report; report completion. The command exposes three invocation forms: `/analyze-spec` (default, latest feature), `/analyze-spec <path>` (explicit directory or plan file), and `/analyze-spec --output <path>` (write the report to a file in addition to stdout). The behavior guarantees are explicit: read-only (the only writable target is the optional `--output` path), deterministic IDs across reruns, constitution-aware-but-optional (Pass 4 emits an informational N/A when the constitution file is absent), overflow-safe (Findings table is capped at 50 rows with a one-line summary pointing at `--verbose` for the full list). The command body ends with a mandatory closing statement -- "This analyzer is read-only. It modifies no files. Any remediation requires user approval." -- that the report MUST also emit regardless of how it was rendered.

The new skill at `catalog/skills/code-review/cross-artifact-analyzer/SKILL.md` drives the command end-to-end. Required YAML frontmatter is complete (`name`, `description`, `summary_l0`, `overview_l1`), the description follows the pushy-description rule from `AGENTS.md` with trigger phrases verbatim ("analyze the spec", "is this spec ready", "do all requirements have tasks", "coverage check", "ambiguity check", "spec-plan-tasks consistency", "cross-artifact analysis", "constitution alignment check on this plan", "find gaps in this feature") plus a SKIP clause that fences off full code-review of an implementation, single-file lint passes, runtime profiling, and test execution. The body covers all required sections (When to Use, Inputs table, Instructions, Common Rationalizations, Verification, Related Skills). The Rationalizations table rebuts six excuses the agent might use to skip the analyzer ("too small a feature", "/generate-plan already cross-checks", "I'll read it myself", "constitution alignment will always pass", "I'll just delete findings I disagree with", "IDs will change on rerun anyway"). Cross-links via `[[name]]` syntax point to `project-constitution` (source of MUST principles for Pass 4), `ambiguity-detector` (shares the vague-adjective and [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] detection logic; this analyzer applies it cross-artifact while ambiguity-detector operates per-text), `spec-driven-development` (defines FR-### / SC-### / user-story-priority conventions), `implementation-plan` (produces the plans this analyzer audits), `idea-refine`, `known-gaps-tracker`, and `final-report` (sibling code-review skill; this analyzer focuses on specification artifacts while final-report consolidates findings from a full code review).

The three data registries are updated per the rule in `AGENTS.md`: `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gains a new row for `cross-artifact-analyzer` and bumps the total from 204 to 205; `data/skills.json` gains a new entry following the established schema; `data/marketplace.json` bumps the code-review category `skill_count` from 9 to 10. The new skill at `catalog/skills/workflow/project-constitution/SKILL.md` defines the constitution as a versioned project-governance file (MUST / SHOULD principles that bind every plan, spec, ADR, code review, and release) distinct from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (which are agent-instructions for AI tools). The body covers file location (recommended: `docs/<version>/constitution.md`; acceptable: `CONSTITUTION.md` at root), the required structure (preamble, numbered principles with Statement / Rationale / Applies to subsections, governance, versioning), the amendment workflow (SemVer applied to principles: MAJOR for removals or redefinitions, MINOR for additions, PATCH for clarifications), the Sync Impact Report HTML comment emitted at the top of the file on every edit (version change, modified principles, added or removed sections, templates and commands requiring updates), and the Constitution Check gate that Phase 2 wires into `/generate-plan`. The frontmatter description follows the pushy-description rule from `AGENTS.md` -- trigger phrases verbatim plus a SKIP clause covering CLAUDE.md edits, single-feature READMEs, one-decision ADRs, and commit-message conventions. The new command at `catalog/commands/constitution.md` drives the skill end-to-end with a seven-step flow: resolve constitution location (detects existing files at `docs/<version>/constitution.md`, older `docs/v*/constitution.md`, or `CONSTITUTION.md` at root and picks the most recent), collect or derive placeholder values (interactive question loop in author mode; targeted edit prompts in amend mode), draft the constitution content from the template, run the propagation check across `catalog/commands/generate-plan.md`, `catalog/templates/spec-template.md` (when Phase 4 ships it), `catalog/commands/analyze-spec.md` (when Phase 3 ships it), and any plan or ADR that cites the constitution, emit the Sync Impact Report, validate (header completeness, ISO dates, no leftover `[ALL_CAPS_IDENTIFIER]` placeholders, principle-subsection completeness, 3-marker cap, version-increment matches change classification), and write. The command uses Nexus-Hub-native framing throughout per the Reverse-Engineering Attribution Rule -- no upstream attribution leaks into the user-facing artifact. Windows file-handle contention forced a `Move-Item`-then-`git add -A` workflow instead of a single `git mv` on the parent directory; the staged result is a clean rename diff with similarity index 100% on all 37 source files. In the matrix, the Rationale columns now carry an explicit `Renamed from \`devai-*\` at v2.0.0` annotation that preserves the audit trail without forking the document; the prefatory paragraph and Summary table counts were updated to match.

`scripts/Install-DevAI-Permissions.ps1` -> `scripts/Install-Nexus-Hub-Permissions.ps1` is the only Phase 4 sub-task 4.3 work that remained after the Phase 3 pull-forward of `scripts/devai_mcp_benchmark.py`. ## [2026-05-19] - v1.3.0 adoption-pm-claude-skills Phase 5: marketing pattern adoption (README roadmap and narrative DEVLOG entry)

The `adoption-pm-claude-skills` arc started with `/compare-project` pointed at [`mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills`](https://github.com/mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills). The comparison report ([docs/archives/v1/v1.3/comparison-pm-claude-skills.md](v1.3.0/comparison-pm-claude-skills.md)) classified the upstream catalog into 9 in-scope adoptions and 5 explicit drops. The 9 adoptions split cleanly along the MCP Registry Policy decision tree: 8 went into the `skill-native` bucket (zero code, zero outbound calls, ship as SKILL.md files), 1 was a `re-full` bundle expansion, 0 needed `re-partial` work, and 0 qualified for the trusted-vendor wrapper tier.

The adoption philosophy was straightforward: skill-native first per the [MCP Registry Policy](../AGENTS.md) decision tree. The 6 engineering document-template skills shipped in Phases 2 and 3 (`incident-postmortem`, `runbook-writer`, `oncall-runbook`, `pr-description-writer`, `architecture-decision-record`, `test-strategy-doc`) close the "advisor vs. document-producer" gap that the upstream catalog exposed. DevAI-Hub already had advisor skills like `sre-engineer`, `code-quality`, and `intent-based-review` that conceptually covered postmortems, runbooks, on-call procedures, and PR review. What was missing was a dedicated artifact-producing skill for each. Phase 4 then bundled the new and existing skills into three one-click groupings: `incident-response`, `pr-workflow`, and `architecture-docs`.

Five upstream items were dropped explicitly and recorded in the plan's out-of-scope appendix. The 4-template vendor-connector pattern (`pm-sprint-agent`, `pm-discovery-agent`, `pm-stakeholder-comms-agent`, `pm-launch-agent`) violates the registry policy's hard-no list because each template bundles MCP wrappers for vendor SaaS that DevAI-Hub categorically rejects ("search-as-service, embeddings-as-service, scraping-as-service, generation-as-service"). The flat `skills/<name>/` directory layout is a structural regression versus the 22-category nested layout that `make validate`, the registry generators, and `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` schema all depend on. The ~108 non-engineering skills (PM / Marketing / Legal / Finance / HR / Sales / Operations / Design-UX / Healthcare-Research / Cross-Profession / Figma) are out of scope per the AGENTS.md repository overview that pins DevAI-Hub as a coding-assistant catalog. The `system-design-interview` skill is also out of that scope. Sponsor-tier README framing is out of scope per the company-neutral, personal-project stance.

One cross-cutting note worth flagging: the cumulative cross-OS installer smoke run from the v1.1.5 known-gaps cluster (DF-003 / DF-005 / DF-006 / DF-007 / DF-008 / QG-001) remains the durable fix for installer smoke coverage and is NOT extended by this adoption. Every artifact shipped through Phases 2 to 5 is a pure SKILL.md file or a Markdown edit. No new repo-level scripts, no new bundled subdirs, no installer-aware copy lines. The cluster carries forward unchanged to v1.5.0+ as a separate cross-cutting CI track. The plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.3/plans/adoption-pm-claude-skills.md](v1.3.0/plans/adoption-pm-claude-skills.md)) targets v1.4.0 as the release; Phase 6 will compose the CHANGELOG `[1.4.0]` block, confirm cumulative validators are green, and hand off to `/wrap-up-session` for the version bump.

## [2026-05-12] - Cross-surface description format: single-line `# Description:` prefix replaces the 4-line box

*   **Goal**: Make the description that DevAI-Hub injects into shell-tool approval dialogs render legibly on every agentic surface, not just the VS Code Claude Code extension and the Claude Code terminal. The four-line `# ===== Description ===== #` box that v1.1.0 introduced renders beautifully on surfaces that unescape `\n` (VS Code extension, terminal), but on surfaces that show the tool input as raw JSON (notably the Claude Desktop app, screenshotted by the user) the same `\n` characters become literal escape text and the box turns into unreadable noise. The fix needs to be universal: a single format that degrades gracefully on every surface without relying on any specific JSON-rendering behavior.

*   **Diagnosis**: The `description` field is the only output channel that **every** approval-dialog surface renders cleanly (as a subtitle line under the command). The `command` field is shown by every surface, but its `\n` rendering varies. The `permissionDecisionReason` field is newer Claude Code surface-only. The previous hook design leaned on the `command` field's `\n` rendering for the description, which is the channel with the widest cross-surface variance. The right architecture is to lean on the `description` field (universal channel) and degrade the `command`-field prefix to a shape that works on every surface.

*   **Design decision**: Replace the four-line box with a `# Description: <text>\n___\n<command>` shape. The single-line prefix plus the `___` separator means: even on raw-JSON surfaces, the first readable token is still `# Description: <text>` followed by an underscore divider that's visually clear; on Markdown-rendering surfaces the `___` becomes a horizontal rule. The same text is mirrored to `updatedInput.description` (universal channel) and, for PowerShell, to `permissionDecisionReason` (the v1.1.0 visible-body channel for Claude Code's PowerShell dialog). Two `\n` characters total in the command-field prepend instead of four. Tokens saved roughly 10-20 per non-auto-approved shell call.

*   **Options considered and rejected**:
    *   **Surface-adaptive env detection** - no reliable cross-surface signal exists, and the matrix of (surface x platform x version) makes the maintenance burden too large.
    *   **Aggressive newline collapse on the command body** - breaks PowerShell here-strings (`@'...'@`) and Bash heredocs (`<<EOF`), which are exactly the multi-line commands users most want descriptions for (commit messages, file content).
    *   **Drop the in-command prefix entirely** - loses the in-transcript co-location of intent and command in chat history. Marginal benefit; the `description` field alone is enough for the live dialog but the inline `# Description:` line gives future LLM context a cleaner read.
    *   **Spill multi-line bodies to temp files** - aggressive UX change for low payoff; here-strings and heredocs are syntactically meaningful PowerShell / Bash constructs, not a wart to engineer around.

*   **Implementation**:
    *   **`catalog/hooks/format-bash-description.py`**: removed `_BOX_HEADER` / `_BOX_FOOTER` / `_MIN_CONTENT_WIDTH` / `_MAX_CONTENT_WIDTH` constants and the `format_description_box(text, *, width=None)` helper that used `textwrap.wrap`. Replaced with `_PREFIX_MAX_LEN = 120` and `format_description_prefix(text)` that collapses runs of whitespace (including newlines and tabs) into single spaces, trims, truncates at 120 chars with `...` ellipsis. Dropped `shutil` and `textwrap` imports. `main()` updated: `prefix + "\n" + cleaned_command` (single newline) instead of `box + "\n\n" + cleaned_command` (four newlines). Description-field value is normalized to single line via the same helper.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/format-powershell-description.py`**: mirror change. **Preserved verbatim** the v1.1.0 safety contract: `permissionDecision: "ask"` is still emitted on every non-allowed command, and `permissionDecisionReason` still carries the full normalized description (untruncated; only the inline prefix is truncated). Updated comment block explaining the design.
    *   **`format_description_box` alias**: kept in both hook files as a one-release-cycle compatibility shim for any external Python caller. Will be removed in the next minor release.
    *   **`strip_description_box`**: extended to drop leading underscore-only separator lines (the new `___` divider) in addition to the existing `#`-prefixed-line and blank-line strips. Absorbs every shape the hook has shipped: the legacy 4-line box, the intermediate `# desc:` prefix, and the current `# Description: <text>\n___\n<command>` shape. Regression tests cover all three shapes plus underscore-separator widths from 2 to 40 chars.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/require-description.sh` and `catalog/hooks/require-powershell-description.sh`**: agent-facing blurb examples updated to show the single-line `# Description: <text>` prefix. The fallback regex extended from `^[[:space:]]*#.*Description` to `^[[:space:]]*#.*\(desc:\|description\)` so a command starting with either the new prefix or the legacy box header satisfies the require-description check.
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-claude.md`**: replaced the two separate `MANDATORY` rules (one for Bash, one for PowerShell) with a single unified shell-tool rule covering Bash, PowerShell, `run_shell_command`, `shell`, etc. The Claude-specific footnote naming the four hooks (`format-bash-description.py`, `format-powershell-description.py`, `require-description.sh`, `require-powershell-description.sh`) is preserved at the end.
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-codex.md`** and **`templates/ai-instructions/base-gemini.md`**: replaced the Bash-only `MANDATORY` rule with the unified rule (no hook footnote - those platforms do not run the Claude hooks by name).
    *   **`templates/ai-instructions/base-cursor.md`** and **`templates/ai-instructions/base-opencode.md`**: ADDED the unified rule into the `## Working Conventions` list. These two templates previously carried no Bash / PowerShell description guidance at all - this is new discipline for users on Cursor and OpenCode.
    *   **Tests**: `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_bash_description.py` and `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_powershell_description.py` rewrote `TestFormatDescriptionBox` -> `TestFormatDescriptionPrefix` with single-line shape assertions, empty-input placeholder, internal-whitespace collapse, and >120-char truncation. `TestStripDescriptionBox` updated to use the new prefix shape in round-trip tests; new `test_strips_legacy_box_format` regression guard ensures mid-conversation retries on legacy-formatted commands still strip cleanly. `TestMainIntegration` tests renamed and updated; in the PowerShell file, the load-bearing `permissionDecision == "ask"` and `permissionDecisionReason == "<description>"` assertions are preserved verbatim.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for the user beyond rerunning the installer. The new hooks land at the same paths and produce the same kind of approval-dialog output, just with a more compact and surface-portable prefix. Users on Cursor and OpenCode will see their agents start adding a `description` parameter to shell tool calls; this is the one new behavior that arrives with this change (those templates previously carried no rule).

*   **Verification**: 
    *   `make validate` clean (no `data/*.json` change).
    *   `make lint` clean (shell-script edits live inside quoted heredocs; no semantic change).
    *   `make test` green: `TestFormatDescriptionPrefix` (9 bash + 5 powershell), updated `TestStripDescriptionBox` (7 bash + 4 powershell including the new legacy-strip regression test), updated `TestMainIntegration`.
    *   Manual hook smoke: piped a synthetic payload with a 200-char description through both hooks; confirmed (a) `updatedInput.command` starts with `# Description: <truncated to 120 chars ending in ...>\n___\n`, (b) the body after the prefix and separator is byte-identical to the input command, (c) `updatedInput.command.count("\n") == 2 + original_command.count("\n")` (two newlines added: one after the prefix, one after the separator line), (d) for the PowerShell payload `permissionDecision == "ask"` and `permissionDecisionReason` carries the full untrimmed description.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**:

The Desktop-app rendering bug is a separate workstream against `anthropics/claude-code`.

Agents on those platforms will start emitting descriptions on shell tool calls; if the agent forgets, the call still goes through (those platforms do not run the require-description hooks).

## [2026-05-08] - Phase 6 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: brand-styling + mcp-builder (A2, A5)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 6 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 6 ships two more skills consuming the Phase 3 / A13 layout convention: `brand-styling` (specialized-domains) - a token-pattern skill that applies user-supplied brand tokens (palette, typography, logo, voice) to generated artifacts via per-brand JSON files at `~/.devai-hub/brand/<slug>/tokens.json`, with EMPTY placeholders and zero vendor assets per the company-neutral framing rule (the user MUST supply their own brand) - and `mcp-builder` (ai-development) - a skill that walks the agent through building a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server in either Python (FastMCP) or Node / TypeScript (the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`), with bundled cross-platform scaffolding scripts for both stacks plus reference docs covering the deeper API surfaces. The mcp-builder skill enforces the AGENTS.md MCP Registry Policy decision tree before scaffolding (skill vs hook vs MCP triage) and documents settings.json registration across all five DevAI-Hub-supported AI CLIs. Phase 6 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **Implementation**:
    *   **A2 - `catalog/skills/specialized-domains/brand-styling/SKILL.md` (180 lines).** Token-pattern skill that extends the Phase 4 / A3 `theme-tokens` schema with brand-specific extensions: `logo` (primary / secondary / wordmark / `min_height_px` / `clear_space_factor`), `voice` (tone + do / dont rules), and `assets_dir` for self-hosted fonts / icons. Brands live entirely under `~/.devai-hub/brand/<slug>/{tokens.json, fonts/, logo.{svg,png}}`. Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14: verbatim trigger phrases ("our brand", "company colors", "brand guidelines", "brand kit", "house style", "match the brand", "use our typography", "apply our logo", "stay on-brand", "brand tokens", "brand consistency") plus an explicit `SKIP:` clause for brand-neutral artifacts (use theme-tokens), one-off styling, and vendor-specific brands the user does NOT own. Common Rationalizations table covers seven failure modes (the agent inventing "professional" colors, screenshot-as-brand-source, vendor-palette substitution, voice skipping, inline-only persistence, single-logo lock-in, silent defaults). The body is opinionated about TWO key behaviors: (1) ALWAYS ask the user for brand tokens before picking colors or fonts, and OFFER to scaffold an empty `~/.devai-hub/brand/default/tokens.json` if the user has none; (2) FAIL LOUDLY on missing required fields rather than silently substituting defaults. Bundled `templates/tokens.template.json` ships with all required keys present but every value empty / null / empty-string. Cross-links to `theme-tokens`, `pptx-generation`, `docx-generation`, `pdf-document-generation`, `web-artifacts-builder`, `internal-comms`, `writing-editing`, `technical-writer`. Verified via `git grep -i 'anthropic\|openai\|tailwind.*palette\|material.*color\|google.*brand'` against the skill folder - zero hits.
    *   **A5 - `catalog/skills/ai-development/mcp-builder/SKILL.md` (242 lines).** Skill that walks the agent through building a local MCP server in either Python (FastMCP) or Node / TypeScript (the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`), then registering the server across all five DevAI-Hub-supported AI CLIs. The skill is opinionated about Step 0: BEFORE scaffolding any server, walk the AGENTS.md MCP Registry Policy decision tree with the user. The "When to build vs. skill vs. hook" comparison table makes the triage concrete: skill when LLM-native, hook when one-shot lifecycle event, MCP when deterministic capability returning structured data the LLM cannot reliably do. Step 6 documents the settings.json registration shape across all five CLIs (Claude `~/.claude/settings.json`, Cursor `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, Codex `~/.codex/config.json`, Gemini `~/.gemini/mcp.json`, OpenCode `~/.config/opencode/mcp.json`); the entry shape is identical across all five. Common Rationalizations table covers eight common drift modes including search-as-service wrappers (categorically rejected by policy), MCP-when-skill-suffices, Step-0 skipping, HTTP-by-default, auth deferral, and terse tool descriptions (which under-trigger like skill descriptions do). Cross-links to `developer-experience/tool-design`, `workflow/create-skill-or-command`, `ai-development/ai-agent-development`, `ai-development/claude-agent-sdk`, `architecture/api-design`, `language-specialists/python-expert`, `language-specialists/typescript-expert`.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `references/` (2 files, both referenced from SKILL.md per the A13 audit).** `references/fastmcp.md` covers the deeper FastMCP API surface: install + minimum runtime, minimal server template, tool definitions with Pydantic models, transports (stdio default, HTTP, SSE), HTTP / SSE auth via FastAPI middleware, resources and prompts, four named testing patterns, six common pitfalls, and going-beyond-the-scaffold guidance. `references/ts-sdk.md` covers the same topics for Node / TypeScript with Zod schemas: install, minimal `McpServer` + `StdioServerTransport` template, tool definitions with `server.tool(name, schema, handler)` shape, transports, HTTP auth via Express middleware, resources and prompts, four testing patterns, six common pitfalls (especially ESM/CJS interop and `~` path-expansion bugs), and production-build guidance.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `scripts/` (4 files in two parallel pairs, all referenced from SKILL.md).** `scripts/init-mcp-fastmcp.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`) verifies Python 3.10+, creates `<name>/`, writes `pyproject.toml` with `mcp[cli]>=1.0.0` + `pydantic>=2.0.0` deps, writes `server.py` with one example `@mcp.tool()` decorated `echo` function returning a Pydantic `EchoResult` model, writes `.gitignore`, creates a venv at `.venv/`, installs the deps into the venv, prints next-step instructions including `mcp dev server.py`. `scripts/init-mcp-fastmcp.ps1` is the PowerShell sibling (same output, `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`). `scripts/init-mcp-ts.sh` verifies Node 20+, runs `npm init -y`, installs `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` + `zod` + `tsx` + `typescript` + `@types/node`, writes ESM-native `package.json` with `dev` / `build` / `start` scripts, writes `tsconfig.json` targeting ES2022 / ESNext / Bundler resolution, writes `src/server.ts` with one example `server.tool()` registration using a Zod schema and stdio transport, writes `.gitignore`, runs `npm install`, prints next-step instructions including `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector npm run dev`. `scripts/init-mcp-ts.ps1` is the PowerShell sibling. Each `.sh` and its `.ps1` sibling produce equivalent scaffolds; neither cross-references the other (v1.1.3 four-hook precedent).
    *   **Registry updates.** `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gets two new rows (`brand-styling` in specialized-domains, `mcp-builder` in ai-development); total updated from 192 to 194. `data/skills.json` gets two new entries with full schema (description, long_description, summary_l0, overview_l1, version=1.0.0, category, language, tags, priority=MEDIUM, tools_required, path, file, size, security 100/100/95); `statistics.total_skills` 194 -> 196; `statistics.categories.specialized-domains` 11 -> 12; `statistics.categories.ai-development` 8 -> 9. `data/marketplace.json` category descriptions updated and `skill_count` incremented for both categories.
    *   **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` extended with Phase 6 sections.** Intro paragraph updated to mention Phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, AND 6. Two new bullets under `### Added` -> `New skills (Phase 6)`, plus a `Per-skill bundled references/` block, a `Per-skill bundled scripts/` block, and a new `Registry updates (Phase 6)` block. New `Cross-platform installer parity (Phase 6)` block under `### Verified` documenting the recursive-copy auto-distribution path, the no-vendor-assets verification, the bundle audit clean state, and the syntax validation. `### Tests` section updated with Phase 6 confirmation that no new tests were added (no new dispatcher scripts or hooks - the bundled scaffolders are user-facing initialization tools, not part of the catalog test surface; pre-existing 428 passed remain green). `### Known gaps` paragraph extended with DF-007.
    *   **`docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` updated for Phase 6.** One new open item: DF-007 (Phase 6 mcp-builder bundled scaffolders not exercised end-to-end - static syntax validation clean on all four scripts, but actual scaffold-and-launch cycles against real Python 3.10+ / Node 20+ hosts were not run; the gap rolls up into the cumulative DF-003 / DF-005 / DF-006 cross-OS verification queue scheduled for Phase 7's `/update-version` step). Summary table updated: 10 open items (was 9), 0 resolved this version. Last-updated date stamped 2026-05-08 (Phase 6 complete).

*   **Design Rationale**: Three calls shaped the Phase 6 work. **First**, the brand-styling skill's strongest opinion is that the agent must NOT invent brand decisions on the user's behalf. The pre-Phase-6 state of the world had no such guard - any artifact that needed a "brand-looking" treatment got one with the agent's defaults (typically the AI-slop palette: navy, gray, blue accent). The skill's body explicitly catches the rationalization "the user wants 'professional' colors - I'll just pick navy and gray" and rebuts it with: ASK the user for their brand; OFFER an empty default scaffold if they have none; FAIL LOUDLY if a required brand field is missing. The bundled template's empty placeholders make the contract concrete - the user CANNOT use the skill without filling values. The N1 dropped-outright item from the comparison report (Anthropic's actual brand colors / fonts / logo) drove this design: the skill captures the PATTERN without shipping any vendor assets, satisfying both the company-neutral framing rule (memory `feedback_no_employer_refs.md`) and the AGENTS.md reverse-engineering attribution rule. **Second**, the mcp-builder skill's most-load-bearing section is Step 0 (the policy-decision-tree walk), not the scaffolders themselves. Many requests for "an MCP that does X" are actually requests for "the agent to do X reliably", which is a SKILL not an MCP - the skill catches that case before any infrastructure is built. The "When to build vs. skill vs. hook" comparison table is the operational expression of Step 0. The four scaffolders (FastMCP bash + ps1, TS SDK bash + ps1) are intentionally minimal: each generates a one-tool hello-world `echo` server in under 30 seconds, deferring all production concerns (auth, multi-tool, distribution) to the reference docs. This matches the Phase 4 `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` precedent: the scaffolder's value is "30 seconds and no version-mismatch debugging", not "a complete production server". **Third**, the installer-edit decision was straightforward. The plan's prompt for sub-task 6.2 says "Register the four bundled scripts in BOTH installers per the AGENTS.md installer-aware changes rule." But AGENTS.md "Installer-Aware Changes" makes a clear distinction: per-skill bundled scripts under `catalog/skills/<>/scripts/` are auto-distributed via the recursive-copy logic (the `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` primitives validated in Phase 3 / WN-001), and only repo-level `scripts/<name>.py` artifacts require explicit-name registration. The Phase 4 web-artifacts-builder bundled `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` scripts were NOT registered explicitly - they ride the recursive copy. The Phase 6 mcp-builder scripts follow the same pattern. So no installer edit was made; verification was done via static analysis (bash -n + ShellCheck + PowerShell parse-check) and bundle-audit confirmation that all four scripts are referenced from the parent SKILL.md.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users beyond two new skills appearing in their installed catalog after the next installer run. No schema changes, no `settings.json` changes, no installer behavior changes (the recursive copy already handles bundled subdirs from Phase 3), no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up: (a) two new skill folders under `~/.claude/skills/specialized-domains/brand-styling/` and `~/.claude/skills/ai-development/mcp-builder/` (and the equivalent destinations for Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode) with their `templates/` and `references/` + `scripts/` subdirectories; (b) updated `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in each platform's `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`-rendered instruction file with the two new rows. **Important (carried forward through v1.1.5 phases 3-5)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skills to become callable. **For brand-styling**: users who want to apply their brand should populate `~/.devai-hub/brand/<their-brand-slug>/tokens.json` from the bundled `templates/tokens.template.json` BEFORE asking the agent to "stay on-brand"; the skill explicitly refuses to invent brand values on the user's behalf.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: One new item in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`: DF-007 (Phase 6 mcp-builder bundled scaffolders not exercised end-to-end - static syntax validation only; the recommended fix is a CI matrix step that runs each scaffolder against a clean fixture directory and verifies the generated server starts under `mcp dev` / `npm run dev`). Carried over from earlier phases: DF-001 (`create-skill-or-command` not in catalog), DF-002 (Phase 2 A4 starting-state mismatch), DF-003 (macOS / Linux real-install verification deferred), DF-004 (`--dry-run` flag not added to installers), DF-005 (Phase 4 cross-OS verification gap), DF-006 (Phase 5 cross-OS verification gap), QG-001 (cross-OS verification gate ran on one OS only), WN-001 (4 pre-existing orphan reference files in framework-specialist skills), MT-001 (real-CLI integration test for the optimizer not exercised in CI). Total open: 10. Phase 7 (the OPTIONAL `.skill` packager) starts next; per the plan, it ships only if the user confirms Claude.ai / Anthropic API distribution is a goal.
