## [2026-05-08] - Phase 5 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: skill-eval-loop + description optimizer (A6, A7)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 5 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 5 ships the eval-iteration workflow + browser viewer + description optimizer as a single integrated skill, with a CLI-agnostic adapter following the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent (claude / gemini / codex / opencode parity). Specifically: (a) a new workflow skill `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/` that drives a closed-loop evaluation against any DevAI-Hub skill (paired with-skill / without-skill runs, assertion-graded outputs, browser-reviewed benchmarks, structured feedback capture, five named improvement heuristics); (b) three repo-level dispatcher scripts under `scripts/`: `aggregate_benchmark.py` (post-processes paired runs into `benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md`), `skill_eval_viewer.py` (server + static modes for browser-based eval review with feedback capture), `optimize_skill_description.py` (60/40 train-test split optimizer with held-out-test selection that prevents overfitting); (c) a parametrized pytest at `catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py` enforcing the no-cross-CLI-bleed invariant via source inspection (parametrized over four CLIs x one dispatcher = four parity assertions, plus dry-run schema and aggregator/viewer smoke). Phase 5 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A6.1 - `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/SKILL.md` (~200 lines).** Workflow skill with full DevAI-Hub frontmatter that drives the 10-step iteration loop. Steps 1-2 are one-time setup (capture user intent into `<workspace>/intent.md`; author 2-3 realistic test prompts to `evals/evals.json`). Steps 3-10 are the per-iteration loop: spawn paired `with_skill` / `without_skill` runs in `<workspace>/iteration-N/eval-XXX/{...}/outputs/`; capture `total_tokens` + `duration_ms` per run; grade against assertions via the bundled `agents/grader.md` sub-agent (exact field names `text` / `passed` / `evidence`); aggregate to `benchmark.json` via `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py`; launch `scripts/skill_eval_viewer.py`; collect `feedback.json` from the user's review; apply improvement heuristics from `references/improvement-heuristics.md`; re-run as `iteration-N+1`. Stop conditions documented: pass-rate stable across 2 consecutive iterations, OR explicit user accept, OR pass-rate regresses for 2 consecutive iterations (rolls back). Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14: trigger phrases include "evaluate a skill", "benchmark a skill", "A/B test a skill", "optimize a skill description", "run an eval set", "score a skill against test prompts", "iterate on a skill", "skill regression", "with-skill vs without-skill", "eval harness", "eval workspace", "paired runs", "eval iteration", "make this skill actually work"; `SKIP:` clause covers one-off prompt tests, ad-hoc skill drafting, deterministic-code unit tests, live-traffic A/B, and vendor-specific eval suites. Common Rationalizations table covers eight failure modes (eyeball-only, two-prompts-is-enough, tokens-don't-matter, held-out-test-is-overkill, manual-grading, with-skill-only, parity-test-is-bureaucracy, vibes-stop-condition). Verification checklist is binary and observable. Cross-links to `developer-experience/ai-output-evaluation`, `workflow/create-custom-command` + AGENTS.md, `tests-generation/code-coverage`, `orchestration/multi-agent-coordinator`, `developer-experience/prompt-engineering`, `workflow/known-gaps-tracker`.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `references/` (4 files, all linked from SKILL.md).** `schemas.md` documents the JSON schema for every artifact in the loop (`evals/evals.json`, per-run `run_metadata.json`, per-run `grading.json`, per-iteration `benchmark.json`, per-iteration `feedback.json`, per-optimizer-iteration result). `improvement-heuristics.md` documents the five heuristics applied at step 9 (H1 pushy descriptions, H2 explain-the-why, H3 repeated-work elimination, H4 negative-space coverage, H5 assertion calibration), each with symptom + fix + worked example + validation criterion, and the priority order (H1 -> H4 -> H2 -> H5 -> H3) with the one-heuristic-per-iteration constraint. `cli-adapter.md` documents the option-A-vs-option-B design rationale (option A = four parallel scripts, the v1.1.3 hooks pattern; option B = single dispatcher with `--cli` flag, selected for files of this size since duplication ratio 50:150 lines is too high to justify the deletion-safety affordance), the per-CLI invocation patterns for `claude` / `gemini` / `codex` / `opencode` (skill-loading flag + prompt flag + token-capture pattern per CLI), and the parity-test specification. `description-optimizer.md` documents the 60/40 train-test split rationale (without held-out, the optimizer picks descriptions that memorize train-query phrasing verbatim), the iteration structure (`<workspace>/optimizer/iteration-N.json` + `final.json`), the candidate-generation prompt template, the held-out-test selection rule (`max(pool, key=test_trigger_rate)` with train-rate + length tiebreakers, shorter wins to minimize Tier 1 token cost), and the `--dry-run` mode contract.
    *   **Per-skill bundled `agents/` (3 sub-agent prompt files).** `grader.md` instructs the grader sub-agent to evaluate assertions against a run's `outputs/response.txt` and write `grading.json` with the exact field names `text` / `passed` / `evidence` (the aggregator depends on these). The grader's six rules: read assertion text literally, evidence is mandatory and concrete (line number + quoted span), read response.txt cold without bias from prior turns, do not invent assertions, be conservative on borderline calls, no overall-quality opinions. `comparator.md` instructs the comparator sub-agent to perform a blind A/B comparison: the runner shuffles A/B per eval so the comparator never knows which is `with_skill`; verdict alphabet is exactly `A_better` / `B_better` / `tie`; six rules: read both cold, judge by query relevance not surface polish, use eval tags as context not scoring, cite concrete differences, default to `tie` when ambiguous, calibrate confidence honestly. `analyzer.md` instructs the analyzer sub-agent to read `benchmark.json` (and optionally the per-run `grading.json` files plus the previous iteration's `benchmark.json`) and surface three classes of finding: non-discriminating assertions (same `passed` value across `with_skill` AND `without_skill` for every eval -> recommend H5), high-variance evals (`stddev/mean > 0.3` -> recommend H3), time/token trade-offs (>2x ratio between with_skill and without_skill -> surface for owner decision). The analyzer caps recommendations at 3 per iteration and maps every recommendation to a heuristic in `references/improvement-heuristics.md`. The agent files sit under `agents/` (sibling to `references/`) - intentionally outside the A13 orphan-audit scope (`scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` only) since they are sub-agent prompts, not bundled scripts or assets.
    *   **A6.3 - `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py`.** Stdlib-only Python 3.10+ aggregator that walks `<workspace>/iteration-N/` and emits `benchmark.json` + `benchmark.md` in the same directory. Per-eval metrics: `pass_rate`, `duration_ms_mean`, `duration_ms_stddev`, `tokens_mean`, `tokens_stddev`, plus a `delta` block (`with_skill - without_skill` for each metric). Overall metrics: `with_skill_pass_rate`, `without_skill_pass_rate`, `pass_rate_delta`, `with_skill_duration_ms_mean`, `without_skill_duration_ms_mean`, `with_skill_tokens_mean`, `without_skill_tokens_mean`. Pure post-processing - no CLI invocation. Schema documented at `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/references/schemas.md`. `--output-dir` lets the user redirect output for non-destructive runs.
    *   **A6.3 - `scripts/skill_eval_viewer.py`.** Stdlib-only Python 3.10+ browser viewer with two modes. Server mode (default) starts an `http.server` on a random port, opens the user's browser via `webbrowser.open()` (suppressible via `--no-open`), and accepts `POST /submit-feedback` that writes `<iteration_dir>/feedback.json`. Static mode (`--static <path>`) writes a self-contained HTML file whose "Submit All Reviews" button downloads `feedback.json` as a JS Blob - designed for headless / CI environments. Two-tab UI: "Outputs" (per-eval, `with_skill` vs `without_skill` side-by-side, with assertion-grading badges color-coded green/red, run-metadata badges showing duration / tokens / cli, free-form feedback textareas + a 3-option verdict selector per eval) and "Benchmark" (the `benchmark.json` table). Templating done with `str.format` - no jinja dependency.
    *   **A7 - `scripts/optimize_skill_description.py`.** Description optimizer with deterministic 60/40 train-test split (`--seed` default 42; `--train-fraction` configurable). For each iteration: `estimate_trigger_rate()` runs each train query `--repeats` times (default 3) under the current description and computes the per-query trigger rate; `generate_candidates()` asks the chosen CLI to PROPOSE 3 candidate description rewrites via the prompt template at `references/description-optimizer.md`; each candidate is evaluated on train AND test; `select_best()` picks the candidate with the highest `test_trigger_rate`, ties broken by `train_trigger_rate` then by description length (shorter wins per the AGENTS.md three-tier loading model where Tier 1 fields cost tokens on every catalog read). The optimizer terminates when `--max-iterations` (default 5) is reached, OR two consecutive iterations show no improvement in `test_trigger_rate` (early-stop), OR `test_trigger_rate` reaches 1.0. The `--dry-run` mode prints the train/test split, the baseline description, and the candidate-generation prompt template, then exits 0 without invoking any CLI - the pytest at `test_eval_loop.py::TestOptimizerDryRun` verifies this contract under three sub-cases (schema, determinism under fixed seed, no-CLI-invocation under empty PATH). CLI dispatch follows the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent: `assert cli in {"claude", "gemini", "codex", "opencode"}` near the top of `invoke_cli()`, four parallel `if cli == "X":` branches, no cross-CLI fallback. The parity invariant is enforced by `test_eval_loop.py::TestEvalLoopCLIAdapter`.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/tests/test_eval_loop.py` (14 tests, all green).** Three test classes: (1) `TestEvalLoopCLIAdapter` - parametrized over (`optimize_skill_description.py`, each of the four supported CLIs) plus `test_dispatcher_has_assertion_against_unsupported_cli` and `test_dispatcher_has_branch_for_each_cli`; the source-inspection technique mirrors `test_diff_review_hooks.py::TestPlatformIndependence` (find the `if cli == "X":` line, walk forward collecting lines whose indent is strictly greater than the header's indent, stop at the next sibling line, then assert no other CLI binary appears in argv-list form within the collected body). (2) `TestOptimizerDryRun` - asserts `--dry-run` returns 0 with the declared schema (`mode` / `cli` / `selection_metric` / `n_train` / `n_test` / `split` / `baseline_description` / `candidate_generation_prompt_template_preview`), the split is deterministic for the same `--seed`, and the optimizer does NOT invoke any CLI when run with `PATH` pointing at an empty directory (the strongest evidence of dry-run isolation). (3) `TestAggregator` and `TestViewerStaticMode` - build a fixture iteration directory with one eval, paired runs, and `grading.json`, run the aggregator, assert `benchmark.json` has `with_skill_pass_rate=1.0` / `without_skill_pass_rate=0.0` / `pass_rate_delta=1.0`, then run the viewer with `--static review.html` and assert the HTML body contains the eval id, both run-condition labels, and the `submitFeedback` JS function name (proves the viewer renders the static-mode submit handler).
    *   **Both installers updated in lockstep.** `scripts/installer.sh` gains a Phase-5 `safe_copy` block (line ~1424) that registers `aggregate_benchmark.py` + `skill_eval_viewer.py` + `optimize_skill_description.py` to `~/.devai-hub/scripts/`, modeled after the existing `generate_report.py` / `devai_mcp_benchmark.py` blocks. `scripts/installer.ps1` gains the matching PowerShell `Safe-Copy` block (line ~1735) using `Join-Path $RepoRoot "scripts\<name>.py"` and `Join-Path $scriptsDest "<name>.py"`. Both blocks include the same comment header explaining why these are repo-level scripts that need explicit registration (vs the per-skill bundled scripts under `catalog/skills/.../scripts/` which are auto-distributed by the recursive copy).
    *   **Registry updates.** `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gets one new `skill-eval-loop` row in the workflow category; total 191 -> 192. `data/skills.json` gets one new entry (full schema, version=1.0.0, category=workflow, language=Python, tags=[skill-evaluation, ab-testing, benchmark, eval-harness, paired-runs, iteration-loop, description-optimizer, cli-agnostic, held-out-test], priority=MEDIUM, tools_required=[Read, Write, Edit, Bash], status=production, security 100/100/95); `statistics.total_skills` 193 -> 194; `statistics.categories.workflow` 18 -> 19. `data/marketplace.json` workflow category description updated to mention "skill evaluation"; `skill_count` 19 -> 20.
    *   **`.gitignore` updated.** New `*-workspace/` entry to ignore user-generated eval workspaces. The loop creates `<skill-name>-workspace/` directories at the repo root with per-iteration outputs, benchmarks, and feedback that should not leak into commits.

*   **Design Rationale**: The first key call was **option A vs option B for the CLI adapter**. Option A (four parallel scripts) is the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent applied verbatim. Option B (single dispatcher with `--cli` flag) was selected because the eval-loop dispatchers are 250-400 lines each; replicating ~150 lines of workspace-layout / JSON-I/O / paired-run plumbing across four scripts produces 600 lines of duplication for ~50 lines of CLI-specific logic per script. The v1.1.3 hooks were 80 lines each, so duplication was acceptable; it is not at this size. Option B preserves the parity invariant via a 50-line pytest module that source-inspects each `if cli == "X":` branch, which is a much lower maintenance cost than four parallel files. The second call was **whether to make the orphan-bundle audit fail-closed on `agents/`**. The validator's `BUNDLED_SUBDIRS` constant covers `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` only; sub-agent prompt files live under `agents/`, which is outside the audit scope. The plan prompt for sub-task 5.5 specifies `catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/agents/`, and the AGENTS.md "Per-skill Bundled Resources" section says `MAY (not MUST) contain three subdirectories` and explicitly does not forbid other names. So `agents/` is auto-distributed by the recursive `safe_folder_copy` like every other subdirectory in the skill folder, but is not subject to the orphan audit. The third call was **selection metric for the optimizer**. The plan called for `best_description` selection by held-out test score; the alternative was train score plus regularization. Held-out test was selected because the candidate-generation prompt SEES the train queries (via the "queries that the description CURRENTLY MISHANDLES" block) and would therefore tune candidates to those specific phrasings; the held-out test set is the only signal that measures generalization. Tie-breakers added: train-rate (more general descriptions among equally-effective candidates) and description length (shorter wins, since description is Tier 1 metadata loaded on every catalog read). Length-as-tiebreaker is what the AGENTS.md three-tier loading model rationalizes - 50 saved tokens times the number of catalog reads per session adds up.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users beyond the new skill appearing in their installed catalog and three new repo-level scripts being available at `~/.devai-hub/scripts/{aggregate_benchmark,skill_eval_viewer,optimize_skill_description}.py` after the next installer run. No schema changes, no `settings.json` changes, no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up: (a) one new skill folder at `~/.claude/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop/` (and the equivalent destinations for Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode) with the full `references/` + `agents/` subdirectories; (b) three new scripts under `~/.devai-hub/scripts/`; (c) updated `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in each platform's `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`-rendered instruction file with the new row. **Important (carried from v1.1.4 / v1.1.5 Phases 3-4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skill to become callable.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: Two new items in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`: DF-006 (Phase 5 cross-OS installer dry-run deferred - extends DF-003 / DF-005 with the Phase-5-specific context that the three new scripts need real `bash scripts/installer.sh` execution on a real macOS / Linux host before the v1.1.5 -> v1.2.0 version bump) and MT-001 (the optimizer's `run_iteration()` function lacks a "stub CLI binary on PATH" smoke test analogous to the v1.1.3 hooks - covered indirectly via the parity test + dry-run schema test, but a direct integration test would be stronger; out of scope for v1.1.5 if Phase 7 ships first). Carried over from earlier phases: DF-001, DF-002, DF-003, DF-004, DF-005, QG-001, WN-001. Total open: 9. Phase 6 starts next; it ships `brand-styling` (specialized-domains, token-pattern only - no vendor assets) and `mcp-builder` (ai-development, FastMCP + TS SDK runbook with bundled scaffolding scripts). Both Phase 6 skills will exercise the same `safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` recursive-copy primitives this Phase 5 work confirmed clean.

*   **Test Posture**: All four test suites green. `python -c "json.load(...)"` passes for `data/skills.json` (194 skills, +1 from Phase 4 close), `data/bundles.json`, `data/marketplace.json`, `data/workflows.json`, `data/templates.json`. `python -m pytest catalog/hooks/tests/` results: **332 passed, 0 failures** (+14 new from `test_eval_loop.py` on top of the +8 from Phase 3 / `test_skill_bundles.py`). Across all four test suites: `extensions/devai-skill-server` 37 passed; `extensions/devai-code-search` 36 passed, 1 skipped; `extensions/devai-web-fetch` 23 passed; `catalog/hooks/tests` 332 passed. Total **428 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures**. `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` against the 198-skill catalog: **0 errors, 4 warnings** (carried from WN-001; no new orphans introduced). Per-skill independent validation: `python scripts/validate_skills.py --path catalog/skills/workflow/skill-eval-loop` returns PASS with 0 errors and 5 warnings of optional-field kind. `python -m py_compile scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py scripts/skill_eval_viewer.py scripts/optimize_skill_description.py` clean. `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` clean. PowerShell parser-check on `scripts/installer.ps1` clean. ShellCheck (`--severity=warning`) clean against `scripts/installer.sh` and `install.sh`.

## [2026-05-08] - Phase 4 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: net-new content skills batch 1 (A1, A3, A8, A10)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 4 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 4 ships four net-new content skills that all consume the Phase 3 bundled-resources layout convention. Item A1 ships `generative-art` (specialized-domains) - a p5.js-based generative-art skill with three starter templates under `assets/`. Item A3 ships `theme-tokens` (specialized-domains) - ten brand-neutral curated theme JSON files under `themes/` plus a stable token schema consumed by `pptx-generation`, `docx-generation`, `pdf-document-generation`, `web-artifacts-builder`, and `generative-art`. Item A8 ships `internal-comms` (business-product) - six structured templates (3P Update, Weekly Status, Leadership Update, Company FAQ entry, Incident Report, Project Update) with worked examples under `examples/` using placeholder organizations (Project Aurora, Team Phoenix, Apex Logistics). Item A10 ships `web-artifacts-builder` (developer-experience) - a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui scaffolder with cross-platform `init-artifact.sh` + `init-artifact.ps1` siblings under `scripts/` (the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent). Phase 4 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A1 - `catalog/skills/specialized-domains/generative-art/SKILL.md` (130 lines) plus three starter templates under `assets/`.** The body documents a strict two-step workflow: Step 1 writes a 30-80 line Markdown philosophy manifesto fixing six required sections (Movement reference, Underlying principle, Color and density behavior, Motion behavior, Parameter surface, "What this is NOT" negative-space declaration); Step 2 ships a p5.js sketch (`<piece>.js`) plus an HTML viewer (`<piece>.html`) that exposes every manifesto-declared parameter as a native `<input type="range">` slider, with `randomSeed()` + `noiseSeed()` called in `setup()` before any random / noise call so the same seed produces a render-identical image. Templates: `assets/flow-field.html` (curl-noise traced particles, 88 lines), `assets/particle-system.html` (force-directed swarm with mouse target, 95 lines), `assets/l-system.html` (recursive grammar with seeded jitter, 85 lines). Each template is self-contained (single HTML file with embedded p5 + sliders + sketch, p5 from CDN, no build step). Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14: verbatim trigger phrases (generative art, p5.js, flow field, particle system, L-system, generative wallpaper, parametric sketch, code-driven art) plus an explicit `SKIP:` clause for data dashboards / static posters / 3D shaders / fixed-output visuals. Common Rationalizations table rebuts the six most likely shortcuts (skipping the philosophy step, accepting the perlin-noise default, skipping seeded randomness, skipping sliders, adding a UI library, improvising parameters). Cross-links to `creative-generation`, `glsl-shader-development`, `brand-styling`, `ui-component-generation`, `gif-sticker-maker`.
    *   **A3 - `catalog/skills/specialized-domains/theme-tokens/SKILL.md` (175 lines) plus ten theme JSON files under `themes/`.** The body documents the token schema (palette: 6 slots `primary`/`secondary`/`accent`/`background`/`foreground`/`muted`; fonts: 3 slots `heading`/`body`/`mono`; `spacing.base` + `spacing.scale`; single `radius`; single `shadow` value or `"none"`) and explains the rationale for each choice (six is the slot cap, three is the font cap, base+scale beats hardcoded px, slot expansion breaks every downstream generator simultaneously). Maps the schema onto each downstream consumer (`pptx-generation`, `docx-generation`, `pdf-document-generation`, `web-artifacts-builder`, `generative-art`). Documents the bundled-set-is-closed rule: user-supplied themes route through `brand-styling` instead of extending this skill's `themes/`. Ten themes shipped: `editorial-serif.json` (long-form magazine, EB Garamond), `brutalist-sans.json` (Space Grotesk, radius 0, no shadow, accent #ff3b00), `pastel-soft.json` (low-contrast, generous radius 12, soft shadow), `terminal-mono.json` (all-mono triple on dark background with cyan accent #3ad7c8), `corporate-slate.json` (cool grays, navy primary #1f3559), `sunset-warm.json` (terracotta + amber + cream, Cormorant Garamond), `forest-cool.json` (deep green + sage + parchment, Lora), `mid-century-modern.json` (mustard + teal + cream, Work Sans / Futura), `neon-cyber.json` (neon magenta + electric cyan on near-black, mono body, glow shadow), `newsprint-mono.json` (cream + ink-black, Playfair Display, no accent). *   **Design Rationale**: The first key call was **whether the four new skills should adopt the standard `BUNDLED_SUBDIRS` names from AGENTS.md (`scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`) or the names called out in the plan prompt (`templates/` for generative-art, `themes/` for theme-tokens, `examples/` for internal-comms, `scripts/` for web-artifacts-builder)**. AGENTS.md "Per-skill Bundled Resources" says `MAY (not MUST) contain three subdirectories` and explicitly does not forbid other names; the orphan-validator's `BUNDLED_SUBDIRS` constant only validates the three standard names. Three options: (a) rename all four skills' bundled directories to the standard `assets/` (which would put `assets/themes/*.json` for theme-tokens, `assets/examples/*.md` for internal-comms - more nesting); (b) keep the plan's named directories (`themes/`, `examples/`, `scripts/`) and accept that `themes/` and `examples/` won't be orphan-validated; (c) update `BUNDLED_SUBDIRS` to include `themes/`, `examples/`, `templates/` so they're validated too. Picked (b) because it matches the plan prompt verbatim, the installer's `safe_folder_copy` is recursive (every subdirectory is copied regardless of name), and adding more names to the validator's whitelist crosses Phase 3's locked scope. The second call was **whether to register the per-skill `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` scripts in `scripts/installer.sh` and `scripts/installer.ps1` explicitly**. The AGENTS.md installer-aware-changes table says repo-level `scripts/<name>.py` requires explicit registration but per-skill bundled scripts under `catalog/skills/<>/scripts/` are auto-distributed via the recursive copy. The plan prompt for A10 confirms this: "Register both scripts in BOTH installers per the AGENTS.md installer-aware changes rule (this is a per-skill bundled script under the new A13 convention - the installer's recursive copy from 3.2/3.3 handles it; verify the dry-run lands `init-artifact.{sh,ps1}` at the right path)." So the registration is the recursive copy itself, not an explicit-name copy line. No installer edit was made; verification was done by file-system inspection (the four new skill folders all sit under `catalog/skills/` which is already part of `safe_folder_copy`'s scope) and by the bash/PowerShell parse checks. The third call was **how to handle the 6 pre-existing strict-validator errors and 4 pre-existing orphan warnings surfaced by `python scripts/validate_skills.py`**. Phase 3 already wrote `make validate` to invoke `--bundles-only` mode (which the four Phase 4 skills pass cleanly with 0 errors), and the 6 strict-mode errors are all in unrelated skills (`user-documentation`, `cd-pipeline-generator`, `rollback-strategy-advisor`) that pre-date the Phase 4 work. None of these were introduced by Phase 4; they remain logged under the existing WN-001 / strict-mode-noise debt and are out of Phase 4 scope.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users beyond the four new skills appearing in their installed catalog after the next installer run. No schema changes, no `settings.json` changes, no installer behavior changes (the recursive copy already handles bundled subdirs from Phase 3), no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up: (a) four new skill folders under `~/.claude/skills/specialized-domains/generative-art/`, `~/.claude/skills/specialized-domains/theme-tokens/`, `~/.claude/skills/business-product/internal-comms/`, `~/.claude/skills/developer-experience/web-artifacts-builder/` (and the equivalent destinations for Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode); (b) updated `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in each platform's `templates/ai-instructions/base-*.md`-rendered instruction file with the four new rows. **Important (carried from v1.1.4 / v1.1.5 Phase 3)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skills to become callable.

## [2026-05-08] - Phase 3 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: per-skill bundled-resources layout convention (A13)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 3 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 3 is the foundational tier of the plan - it formalizes the per-skill `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` layout convention (item A13 from the comparison report's Section 5), updates AGENTS.md to document it, confirms both installers' existing recursive-copy primitives auto-distribute the new subdirs, extends `make validate` with an orphan-bundle audit, and ships a sentinel `.gitkeep` proving the round-trip. Every later phase (4 through 7) consumes this convention to ship per-skill bundled scripts and reference docs without inflating the SKILL.md body. Phase 3 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump itself remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A13.1 - AGENTS.md "Per-skill Bundled Resources" subsection added.** New `#### Per-skill Bundled Resources` block placed right after the SKILL.md size norm and before "### 4. Register the skill". Documents the optional `scripts/` (executable code, tier-3 deterministic operations), `references/` (Markdown docs the agent reads on demand), `assets/` (templates / icons / fonts / fixtures) subdirectories that any skill folder MAY contain. Documents file naming (kebab-case, scoped by topic), the cross-shell parity rule (every `.sh` script MUST ship a `.ps1` sibling so Windows users get the same capability), the reference rule (every bundled file MUST be referenced from SKILL.md or another reference file in the same bundle, except `.gitkeep`), the installer behavior (`safe_folder_copy` / `Safe-Folder-Copy` already preserve subdirs via `rsync -a` / `cp -R` / `robocopy /MIR`; no installer edit needed for skill-bundled content), and the orphan-bundle audit. Updated the forward-reference in the Three-Tier Loading Model block from "the Per-skill Bundled Resources section that gets added in Phase 3" to "the Per-skill Bundled Resources subsection further down" since the section now exists. Cross-links from the A13 section to the size norm (when to push body content into `references/`), to the v1.1.3 four-hook precedent (per-CLI parity invariants for `scripts/` directories that ship per-CLI variants), and to the Distribution channels table (the auto-distribution path the new subdirs use).
    *   **A13.2 / A13.3 - Both installers gain a clarifying block comment above the recursive-copy function.** `scripts/installer.sh::safe_folder_copy` (around line 128) gains a 6-line comment explaining that the existing `rsync -a --delete` / `cp -R` primitives already preserve per-skill bundled subdirectories, with a cross-reference to the AGENTS.md convention. `scripts/installer.ps1::Safe-Folder-Copy` (around line 298) gains the same 8-line comment in lockstep, documenting the `robocopy /MIR` parity. **No code change in either function body** - the Phase 3 audit confirmed the recursive-copy primitives already handle the new convention correctly. The plan's sub-task 3.3 also suggested adding a `--dry-run` flag to both installers if missing; this was assessed out of scope (logged as DF-004) because adding a real dry-run mode to two ~1700-line installers is a substantive feature, not a sub-task tweak, and the smoke test verification can be performed by direct invocation of the recursive-copy primitives instead.
    *   **A13.4 - `scripts/validate_skills.py` orphan-bundle audit + `make validate` wiring.** New `validate_skill_bundles(skill_dir, skill_md_content)` function in `scripts/validate_skills.py`: walks a skill directory, lists every file under `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/` (recursive), builds a haystack from the parent SKILL.md plus every `references/*.md`, and emits a warning for each bundled file whose basename does not appear in the haystack. The exempt-filename set is `{".gitkeep"}` (placeholder for future-expansion subdirs). Warnings, not errors - work-in-progress branches can carry orphans without failing CI. New `--bundles-only` CLI flag scopes the validator to this audit only, skipping the full-strict-validator's frontmatter and secret-scan passes (which currently produces 6 false-positive secret detections in code-example blocks of three pre-existing skills - those were never gating CI and are out of Phase 3's scope). The Makefile's `validate` target now runs `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` after the JSON catalog loads.
    *   **A13.4 (cont.) - 8-test pytest module `catalog/hooks/tests/test_skill_bundles.py`.** Covers: (1) orphan in `scripts/` is warned; (2) referenced file is silent; (3) `.gitkeep` is exempt; (4) reference-from-another-reference-file satisfies the audit (a top-level `references/index.md` can act as a TOC for sub-resources); (5) mix of orphan and referenced reports only the orphan; (6) orphan in nested `assets/<subdir>/` is detected; (7) skills with no bundled subdirs return an empty list; (8) `python scripts/validate_skills.py --bundles-only` exits clean against the real 193-skill catalog (subprocess test). Follows the importlib-based loader pattern from `test_format_bash_description.py` because `validate_skills.py` is a top-level script (no package).
    *   **A13.5 - Sentinel `catalog/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/scripts/.gitkeep`.** Empty placeholder that proves the per-skill bundled-resources convention survives a real installer copy. Round-trip-tested on Windows via two copy mechanisms: `cp -R catalog/skills <tmp>` (Git Bash, exercises the same `cp -R` fallback `installer.sh` runs on Linux/macOS) preserved the file at `<tmp>/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/scripts/.gitkeep`; `robocopy catalog\skills <tmp> /MIR` (PowerShell, exercises the exact primitive `installer.ps1::Safe-Folder-Copy` invokes) preserved the same path. The doc-coauthoring SKILL.md gained a brief "Bundled Resources" trailer noting the directory's role; this also satisfies the orphan-audit reference rule for the skill.
    *   **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` extended with Phase 3 sections.** Intro paragraph updated to mention Phases 1, 2, AND 3 explicitly. New `### Changed` bullets cover the AGENTS.md A13 subsection, both installer comment blocks, and the Makefile validate target wiring. New `### Added` bullets cover the orphan-bundle audit, the 8-test pytest module, and the sentinel `.gitkeep`. New `### Verified` bullets cover the Windows + Git Bash smoke (cp -R primitive) and the Windows + PowerShell smoke (robocopy /MIR primitive). The `### Tests` section updates the catalog/hooks/tests count from 310 to 318 (+8 new tests) and totals from 406 to 414. The `### Known gaps` section adds DF-004 (--dry-run not added) and WN-001 (4 pre-existing orphan reference files in framework-specialist skills surfaced by the new audit).
    *   **`docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` updated for Phase 3.** Two new open items: DF-004 (`--dry-run` flag NOT added to either installer - intentionally deferred for scope; the smoke test was performed by direct primitive invocation instead) and WN-001 (4 pre-existing orphan files in `fastapi-expert`, `nextjs-expert`, and `react-expert` `references/` subdirs). DF-003's "Suggested next step" updated to remove the obsolete reference to Phase 3 adding dry-run capability. Summary table updated: 6 open items (was 4), 0 resolved this version. Last-updated date stamped 2026-05-08 (Phase 3 complete).

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **whether to add a real `--dry-run` flag to both installers as the plan's sub-task 3.3 suggested**. The conditional clause in the plan said "if `--dry-run` does not exist, add it as a no-op flag that prints what would be copied without touching the filesystem". Three options: (1) add a real, fully-functional dry-run mode that gates every filesystem write in both installers behind a flag check (substantive feature, several-hundred-line refactor across two ~1700-line files); (2) add a stub `--dry-run` flag that doesn't actually skip writes, just prints a banner (misleading - the flag would not behave the way users expect); (3) skip the dry-run flag entirely and verify the smoke test by direct invocation of the underlying recursive-copy primitives (cp -R, robocopy /MIR) on a temp directory. Picked (3) because it gives the same verification confidence (the actual primitive the installer would run is exercised) without taking on a feature-sized refactor in a phase whose actual goal is the per-skill layout convention, not installer architecture. Documented the decision in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` as DF-004 with a clear handoff note: any future plan that wants real dry-run capability should treat it as a coordinated multi-line refactor across both installers, not as a sub-task tweak. The second key call was **whether to wire the new validator into `make validate` strictly or via a narrow flag**. The existing `validate_skills.py` (which had been authored at some earlier point but was never wired into the Makefile) failed strict-validator mode against the current catalog with 6 false-positive secret detections - generic `password = ...` / `secret = ...` / `token = ...` patterns appearing inside code-example blocks of `user-documentation`, `cd-pipeline-generator`, and `rollback-strategy-advisor`. Wiring the strict validator wholesale would have broken `make validate` immediately. Three options: (a) fix the false positives now (out of scope - those are existing skills with code examples that legitimately use those words); (b) tune the secret-detection regex to skip code blocks (small refactor, but changes detection behavior in ways that may need its own audit); (c) add a `--bundles-only` flag that scopes the validator to the new orphan audit only, leaving the strict full-validator available for manual deep audits but not gating CI. Picked (c) because it gives the new orphan-detection capability requested by the plan without inheriting the 6 pre-existing false positives, AND it preserves the strict validator as a callable tool for anyone who wants to run the deeper audit manually. The third call was **how to handle the 4 pre-existing orphan reference files surfaced by the new audit**. Three framework-specialist skills (`fastapi-expert`, `nextjs-expert`, `react-expert`) ship a `references/` subdirectory with files that are not referenced from their parent SKILL.md. Three options: (1) fix them in this phase (small per-skill body edits adding a `## References` section); (2) delete the orphan files (might be genuinely abandoned, might be deliberate offload); (3) document them as a known gap and let a future patch decide per skill. Picked (3) because the audit is explicitly in scope for Phase 3 but the per-skill body edits are out of scope (Phase 3 ships the layout convention, not skill-body normalization), and the warnings do not gate CI. Logged as WN-001 with a recommended fix.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users. No schema changes, no settings.json changes, no installer behavior changes, no `data/` registry changes, no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up the documentation update in `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, the AGENTS.md mirror locations for Gemini / Codex, and the new sentinel `~/.claude/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/scripts/.gitkeep` (and platform mirrors). The new `make validate` orphan-bundle audit is a developer-facing change, not a user-facing one. **For DevAI-Hub maintainers and skill authors**: any new skill MAY now ship `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` subdirectories alongside `SKILL.md`, and `make validate` will warn on any bundled file not referenced from SKILL.md or another reference file. The strict full validator (`python scripts/validate_skills.py` with no flag) remains available as a manual deep-audit tool but is not part of the default validate target. **Important (carried from v1.1.4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the AGENTS.md update to take effect.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: Two new items in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`: DF-004 (`--dry-run` flag not added to either installer - documented above) and WN-001 (4 pre-existing orphan reference files in framework-specialist skills - recommended fix is a brief `## References` block in each affected SKILL.md, scheduled for a future patch). Carried over from earlier phases: DF-001 (missing `create-skill-or-command` skill referenced by Phase 1's plan prompt), DF-002 (Phase 2 A4 starting-state mismatch), DF-003 (macOS / Linux real-install verification deferred), QG-001 (cross-OS verification gate ran on one OS only). Total open: 6. Phase 4 starts next; it will ship four net-new content skills (`generative-art`, `theme-tokens`, `internal-comms`, `web-artifacts-builder`) that consume the Phase 3 layout convention by bundling templates, themes, examples, and per-skill scripts under the new subdirectory pattern.

*   **Test Posture**: All four test suites green and JSON catalogs valid. `python -c "json.load(...)"` passes for `data/skills.json` (189 skills, +1 from v1.1.5 baseline of 188), `data/bundles.json` (11 bundles), `data/workflows.json` (17 workflows), `data/templates.json`. ShellCheck (`--severity=warning`) clean against `scripts/installer.sh` and `install.sh`. `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` syntax check clean. `python -m pytest catalog/hooks/tests/` results: 318 passed (was 310; +8 from `test_skill_bundles.py`). Across all four test suites: `extensions/devai-skill-server` 37 passed; `extensions/devai-code-search` 36 passed, 1 skipped; `extensions/devai-web-fetch` 23 passed; `catalog/hooks/tests` 318 passed. Total 414 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures. New `make validate` pass: per-skill bundled-resources orphan audit (193 skills scanned, 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings logged in WN-001).

*   **Current Status**: Phase 3 complete and ready for commit. Modified files: `AGENTS.md` (new "Per-skill Bundled Resources" subsection + cross-link fix), `scripts/installer.sh` (block comment), `scripts/installer.ps1` (block comment, lockstep), `scripts/validate_skills.py` (new function + --bundles-only flag), `Makefile` (validate target wiring), `catalog/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/SKILL.md` (Bundled Resources trailer), `CHANGELOG.md` (Phase 3 sections appended), `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` (DF-004 and WN-001 added; DF-003 suggested-next-step updated), `docs/DEVLOG.md` (this entry). ## [2026-05-08] - Phase 2 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: P0 cleanup + doc-coauthoring skill (A4, A9)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 2 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 2 has two scope items: (A4) resolve the `claude-api` skill index drift identified in the comparison report ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/comparison-skills.md](v1.1.5/comparison-skills.md) Section 5a), and (A9) ship a new `doc-coauthoring` workflow skill that wraps the 3-stage co-authoring pattern (Context Gathering -> Refinement and Structure -> Reader Testing). Phase 2 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump itself remains deferred to after Phase 7 per the user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A4 - claude-api index drift verified clean (no code change needed).** The plan's sub-task 2.1 described the starting state as `claude-api` row present across `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, and `data/marketplace.json` while the file `catalog/skills/ai-development/claude-api/SKILL.md` did not exist - and asked the agent to choose between four options (A restore from upstream, B restore from prior history, C de-list, D user-supplied content). At Phase 2 start, the actual state was already consistent: `grep claude-api data/` returned zero matches across all three registry files, and the skill file itself did not exist. The de-list path (option C in the plan's question) had effectively been executed at some earlier point between the comparison report and Phase 2. So sub-task 2.1 was a no-op verification rather than an edit, and the four-option question in the plan was not surfaced. Logged in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` as DF-002 with full context and the suggested next step (if a future plan wants to actually adopt the upstream `claude-api` skill, treat it as a fresh net-new skill addition - not in scope for v1.1.5).
    *   **A9 - `catalog/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/SKILL.md` shipped.** New 114-line workflow skill that drives a 3-stage co-authoring workflow for any non-trivial written artifact (specs, proposals, decision docs, RFCs, ADRs, technical memos, long-form internal writeups). Stage 1 - Context Gathering surfaces audience, purpose, prior art, and constraints in a single batched turn before any prose is written. Stage 2 - Refinement and Structure produces an outline first, then a draft against the accepted outline, with explicit checkpoints to detect drift from the Stage 1 Purpose. Stage 3 - Reader Testing simulates a fresh reader who has not seen the conversation, surfaces a gap list (unbacked claims / missing antecedents / lost-thread transitions) the user resolves or accepts. Frontmatter follows the v1.1.5 pushy-description rule from A14 (lists trigger phrases including "co-author", "co-write", "draft a proposal", "write a spec", "write an RFC", and an explicit `SKIP:` clause for simple READMEs / one-line commit messages / quick inline questions). Common Rationalizations table covers the six most common reasons agents skip stages, with the heaviest weight on Stage 1 inference (the single most common cause of a Stage 2 draft that gets thrown away). Verification section is binary and observable. Cross-links to `business-product/technical-writer`, `developer-experience/writing-editing`, `documentation/technical-documentation`, `business-product/internal-comms`, `developer-experience/idea-refine`, and `developer-experience/spec-driven-development`.
    *   **Registry updates for doc-coauthoring.** `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` gets a new workflow row (total updated 186 -> 187). `data/skills.json` gets a new entry following the full schema (name, title, description, long_description, summary_l0, overview_l1, version=1.0.0, author, category=workflow, language=Multi-language, tags, priority=MEDIUM, based_on, tools_required, path, file, size {lines: 114, tokens_estimate: 2200}, downloads=0, status=production, security 100/100/95); `statistics.total_skills` incremented (188 -> 189), `statistics.categories.workflow` incremented (17 -> 18), `statistics.priorities.MEDIUM` incremented, `total_lines` and `total_tokens_estimate` adjusted. `data/marketplace.json` workflow category `skill_count` incremented (18 -> 19).
    *   **Cross-platform installer parity verified without an installer edit.** Both installers' recursive-copy primitives auto-distribute new skill files: `scripts/installer.sh::safe_folder_copy` uses `rsync -a --delete` (or `cp -R` fallback) on `catalog/skills/`; `scripts/installer.ps1::Safe-Folder-Copy` uses `robocopy ... /MIR`. All 5 platform templates (`templates/ai-instructions/base-{claude,cursor,codex,gemini,opencode}.md` and `generic-instructions.md`) use a `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` placeholder substituted from `data/SKILL_INDEX.md` at install time, so the new index row reaches all 5 supported IDEs in a single edit. No installer edit required - the existing recursive-copy logic already covers Phase 2's surface.
    *   **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` extended.** Added Phase 2's `### Added` (doc-coauthoring skill + registry updates), `### Removed` (claude-api index drift resolution), `### Verified` (cross-platform installer parity), and updated `### Tests` and `### Known gaps` sections. The intro paragraph now mentions Phases 1 AND 2 explicitly and re-states the version-bump-deferred-to-Phase-7 constraint.

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **how to handle the A4 starting-state mismatch**. The plan's prompt asked the agent to surface a four-option question to the user (restore from upstream / restore from history / de-list / user-supplied content). Three options for handling the mismatch: (1) skip the question entirely (de-list state already exists; nothing to ask); (2) ask the user a different question - "the row is already absent; do you want to restore it now from upstream?" - and stall on input; (3) document the actual state, treat sub-task 2.1 as a no-op verification, log the deviation in known-gaps with a clear handoff note for any future plan that wants to actually adopt `claude-api`. Picked (3) because the plan's intent (resolve the index drift) is satisfied by the consistent-de-listed state and (2) would have stalled an auto-mode session on a question the repo state already answers. The trade-off: a future plan that wants the `claude-api` skill content has to start from scratch rather than from a partial restoration, and the plan's option-A path (upstream restore + de-vendor + DevAI-Hub frontmatter) is documented in DF-002 so it doesn't have to be re-discovered. The second key call was **how pushy to make the doc-coauthoring description**. The A14 / Phase 1 rule says to lead with the action then the trigger surface, list trigger phrases verbatim, and add an explicit `SKIP:` clause. Two failure modes to avoid: (a) under-trigger - the description is so short or generic that the agent skips a clearly-relevant request; (b) over-trigger - the description is so broad that the agent invokes the workflow on every doc-adjacent request, including the simple ones the workflow is overkill for. The shipped description threads both: trigger phrases include "co-author", "co-write", "draft a proposal", "write a spec / RFC / ADR / proposal / design doc", "internal memo", AND the SKIP clause explicitly fences off simple READMEs, single-paragraph commit messages, one-line code comments, and quick inline questions that resolve in one turn. The description is 6x longer than a "clean" one-sentence framing - that is the deliberate cost of the pushy-description rule, paid back the first time the agent would have skipped a relevant invocation. The third call was **whether to ship a `references/` subdirectory now (anticipating the A13 layout convention from Phase 3)**. Phase 3 formalizes per-skill `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` subdirs and updates both installers + `make validate` to handle them. Two options: (a) ship doc-coauthoring as SKILL.md only and add references later; (b) pre-empt Phase 3 by including a `references/` subdir now. Picked (a) because Phase 3 also adds `make validate` orphan-bundle detection that flags subdirs not referenced from SKILL.md - shipping references/ now without the validator could mask a future regression. The 114-line SKILL.md fits well within the new 500-line target from A15 and does not need an offload to references yet; the body is self-contained.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE. No schema changes, no settings.json changes, no installer behavior changes, no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up the new `doc-coauthoring/SKILL.md` under `~/.claude/skills/workflow/` (and the `skills/` mirror locations for Gemini / Codex). Cursor / OpenCode / Copilot pick up the new skill via the `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block in their respective instruction-file rendering paths - they get the index-level metadata only, which is the existing platform-coverage state per the AGENTS.md "Platform coverage caveats" matrix and is not changed by Phase 2. **Important (carried from v1.1.4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new skill to take effect.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: Three new items in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`: DF-002 (A4 plan-described starting state did not match repo state - documented for traceability), DF-003 (macOS / Linux installer dry-run deferred to Phase 3 or a release-readiness smoke task; Phase 2 verification was Windows / Git Bash only), and QG-001 (cross-OS verification gate ran on one OS only, satisfying the plan's "at least one OS" minimum but not the cross-cutting constraint's "cross-OS once per phase" preference - de-prioritized because Phase 2 does not add bundled scripts and the recursive-copy primitive analysis covers the parity question structurally). Carried over from Phase 1: DF-001 (the missing `create-skill-or-command` skill referenced by the plan's sub-task 1.1 prompt). Phase 3 starts next; it formalizes the per-skill `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` layout convention (A13) and adds the `--dry-run` capability to both installers, after which DF-003 / QG-001 can be retired by running the dry-run on at least one Unix host.

*   **Test Posture**: All four test suites green and JSON catalogs valid against the new state. `python -c "json.load(...)"` passes for `data/skills.json` (189 skills, +1 from v1.1.5 baseline of 188), `data/bundles.json` (11 bundles), `data/workflows.json` (17 workflows), `data/templates.json`, `data/marketplace.json`. ShellCheck (`--severity=warning`) clean against `scripts/installer.sh` and `install.sh`. `bash -n scripts/installer.sh` syntax check clean. `python -m pytest` results identical to v1.1.5 baseline: `extensions/devai-skill-server` 37 passed; `extensions/devai-code-search` 36 passed, 1 skipped; `extensions/devai-web-fetch` 23 passed; `catalog/hooks/tests` 310 passed. Total 406 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures - Phase 2 adds no test surface (the new skill is a Markdown file; the registry edits are JSON and the index Markdown that `make validate` already covers).

*   **Current Status**: Phase 2 complete and ready for commit. New file: `catalog/skills/workflow/doc-coauthoring/SKILL.md`. Modified files: `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, `data/marketplace.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`, `docs/DEVLOG.md` (this entry). Plan advances to Phase 3 (the foundational A13 layout convention - per-skill `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` subdir support, both installers + `make validate` extended) once the user reviews and commits.

## [2026-05-08] - Phase 1 of v1.1.5 adoption-skills plan: Skill-native doc edits (A14, A17, A15, A11, A12)

*   **Goal**: Execute Phase 1 of the v1.1.5 `adoption-skills` plan ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/plans/adoption-skills.md](v1.1.5/plans/adoption-skills.md)). Phase 1 is the "skill-native" tier of the plan - five doc-only edits to existing tracked Markdown files that close the cheapest capability gaps identified in the comparison report ([docs/archives/v1/v1.1/comparison-skills.md](v1.1.5/comparison-skills.md)) without adding any new file to the catalog file tree. Phase 1 ships under `[Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG; the version bump itself is deferred to after Phase 7 per a user-supplied constraint that the entire seven-phase plan ships as a single v1.2.0 release rather than as seven incremental patch versions.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **A14 - Pushy description guidance** institutionalized in two places. AGENTS.md "Adding a New Skill -> Write SKILL.md" gains a new "Description style: combat undertriggering" block that documents Claude's measurable tendency to under-trigger on narrow descriptions, the four rules of pushy descriptions (verbatim trigger phrases, explicit `SKIP:` clauses, synonym coverage, action-then-trigger structure), and a 6-words-vs-60-words before / after example. The same guidance is mirrored into `catalog/skills/workflow/create-custom-command/SKILL.md` (commands also have descriptions and the same under-triggering risk applies); the SKILL.md gains a Common Rationalizations table it didn't previously have, with three rebuttals targeting the most common reasons authors leave descriptions narrow.
    *   **A17 - Three-Tier Loading Model** documented as a new `#### Three-Tier Loading Model` subsection under "Write SKILL.md" in AGENTS.md. Documents the three tiers explicitly: tier 1 (always loaded, ~150-300 tokens, determines triggering) = `name` + `description` + `summary_l0` + `overview_l1`; tier 2 (loaded on trigger) = SKILL.md body, target ≤500 lines; tier 3 (loaded on demand) = bundled `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/` per the A13 convention from Phase 3, with the critical performance affordance that scripts EXECUTE without their source being loaded into context. Practical authoring implications added: push some-of-the-time content to references, push deterministic steps to scripts, keep tier 1 fields tight because they pay tokens on every catalog read across every session.
    *   **A15 - SKILL.md size norm reconciled** in AGENTS.md. The previous "Keep SKILL.md under 800 lines." rule replaced with "Target ≤500 lines for the SKILL.md body. Soft cap 800 lines." Beyond 500 lines, authors add a `references/` subdirectory with a TOC and link to it from the body. Beyond 800 lines, the skill MUST be split or refactored before merge. Existing skills that exceed 500 lines are explicitly grandfathered - the norm is forward-looking and applies to new and substantially-rewritten skills only, so this change does not retroactively flag any existing catalog skill.
    *   **A11 - Aesthetic-distinctiveness lens** added to `catalog/skills/developer-experience/frontend-ui-engineering/SKILL.md` as a new "Aesthetic Distinctiveness" section after Step 7. Documents the recognizable AI-default aesthetic that production-grade UI must avoid (centered hero + three-card grid + gradient button + Inter typeface + uniform padding + 12px border-radius), six countermeasures (custom typography pairing, asymmetric layout, intentional density, distinctive accent color, motion that means something, copy with a voice), three reference patterns the agent can pick one of (editorial multi-column, brutalist over-borders, restrained motion), and a process step (write a one-page direction note up-front, not as a polish pass). Adds a Common Rationalizations row rebutting "the agent's default looks fine, we can polish later" and a Verification entry requiring the project to deviate from the AI-default in at least 2-3 dimensions.
    *   **A12 - Static-poster / print workflow** added to `catalog/skills/developer-experience/creative-generation/SKILL.md` as a new "Static Poster / Print Workflow" section after the existing Ideation section. Documents a deliberate two-step approach: step 1 writes a 30-80 line Markdown design philosophy fixing color palette, typography, composition principles, and 1-2 reference movements; step 2 renders the actual `.png` / `.pdf` output via `pptx-generation` / `docx-generation` / `pdf-document-generation` for standard formats or a single-purpose Pillow / matplotlib script for one-off bespoke layouts. Generative / algorithmic / interactive visual outputs (p5.js sketches, HTML canvas) are explicitly scoped OUT - those belong to the `generative-art` skill that Phase 4 / A1 will ship, not here. Adds a Common Rationalizations table (which the file did not previously have) with three rebuttals targeting the most common reasons authors skip the philosophy step.
    *   **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` populated.** A new `### Changed` block under `## [Unreleased]` lists all five edits in sectioned-bullet form (Skill-authoring guidance in AGENTS.md / Skill body edits / Tests / Known gaps), with a Tests section recording the four-suite green run (37 + 36 + 23 + 310 = 406 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures) and a Known gaps section pointing at `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`. No version-string bump anywhere - the entry stays under `[Unreleased]` until Phase 7 wraps.

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **how to handle the missing `create-skill-or-command` skill** in sub-task 1.1. The plan prompt said to update both `create-skill-or-command/SKILL.md` and `create-custom-command/SKILL.md`, but only the latter exists in the catalog (`Glob` for `catalog/skills/**/create-skill*/SKILL.md` returned no results). The skill name appears in the harness's global skill list, but that's an external skill (likely a Claude Code built-in or a separately-installed skill), not a DevAI-Hub catalog entry. The de facto skill-authoring guide for DevAI-Hub authors is `AGENTS.md` "Adding a New Skill -> Write SKILL.md", which sits at line 59-112 of AGENTS.md and documents the YAML frontmatter, body sections, registration steps, and validation. Three options: (a) skip A14 for the missing file and apply only to `create-custom-command`; (b) create a new `create-skill-or-command` SKILL.md that duplicates AGENTS.md content; (c) apply A14 to AGENTS.md "Adding a New Skill" instead. Option (a) leaves the most important location (the skill-authoring guide for actual skill authors) untouched. Option (b) creates a documentation duplication that will drift. Option (c) applies the rule where it actually matters, with a cross-reference from `create-custom-command` for command authors. Picked (c) and logged the decision in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` as DF-001 with a clear "suggested next step" pointing at whether to formalize a dedicated catalog skill (recommendation: leave in AGENTS.md, since AGENTS.md is the canonical authoring guide and a catalog skill that duplicates it would drift). The second key call was **how aggressive to be on the aesthetic-distinctiveness section in A11**. The comparison report's Section 4 framed the upstream pattern as a checklist; in DevAI-Hub the existing `frontend-ui-engineering` skill already has an opinionated voice in its Common Rationalizations table, so the new section was written to match that voice rather than to copy the upstream's flatter checklist style. The "What the AI default looks like (avoid)" sub-section names the visual pattern explicitly so the agent recognizes when it's about to ship that exact thing - which is the fix-mode the comparison report identified as missing. The third call was **whether to inline a Common Rationalizations table into `creative-generation/SKILL.md`** for A12. The file is short (35 lines pre-edit) and didn't follow the standard DevAI-Hub skill structure (no When-to-Use, no Verification, no Common Rationalizations). Adding a full restructure would have exceeded Phase 1's "five doc-only edits" scope. Compromise: A12 ships the Static Poster section AND a Common Rationalizations table specifically about the static-poster decision, leaving the rest of the file's structure unchanged. Future plan items can normalize the rest of the file if needed.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE. No schema changes, no settings.json changes, no installer behavior changes, no `data/` registry changes, no version-string changes. Existing v1.1.5 installations re-run the installer and pick up the five patched Markdown files under `~/.claude/skills/.../` and `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` (and the `skills/` mirror locations for Gemini / Codex). Cursor / OpenCode / Copilot pick up the AGENTS.md edits via their respective instruction-file rendering paths; the three skill-body edits also reach those three platforms via the `{{SKILL_INDEX}}` block, but only as index-level metadata - the per-skill body itself only lands on Claude Code / Gemini / Codex per the AGENTS.md "Platform coverage caveats" matrix, which is the existing platform-coverage state and is not changed by Phase 1. **Important (carried from v1.1.4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them; restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / OpenCode sessions for the new bodies to take effect.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: One open item logged in `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` (DF-001 - the missing `create-skill-or-command` skill referenced by the plan's sub-task 1.1 prompt). No new bugs, no suppressed lint rules, no skipped tests, no quality-gate bypasses. Phase 2 of the plan starts next; it will resolve the `claude-api` skill index drift and ship a new `doc-coauthoring` skill. Phase 3 (the foundational A13 layout convention) front-loads the per-skill `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` subdir support that Phases 4-7 depend on. The version bump to v1.2.0 happens once Phase 7 wraps.

*   **Test Posture**: All four test suites green and JSON catalogs valid. `python -c "json.load(...)"` passes for `data/skills.json` (188 skills), `data/bundles.json` (11 bundles), `data/workflows.json` (17 workflows), `data/templates.json`. ShellCheck (`--severity=warning`) clean against `scripts/installer.sh` and `install.sh`. `python -m pytest` results: `extensions/devai-skill-server` 37 passed; `extensions/devai-code-search` 36 passed, 1 skipped, 52 deprecation warnings (pre-existing third-party `pathspec` library, not introduced by Phase 1); `extensions/devai-web-fetch` 23 passed; `catalog/hooks/tests` 310 passed. Total 406 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures across all four suites - identical to the v1.1.5 release baseline since Phase 1 is doc-only on Markdown files and does not touch any tested surface.

*   **Current Status**: Phase 1 complete and ready for commit. Five Markdown files modified, one new file created (`docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md`), one entry appended to `[Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md, one entry prepended to DEVLOG.md (this entry). Working tree shows exactly the expected six modified files plus `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md` (new) and `docs/archive/v1/v1.1/development/history/...` (Phase 1 session history file, generated next). Plan advances to Phase 2 (P0 cleanup + doc-coauthoring skill) once the user reviews and commits.

## [2026-05-06] - Release 1.1.5: Sectioned-Bullet Structure for Commit Messages

*   **Goal**: Close the structural gap that v1.1.1 / v1.1.4 didn't address. v1.1.1 forbade hard-wrapping inside paragraphs and bullets; v1.1.4 propagated that rule into the downstream commands that actually generate commit messages (`/implement-phase`, `/wrap-up-session`, `/update-version`). But neither release said anything about *body structure* - the agent could still produce a body of 5-6 long flowing paragraphs separated by blank lines, which forces reviewers to read every paragraph linearly to find the change for a specific component. Reported live: a v1.1.4-generated commit (the next `/implement-phase` run after the v1.1.4 install) came out exactly that shape - properly unwrapped paragraphs but six of them in a row, no labeled sections, no scannable anchors. Patch release because the change is content-only across five command and skill files (no schema, no installer, no test changes).

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **`catalog/commands/generate-commit-message.md` body rules + example replaced.** Adds a "Body structure (CRITICAL for non-trivial commits)" rule requiring labeled sections with bullets (headers ending in a colon, grouped by component / module / theme). The 1-2 sentence intro paragraph + sectioned-bullet body shape replaces the prior "paragraphs and/or bullet points" guidance. Always treats **Tests** and **Known gaps** / **Deviations** as dedicated final sections. Whitespace constraint added: exactly one blank line between sections; bullets contiguous within a section. The example block was rewritten to demonstrate the sectioned style on a realistic multi-component commit (Reporting package / Packaging and paths / Desktop UI / Tests / Known gaps - patterned after the user-supplied "after" example). A counter-example block was added showing the multi-paragraph flowing-prose body shape that the agent must NOT produce, even with the no-hard-wrap rule honored.
    *   **`catalog/skills/workflow/code-commit-workflow/SKILL.md` Body subsection + Examples + Rationalizations + Checklist all extended.** New rule paragraph in the Body subsection mirrors the canonical command. New Good Example added at the end of the Good Examples section showing the sectioned style on the same Phase 6 docxtpl scenario (paralleling the user-supplied "after" example). New Bad Example showing the multi-paragraph flowing-prose body shape. New Common Rationalizations row rebutting "flowing paragraphs read better than bulleted lists for prose-heavy commits" - the agent's likely failure mode given its training on academic prose conventions. Quality Checklist gains a sectioned-structure item explicitly naming the Tests and Known gaps / Deviations sections.
    *   **`catalog/commands/implement-phase.md` post-phase sub-step 6 inline rule expanded.** Adds the sectioned-bullet rule with implementation-specific suggested headers. The implement-phase context is the highest-volume commit-generation path in the project (every phase implementation produces one commit), so this is the most important file to get right.
    *   **`catalog/commands/wrap-up-session.md` Phase 7 inline rule expanded.** Adds the sectioned-bullet rule with wrap-up-specific suggested headers (`Session history:` / `DEVLOG:` / `Documentation:` / `Gitignore:` / `Memory:` / `Version bump:`).
    *   **`catalog/commands/update-version.md` Phase E4 inline rule + example + counter-example replaced.** Format and rules block now requires the sectioned-bullet structure using CHANGELOG section names as headers directly (`Added:` / `Changed:` / `Fixed:` / `Removed:` / `Tests:`). The example was rewritten to map CHANGELOG entries to the matching section headers (Phase B layout / gitignore changes also called out as their own sections if relevant); a counter-example showing the previous flat `Changes:` bullet-soup style was added so the agent cannot fall back to that shape. Disambiguation note added: the 72-char subject-line cap is a hard limit, not a wrap (re-stated from v1.1.4 to make sure the structure rule doesn't accidentally re-introduce confusion about that line).
    *   **Canonical version bump 1.1.4 -> 1.1.5** across the same 13 files as v1.1.4. CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.5] - 2026-05-06`; CHANGELOG footer Unreleased link bumped to `v1.1.5...HEAD`, and a new `[1.1.5]: v1.1.4...v1.1.5` comparison link added.

*   **Design Rationale**: Most important call was **how strictly to enforce the sectioned style**. Three options: (1) require sectioned-bullet structure for *every* commit body, including trivial 1-2 file commits where it's overkill; (2) require it only for "non-trivial" commits with no clear definition; (3) define the threshold explicitly as "any commit touching multiple components." Option 3 - the choice this release makes - has a clear rule the agent can apply (count the distinct components in the diff; if > 1, use sectioned style). The same rule now appears in all five files with identical wording, so a future regression in any one is detectable by diffing against the others. The second key call was **what counts as a section header**. The user's example used `Reporting package (`src/reporting/`):` style (component path in backticks, then a colon) which works well for code-component commits. For wrap-up commits, headers are activity-typed (`DEVLOG:`, `Documentation:`); for release commits, they map directly to CHANGELOG section names (`Added:`, `Changed:`, `Fixed:`). The release deliberately gives different suggested header palettes per command so the agent has a context-appropriate starting point rather than a generic "use sections" instruction it has to invent headers for. The third call was **rejecting an enforcement test** - a static check that scans command bodies for "generate" + "commit message" without a sectioned-style rule could prevent regressions but adds maintenance burden and false positives. Tracked as a v1.2.0+ candidate; for now, the cross-file consistency of the rule wording IS the regression signal.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE. No schema changes, no settings.json changes, no installer behavior changes, no test surface changes. Existing v1.1.4 installations re-run the installer and pick up the five patched command + skill bodies under `~/.claude/commands/` / `~/.claude/skills/` (and `commands/` / `workflows/` / `prompts/` mirror locations for Gemini / Codex). **Important (carried from v1.1.4)**: Claude Code reads slash command and skill bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them. After running the v1.1.5 installer, restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / Copilot sessions for the new bodies to take effect.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: No new follow-ups opened by v1.1.5. The sectioned-bullet rule depends on the agent's interpretation of "what counts as a component" in the diff - for diffs that span multiple loosely-related files in the same package, the agent might collapse them into one bullet or split them into multiple sections; that judgment call is left to the agent because hard-coding it would over-fit the rule. Carried-over follow-ups from earlier patches remain (5 PSUseApprovedVerbs warnings in `scripts/installer.ps1` from v1.1.0 era; Codex / OpenCode CLI invocation forms may need adjusting if their CLIs change syntax). A future enhancement could add a static-presence linter for the sectioned-style rule across command bodies (already noted in v1.1.4 as a v1.2.0+ candidate); v1.1.5 reinforces the case for it but doesn't add it.

*   **Test Posture**: All four quality gates clean. `make validate` (JSON integrity) passes. `bash -n` clean on installer.sh and session-start.sh. Hook test suite from v1.1.3 (310/310) still passes against v1.1.5 with zero changes - this release is content-only on five command and skill bodies and does not touch any tested surface. The user-facing fix is verifiable by re-running `/implement-phase` after a session restart and inspecting whether the generated commit message uses labeled section headers (`Reporting package:`, `Packaging:`, `Desktop UI:`, etc.) or falls back to the multi-paragraph flowing-prose shape.

*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.5 surfaces shipped. The annotated `v1.1.5` tag is created locally with the release commit; push to origin happens at user direction.
