## [2026-05-06] - Release 1.1.4: Commit-Message No-Hard-Wrap Rule Reaches the Generators

*   **Goal**: Close a gap that v1.1.1 missed and v1.1.3 did not catch. v1.1.1 extended the no-hard-wrap rule from bullets to all body content in `/generate-commit-message` and the `code-commit-workflow` skill, on the assumption that any command path ending in commit-message generation would route through the patched canonical command. That assumption was wrong: a textual reference to `/generate-commit-message` inside another command body (e.g. `/implement-phase` post-phase sub-step 6 "Run `/generate-commit-message`") is just text - the agent does NOT auto-load that file's body when it sees the reference. So the canonical fix only applied when the user typed `/generate-commit-message` directly. Every other path - `/implement-phase`, `/wrap-up-session`, `/update-version` - kept producing commit messages wrapped at ~70 columns. The user reported the bug live: a v0.3.0 phase-implementation commit, generated from a fresh v1.1.3 install in a brand-new Claude Code session, came out fully wrapped. Patch release because the change is content-only on three command bodies (no schema, no installer, no permission edits) and strictly additive (each patched command gains a new rule paragraph; nothing is removed or restructured).

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **`catalog/commands/implement-phase.md` post-phase sub-step 6 patched.** Sub-step 6 is the one that runs at the end of every successful `/implement-phase` execution and tells the agent to "Run `/generate-commit-message`" as a sub-step. Inlined the explicit no-hard-wrap rule with all three reinforcement clauses: (a) every paragraph and every bullet point in the commit body and footer MUST be a single continuous source line regardless of length, (b) explicit wrap-column callouts (50, 72, 80, 100) so the agent cannot rationalize one as "the convention," and (c) the obsolete-72-char-convention rebuttal that names modern Git, GitHub, GitLab, and `git log` as soft-wrap-on-display so the agent cannot fall back to the historical justification. Subject-line 50-char cap explicitly carved out as the only exception (a hard limit, not a wrap).
    *   **`catalog/commands/wrap-up-session.md` Phase 7 patched.** Phase 7 ("Final Commit") is structurally identical to `/implement-phase` sub-step 6 - it tells the agent to "Run `/generate-commit-message`" with scope guidance. Same rule injection, before the existing scope-and-format bullets.
    *   **`catalog/commands/update-version.md` Phase E4 rules extended.** Phase E4 ("Generate Commit Message") was different from the other two: it does NOT delegate to `/generate-commit-message`, it has its OWN inline format and rules block (lines 418-437). The v1.1.1 fix didn't apply because there was no transitive reference. The single bullet "Keep each bullet point concise and on a single line" was the closest the section got to the no-wrap rule, but it covered only bullets and it carried the dangerous "single line" framing without the explicit "regardless of length" / "no column-width breaks" reinforcement. Replaced with the full paragraph-and-bullet rule. Also disambiguated the existing "First line: `vX.X.X:` followed by a concise summary (under 72 chars)" rule by adding "The 72-char cap on the subject line is a hard limit, not a wrap" so the agent cannot generalize the cap to body lines.
    *   **Canonical version bump 1.1.3 -> 1.1.4** across the same 13 files as v1.1.3: `.claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace}.json`, `data/{bundles,marketplace,templates,workflows}.json`, `catalog/hooks/session-start.sh`, `scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `catalog/skills/README.md`, `guides/reference/SUBAGENTS_GUIDE.md`, `infrastructure/{hooks,tools}/README.md`. CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.4] - 2026-05-06`; CHANGELOG footer Unreleased link bumped to `v1.1.4...HEAD`, new `[1.1.4]: v1.1.3...v1.1.4` comparison link added.

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **inline duplication vs. an upstream "include this skill" mechanism**. Slash commands in Claude Code do not have a transitive-import primitive - "Run `/generate-commit-message`" in a command body is text, not an import directive. Three options exist: (1) inline the rule in every command that generates commit messages, accepting per-command duplication (~5 lines x 3 commands = 15 lines of duplication, which can drift); (2) build a "load this skill" sub-command that the agent runs first to read the canonical guidance into context, accepting an extra tool round-trip per invocation; (3) move the rule to a global like `CLAUDE.md` and trust the agent to apply it. Option 3 is what v1.1.1 effectively assumed - and it failed empirically because the agent's training on the obsolete 72-char convention overrode the global no-wrap rule whenever the word "commit message" appeared near generation time. Option 2 is fragile (depends on the agent reliably executing the side-effect read; nothing forces it). Option 1 - this release's choice - is the most robust against agent context drift because the rule is in the same context window as the generation step. The duplication cost is real but bounded; a future release could add a static check that flags any new command body containing "generate" and "commit message" without the no-wrap rule, but that's a v1.2.0+ candidate. The second key call was **scope of the patch**. Only three commands were known to generate commit messages directly today; I deliberately did not sweep through every other command speculatively (`/generate-changelog`, `/generate-devlog`, etc., produce structured Markdown but not commit messages). Every changed line traces to the user's reported bug.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE. No schema changes, no settings.json changes, no installer behavior changes, no permission edits. Existing v1.1.3 installations re-run the installer and pick up the three patched command bodies under `~/.claude/commands/` (and the `commands/` / `workflows/` / `prompts/` mirror locations for Gemini / Codex). **Important**: Claude Code reads slash command bodies at session start and does NOT hot-reload them. After running the v1.1.4 installer, restart any already-running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / Copilot sessions for the new bodies to take effect.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: No new follow-ups opened by v1.1.4. The carryover follow-ups from v1.1.3 remain (5 PSUseApprovedVerbs warnings in `scripts/installer.ps1` from v1.1.0 era; Codex / OpenCode CLI invocation forms may need adjusting if their CLIs change syntax in future releases). A future enhancement could be a static "commit-message rule presence" linter that flags any new command body containing both "commit message" and "generate" without the explicit no-wrap rule, preventing this exact regression class from recurring; tracked as a v1.2.0+ candidate.

*   **Test Posture**: All four quality gates clean. `make validate` (JSON integrity) passes. `bash -n` clean on installer.sh and session-start.sh. The hook test suite from v1.1.3 (310/310) still passes against v1.1.4 with zero changes - this release is content-only on three command bodies and does not touch any tested surface. The user-facing bug fix is verifiable by re-running `/implement-phase` and inspecting whether the generated commit message has paragraph or bullet line breaks at any column width; per-session restart is required after install so the patched command body is loaded fresh.

*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.4 surfaces shipped. The annotated `v1.1.4` tag is created locally with the release commit; push to origin happens at user direction.

## [2026-05-06] - Release 1.1.3: Platform-Independent Pre-Commit Review Hooks

*   **Goal**: v1.1.2 shipped a Claude-only git pre-commit review hook (`claude-diff-review.sh`) and an `/install-claude-pre-commit-hook` command. Within hours, the user pushed back on the architecture: forcing Cursor / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode users to install Anthropic's `claude` CLI just to use the review hook violated the project's cross-platform independence rule (each AI platform should use its own native equivalents, never depend on a sibling vendor). v1.1.3 reworks the v1.1.2 design into four parallel, fully-independent hooks - one per supported AI CLI - and replaces the Claude-only slash command with an auto-detecting variant. Patch release because the change is strictly additive at the hook level (the v1.1.2 Claude hook is preserved unchanged) and the breaking removal of the v1.1.2 slash command is mitigated by zero-hour migration window (v1.1.2 shipped earlier the same day).

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **Three new platform-parallel hook scripts**: `catalog/hooks/gemini-diff-review.sh` (calls `gemini -p`), `catalog/hooks/codex-diff-review.sh` (calls `codex exec`), and `catalog/hooks/opencode-diff-review.sh` (calls `opencode run`). Each is a fully self-contained ~125-line bash script copied from the v1.1.2 Claude hook with three substitutions: the binary name in the `command -v` presence check, the CLI invocation in the run-command call, and the platform-name string in every log-message prefix. Bypass paths, merge / rebase short-circuit, fail-open behavior, diff-size cap, and `VERDICT: PASS|WARN|BLOCK` parsing are byte-identical across the four variants because they all need to behave the same way as a git pre-commit hook regardless of which CLI runs the actual review.
    *   **Codex and OpenCode use a combined-argument pattern** rather than the `printf '%s' "$DIFF" | claude -p "$PROMPT"` stdin-context pattern that the Claude and Gemini hooks use. Codex's `exec` subcommand and OpenCode's `run` subcommand do not consistently read context from stdin across versions / model providers, so the prompt and diff are concatenated into a single positional argument (`codex exec "$COMBINED"` / `opencode run "$COMBINED"`). The 50 KB diff cap remains relevant because shell argument-list limits on Linux are ~128 KB total - well above the cap - and on Windows are ~32 KB total, so the cap also serves as a Windows-safety guarantee for the Codex / OpenCode variants specifically.
    *   **Slash command renamed and rewritten**. v1.1.2 `catalog/commands/install-claude-pre-commit-hook.md` was deleted via `git rm` (zero-hour migration window since v1.1.2 shipped the same day). New `catalog/commands/install-pre-commit-review-hook.md` replaces it with auto-detection logic: runs `command -v claude/gemini/codex/opencode` to discover which CLIs are on PATH, then either auto-selects (one match), asks the user (multiple matches), or asks the user to install one (zero matches). Optional `--platform=<name>` flag forces a specific platform (useful when the user wants a hook for a CLI not yet installed); `--force` flag skips existing-hook prompts. The marker-comment detection now matches any of the four `# <platform>-diff-review.sh` headers so a re-run can detect which platform is currently installed and offer to switch / re-install cleanly.
    *   **Test refactor**: v1.1.2 `catalog/hooks/tests/test_claude_diff_review.py` was renamed to `test_diff_review_hooks.py` (plural) via `git mv` to preserve history, then rewritten to parametrize every test class over a `(hook_filename, cli_binary_name)` tuple list. Each of the 11 logical scenarios from v1.1.2 now runs 4 times - one per platform variant - for 44 parametrized tests. Plus a new `TestPlatformIndependence` class (4 more tests, one per variant) that inspects each hook's source file directly and asserts no `command -v <other-cli>` check or `<other-cli> -p` / `<other-cli> exec` / `<other-cli> run` invocation exists. Total 48 tests in the new file. Full hook suite: 310 tests (262 v1.1.1 baseline + 48 new), all green.
    *   **Installer wiring expanded**. The single `safe_copy` line from v1.1.2 in both `scripts/installer.sh` (line 1424) and `scripts/installer.ps1` (line 1733) was replaced by a 4-element loop covering all four `*-diff-review.sh` variants. The loop body still uses `safe_copy` / `Safe-Copy` (with the existing pre-existing-warning verb-naming - PSUseApprovedVerbs - inherited unchanged from v1.1.0 era, deliberately not refactored as that would be scope-creep cleanup unrelated to the v1.1.3 directive). Per-variant existence guard (`[ -f ]` / `Test-Path`) silently skips missing files so a partial catalog still installs cleanly.
    *   **Canonical version bump 1.1.2 -> 1.1.3** across the same 13 files as v1.1.2: `.claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace}.json`, `data/{bundles,marketplace,templates,workflows}.json`, `catalog/hooks/session-start.sh`, `scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `catalog/skills/README.md`, `guides/reference/SUBAGENTS_GUIDE.md`, `infrastructure/{hooks,tools}/README.md`. `session-start.sh` `COMMAND_COUNT` stays at 33 (one slash command removed, one added - net zero). CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.3] - 2026-05-06`; CHANGELOG footer Unreleased link bumped to `v1.1.3...HEAD`, and a new `[1.1.3]: v1.1.2...v1.1.3` comparison link added.

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **fully duplicate scripts vs. shared bash library**. A shared library (`catalog/hooks/diff-review-lib.sh` sourced by each thin platform-specific wrapper) would be ~75% less code duplication and easier to maintain a single shared prompt, but it has two real problems for the git-hook use case. First, the hook gets copied into `.git/hooks/pre-commit` as a freestanding artifact - a dependency on `~/.devai-hub/hooks/diff-review-lib.sh` makes the hook fail if the user moves their dotfiles, switches DevAI-Hub install paths, or copies the hook to a new machine. Self-contained scripts survive all those cases. Second, the user's directive ("each platform should be independent") was clear; a shared-library design would technically be 4 thin wrappers but the actual review logic would still funnel through one shared file, which is a different shape than the user asked for. The duplication cost is real (~360 extra lines of bash) but the durability and clarity gains outweigh it. The second key call was **breaking the v1.1.2 command vs. shipping an alias**. The v1.1.2 slash command had only existed for a few hours when v1.1.3 went out, so an alias adds permanent vestigial code to defend against a migration that affects nobody. Per the project rule "Avoid backwards-compatibility hacks ... if you are certain that something is unused, you can delete it completely" - clean removal was correct. The third call was **Cursor and Copilot scope**. Both lack a usable headless review CLI; pretending to support them via a stub hook would be dishonest. Documenting the gap explicitly in the slash command body lets the affected users self-route either to one of the four supported CLIs as a side dependency or to CI-side review.

*   **Migration Impact**: Effectively NONE for v1.1.2 users. The v1.1.2 Claude hook (`~/.devai-hub/hooks/claude-diff-review.sh`) is unchanged byte-for-byte in v1.1.3. Existing v1.1.2 installations of `.git/hooks/pre-commit` (created by the now-removed `/install-claude-pre-commit-hook`) keep working - the hook source still exists at the same path. The only breaking change is the v1.1.2 slash command name, which had a few-hour install window and was almost certainly invoked by nobody beyond the release author.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: The 5 PSUseApprovedVerbs warnings in `scripts/installer.ps1` (`Safe-Copy`, `Safe-Folder-Copy`, `Detect-Languages`, `Detect-ProjectMetadata`, `Render-Template`) pre-date v1.1.0 and remain - inherited unchanged because every cmdlet rename would propagate to dozens of call sites. Tracked as a v1.2.0 candidate. The Codex and OpenCode hook variants use `codex exec` and `opencode run` respectively as the most-documented current invocation forms; future CLI changes may require updating the call line in those two scripts. If users find their CLI uses different syntax, they can edit `~/.devai-hub/hooks/<platform>-diff-review.sh` directly - the script is self-contained and not regenerated by the installer between releases. Cursor and GitHub Copilot remain genuinely unsupported by this command; that gap is documented in the slash command body, not paved over.

*   **Test Posture**: All four quality gates clean. `make validate` (JSON integrity) passes. `bash -n` clean on all 4 hook scripts plus installer.sh and session-start.sh. The new test file (`test_diff_review_hooks.py`) is 48/48 green; full hook test suite is 310/310 against v1.1.3. The v1.1.1 installer-smoke resilience fix from earlier today still works as designed: the v1.1.3 bump did not require a test-code change to keep the smoke test passing.

*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.3 surfaces shipped. The annotated `v1.1.3` tag is created locally with the release commit; push to origin happens at user direction.

## [2026-05-06] - Release 1.1.2: Opt-In Git Pre-Commit Claude Review Hook

*   **Goal**: Close a gap that the existing agent-level `secret-scan.sh` Claude Code hook cannot close on its own. `secret-scan.sh` is a `PreToolUse:Write/Edit` hook, so it only fires when Claude Code itself proposes a write. Code edited from Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini, a terminal editor, or a teammate's machine never passes through that gate. A patch release adds an **opt-in** git pre-commit hook that pipes `git diff --cached` through `claude -p` for an LLM review. Because the trigger surface is `git commit`, the new hook fires on every commit regardless of which agent (or human) authored the change. The two hooks are complementary, not redundant: regex at write-time (deterministic, zero token cost, Claude Code only) plus LLM at commit-time (judgment-driven, catches debug artifacts and TODOs that regex never could, all editor paths). Patch release rather than minor bump because the change is strictly additive and gated behind explicit per-repo opt-in - no existing repository's behavior changes until the user runs the new slash command.

*   **What Changed**:
    *   **`catalog/hooks/claude-diff-review.sh`** - the hook itself, ~120 lines of bash. Reads `git diff --cached`, caps the diff at 50 KB by default (configurable via `DEVAI_DIFF_REVIEW_MAX_BYTES`), pipes it through `claude -p` with a strict review prompt covering hardcoded credentials, debug artifacts, unfinished TODOs, and large commented-out code blocks. Parses Claude's response on the first line (`VERDICT: PASS|WARN|BLOCK`) and exits accordingly: `PASS` silent allow, `WARN` prints findings to stderr but allows the commit, `BLOCK` refuses the commit with exit 1. Fail-open on every error path - missing CLI, empty response, unparseable verdict, oversized diff, merge / cherry-pick / rebase in progress, env-var bypass set. Three explicit bypass paths: `DEVAI_DIFF_REVIEW_DISABLE=1 git commit ...` per-commit override, git's standard `--no-verify` flag, and the configurable size cap.
    *   **`catalog/commands/install-claude-pre-commit-hook.md`** - new slash command. When invoked from inside a target repo, copies `~/.devai-hub/hooks/claude-diff-review.sh` to that repo's `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Detects pre-existing hooks: if the file already contains the DevAI-Hub marker (`# claude-diff-review.sh`), reports already-installed and exits cleanly; otherwise shows the existing hook to the user and offers replace / abort / chain-manually paths, with a `.git/hooks/pre-commit.devai-backup-<timestamp>` backup written before any overwrite. Cross-platform: works on Linux, macOS, and Windows (Git for Windows runs hooks via its bundled bash, so the bash source runs natively).
    *   **Installer wiring** in both `scripts/installer.sh` (line 1424) and `scripts/installer.ps1` (line 1733), inside the existing `install_templates` function next to the style-guides copy. Distributes the hook source to `~/.devai-hub/hooks/claude-diff-review.sh` on POSIX or `%USERPROFILE%\.devai-hub\hooks\claude-diff-review.sh` on Windows, with `chmod +x` on POSIX. The hook is intentionally **not** added to `catalog/hooks/settings.json`, because settings.json wires Claude Code PreToolUse hooks; this is a git hook with a different trigger surface and a different lifecycle. The shared `~/.devai-hub/` location (not per-platform under `~/.claude/hooks/`) reflects that the hook is platform-agnostic on the trigger axis.
    *   **`catalog/hooks/tests/test_claude_diff_review.py`** - 11 new pytest tests covering bash syntax (`bash -n`), env-var bypass short-circuit, empty-diff exit, missing-CLI fail-open with warning to stderr, merge-state skip, rebase-state skip, diff-size-cap warning, and PASS / WARN / BLOCK / unparseable verdict parsing. The stub `claude` CLI is a fake bash binary placed on PATH that emits a fixed response; the temp git repo fixture creates a fresh repo with one staged change so the hook has a real diff to inspect. Combined hook test suite: 273 tests passing (262 prior + 11 new).
    *   **Canonical version bump 1.1.1 -> 1.1.2** across the same 13 files as v1.1.1: `.claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace}.json`, `data/{bundles,marketplace,templates,workflows}.json`, `catalog/hooks/session-start.sh`, `scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `catalog/skills/README.md`, `guides/reference/SUBAGENTS_GUIDE.md`, `infrastructure/{hooks,tools}/README.md`. Plus `session-start.sh` `COMMAND_COUNT` 32 -> 33 (one new slash command). CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.2] - 2026-05-06`; CHANGELOG footer Unreleased link bumped to `v1.1.2...HEAD`, and a new `[1.1.2]: v1.1.1...v1.1.2` comparison link added.

*   **Design Rationale**: The most important judgment call was **opt-in vs. opt-out**. An opt-out design (auto-install the hook on every DevAI-Hub install) was rejected for three reasons. First, every commit becomes a `claude -p` call (~3-8k input + ~200 output tokens, ~2-10s latency); silently imposing that on every user every commit is too aggressive. Second, the hook may produce false positives on legitimate `# TODO(jane):` markers, dummy test data, and config templates with placeholder values; a user surprised by their first BLOCK on a routine commit will reach for `git commit -n` and lose trust in the safety guarantee permanently. Third, a Claude-CLI-not-installed warning printed on every commit by default is noise. The opt-in design (run `/install-claude-pre-commit-hook` once per repo) makes activation an explicit consent gesture and gives the user one clear place to look ('which repos have this enabled?') rather than a per-machine policy that's hard to audit. The second key call was placing the hook source under `~/.devai-hub/hooks/` rather than `~/.claude/hooks/` (where existing PreToolUse hooks live). The hook is not a Claude Code hook - it's a git hook that happens to call the Claude CLI - and putting it under `~/.claude/` would mislead users into thinking it's wired through the Claude Code hook system. The third call was the verdict format: a strict first-line `VERDICT: PASS|WARN|BLOCK` that the bash hook can grep and `case` on, rather than free-form prose the hook would have to parse. The cost is one extra prompt-engineering instruction; the benefit is a deterministic mapping from LLM output to exit code, with a fail-open default for any unparseable response.

*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for any existing repository. The hook ships to `~/.devai-hub/hooks/` but is never auto-wired into any `.git/hooks/pre-commit` - users opt in per-repo by running the slash command. Existing v1.1.1 installations re-run the installer and pick up one new file (`~/.devai-hub/hooks/claude-diff-review.sh`); no existing files are overwritten, no settings.json schema changes, no permission entries added.

*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: The hook depends on Claude Code CLI being on PATH; users on Cursor / Copilot / Codex / Gemini who haven't separately installed Claude Code will get a non-fatal warning on every commit until they install it or set `DEVAI_DIFF_REVIEW_DISABLE=1`. A future minor bump could ship parallel reviewers for other CLIs (e.g. `gh copilot suggest`, `gemini -p`) and select based on which is on PATH. The 50 KB diff cap means very large commits skip review entirely; teams that want full coverage on big commits should either raise the cap (`DEVAI_DIFF_REVIEW_MAX_BYTES=204800`) or move the review to CI rather than pre-commit. The verdict prompt instructs Claude to default-PASS on documentation, lockfiles, and obvious test fixtures, but the LLM's judgment on what counts as "obvious" will produce some false positives until the prompt is tuned against real-world commit data; the WARN verdict (allow with warning) is the intentional escape valve for this. The carryover follow-ups from v1.1.1 (Gemini / Codex / Copilot stale-sentinel bug class in the permission installers; `[System.Environment]::*` family unmatched by `fnmatch`) remain open for a v1.2.0 candidate slate.

*   **Test Posture**: All four quality gates clean. `make validate` (JSON integrity across `data/*.json`) passes. `bash -n` on `claude-diff-review.sh` and `installer.sh` clean. The new test file (`test_claude_diff_review.py`) is 11/11 green; full hook test suite is 273/273 against v1.1.2. The installer-smoke test from v1.1.1 (which now reads the canonical version from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` at runtime) passes against `1.1.2` without a code change - the resilience fix from the prior release is working as designed. No new tests were authored for the slash command itself because the command body is interpreted by Claude at invocation time and is not under unit test (the same pattern as every other slash command in `catalog/commands/`).

*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.2 surfaces shipped. The annotated `v1.1.2` tag is created locally with the release commit; push to origin happens at user direction.

## [2026-05-06] - Release 1.1.1: Commit-Message No-Hard-Wrap Rule + Smoke-Test Robustness

*   **Goal**: Close two small but recurring papercuts shipped to users in v1.1.0. First, `/generate-commit-message` and the `code-commit-workflow` skill enforced a no-hard-wrap rule on bullet points but said nothing about body paragraphs, so the agent kept producing commit messages with paragraph bodies wrapped at ~72 columns - the user had to correct this manually after every commit. Second, the installer-smoke test hard-coded the canonical version string, so every version bump caused the smoke test to fail until a follow-up commit patched the literal. Patch release; no behavioral or schema changes; no installer-rerun side effects.
*   **What Changed**:
    *   **No-hard-wrap rule extended from bullets to all body content** in `catalog/commands/generate-commit-message.md` and `catalog/skills/workflow/code-commit-workflow/SKILL.md`. Both files now require every paragraph and every bullet point in the commit body and footer to be a single continuous source line, regardless of length. The common wrap columns (50, 72, 80, 100) are called out explicitly so the agent cannot rationalize one of them as "the convention." The subject-line 50-character cap remains the only exception (a hard limit, not a wrap).
    *   **Examples reworked** in `code-commit-workflow/SKILL.md` to match the rule. Three "Good Examples" that previously demonstrated wrapped paragraph bodies were unwrapped; a hard-wrapped "Bad Example" was added so the failure mode appears side-by-side with a Good Example. Two new entries in the Common Rationalizations table rebut the "72-column convention" excuse (modern Git tooling, GitHub, GitLab, IDE diff views, and `git log` all soft-wrap on display; hard-wrapped source breaks copy-paste round-trips into changelogs and review comments) and the "split for readability" excuse (visual readability is the renderer's job; if a bullet is genuinely too long, split it into two distinct bullets, not into a continuation line that breaks the bullet's identity in Markdown and Git UIs). Quality Checklist and Verification gain a no-wrap item with a `git show --no-patch HEAD` spot-check.
    *   **Cross-platform reach without an installer edit**: `catalog/commands/generate-commit-message.md` reaches Claude Code (`commands/`), Gemini / Antigravity (`workflows/`), and Codex (`prompts/`) via the installer's recursive copy of `catalog/commands/`. `catalog/skills/workflow/code-commit-workflow/SKILL.md` reaches all five platforms via the skill index in their respective `base-*.md` instruction files. Cursor / OpenCode / Copilot, which do not get a per-command file copy, still inherit the rule because their `base-*.md` instruction templates already carry the global "Never hard-wrap paragraph text" rule and now point at a skill body whose examples and rebuttals are aligned with that rule.
    *   **Installer-smoke test no longer hard-codes the canonical version string** (`catalog/hooks/tests/test_installer_smoke.py`, committed as `3e80f88` between v1.1.0 and v1.1.1). The test now reads the version from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` at test time. Future PATCH / MINOR / MAJOR bumps will not require a follow-up commit to keep the smoke test green - the v1.1.1 bump itself is the first to benefit.
    *   **Canonical 14-file version bump** plus the two installer scripts: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `data/bundles.json`, `data/marketplace.json`, `data/templates.json`, `data/workflows.json`, `catalog/hooks/session-start.sh`, `scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `catalog/skills/README.md`, `guides/reference/SUBAGENTS_GUIDE.md`, `infrastructure/hooks/README.md`, `infrastructure/tools/README.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, plus this DEVLOG entry. CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.1] - 2026-05-06`; CHANGELOG footer Unreleased link bumped to compare from `v1.1.1...HEAD`, and a new `[1.1.1]: v1.1.0...v1.1.1` comparison link added.
*   **Design Rationale**: The bullet-only scope of the original rule was an oversight, not a deliberate scoping decision. The user's `CLAUDE.md` global already carried "Never hard-wrap paragraph text at a fixed column width" as a communication-style rule, but the more specific commit-message guidance in the command and skill files only mentioned bullets - and agents follow the more specific local rule, so the global was effectively shadowed in commit-message generation. The fix is to make the local rule cover the same surface as the global. Adding the explicit column callouts (50, 72, 80, 100) closes off the most common rationalization paths; adding a hard-wrapped Bad Example side-by-side with a Good Example is more durable than a prose rule alone because the agent can pattern-match on shape. The smoke-test fix is a structural improvement: the original test asserted equality against a literal `"1.1.0"`, which is a forward-incompatible coupling between test code and release state. Reading from `plugin.json` makes the test self-updating at every bump.
*   **Migration Impact**: NONE. No file paths changed, no APIs changed, no settings.json schema changed, no permission entries added. Users who installed v1.1.0 will see the new commit-message behavior the next time they invoke `/generate-commit-message` (the command body is re-read on every invocation). The installer can be re-run if desired but is not required for this release - the v1.1.0 install copy of `~/.devai-hub/skills/code-commit-workflow/SKILL.md` is the only file users would refresh, and only because its body content changed.
*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: None opened by v1.1.1. The follow-ups carried over from v1.1.0 remain open: Gemini / Codex / Copilot branches of the permission installers carry the same stale-sentinel bug class as the Claude branch fixed in v1.1.0 (not fixed in v1.1.1 because those branches do not ship new entries in v1.1.1 either); the `[System.Environment]::*` family of read-only patterns cannot be added to the PowerShell allow-list via `fnmatch` because Python interprets `[...]` as a character class. Both are still tracked as v1.2.0 candidates.
*   **Test Posture**: All four quality gates clean. `make validate` (JSON integrity across `data/*.json`) passes. `make lint` (ShellCheck on installer + hooks) carries no new warnings. The installer-smoke test now derives its expected version from `plugin.json` and so passes against `1.1.1` without code changes. No new tests were authored for v1.1.1 because the changeset is documentation-only on the catalog side and a coupling fix on the test side; the catalog files are not under test (they are templates rendered into user-installed paths, validated via the installer-smoke test which already covers the destination structure).
*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.1 surfaces shipped. The annotated `v1.1.1` tag is created locally with the release commit; push to origin happens at user direction.

## [2026-05-05] - Release 1.1.0: PowerShell Tool Parity + Known-Gaps Tracker

*   **Goal**: Close the description-and-auto-approve UX gap for Claude Code's PowerShell tool, which until this release got no description treatment at all - approval dialogs only showed the truncated start of the script body, leaving the user to click "Details" before they could understand what the agent was about to run. The Bash tool has had this treatment since v0.9.x via `format-bash-description.py` + `require-description.sh`. v1.1.0 ships the PowerShell parallel and bundles in the per-version known-gaps tracker authored earlier in the cycle. Minor bump: changes are additive; existing Bash-only configurations are unaffected.
*   **What Changed**:
    *   **PowerShell description hook pair**: `catalog/hooks/require-powershell-description.sh` (direct port of the Bash twin - blocks calls with no `description` field) and `catalog/hooks/format-powershell-description.py` (~270 lines, slimmer than the Bash twin: no shell-construct/env-var/prefix-cmd unwrapping, conservative single-line allow-list). The format hook prepends a `# ===== Description ===== #` comment block to the script body so the description stays visible in the truncated approval-dialog preview, since Claude Code does not surface the `description` field in the PowerShell approval header today (unlike Bash). Both register under `"matcher": "PowerShell"` in `catalog/hooks/settings.json`.
    *   **PowerShell auto-approve allow-list** (~100 patterns) added to `configs/permissions/claude-permissions.json`: read-only `Get-*`, `Test-*`, `Resolve-*`, `Format-*`, `Select-*`, `Sort-*`, `Group-*`, `Measure-*`, `ConvertFrom-*` / `ConvertTo-*`, `Where-Object` (comparison-statement form only), CIM/WMI getters, network info getters, hashing, and the common aliases (`ls`, `dir`, `cat`, `pwd`, `gci`, `gc`, `gm`, `sls`, ...).
    *   **Conservative-by-default safety model**. A PowerShell command auto-approves only when ALL of these hold: single line (no `\n`), no script-block characters (`{` `}`), no statement separator (`;`), no I/O redirection (`>` `<`), no subexpression (`$(`, `@(`, `@{`), no call operator (`&`), no backtick (`` ` ``) outside single-quoted strings - and `$(` and backticks are also rejected inside double-quoted strings because PowerShell interpolates and escapes there. Multi-line scripts never auto-approve. `ForEach-Object` is intentionally excluded because `ForEach-Object Name` (property access, safe) and `ForEach-Object Delete` (method invocation, destructive) are syntactically indistinguishable.
    *   **Installer wiring**: both `scripts/installer.sh` and `scripts/installer.ps1` extended to copy the two new hook files by explicit name (per the project's "installer copies scripts by explicit name, never by folder" rule) and to merge two new PowerShell PreToolUse entries into existing settings.json. The merge logic checks `require-powershell-description` separately from `require-description` so an upgrade path that already has the Bash hook still picks up the PowerShell pair without skipping. The fresh-install path inherits the new entries automatically from the updated `catalog/hooks/settings.json` template.
    *   **MANDATORY rule extension** in `templates/ai-instructions/base-claude.md`. Codex / Gemini / Cursor / OpenCode templates are unchanged because none of those agents expose a PowerShell-specific tool - the cross-platform consistency rule applies to platform-agnostic behavior, not platform-specific features.
    *   **Test coverage**: new `catalog/hooks/tests/test_format_powershell_description.py` with 80 tests covering the pipeline splitter, quote-aware syntax scanner, allow-list matcher, real-config integration (parametrized over safe and unsafe command samples), description-box rendering, and end-to-end subprocess flow. Combined hook test suite: 261 tests passing.
    *   **Known-gaps tracker** (shipped earlier in the cycle as a separate commit, bundled into v1.1.0): `catalog/skills/workflow/known-gaps-tracker/SKILL.md` plus integrations across `/implement-phase` (Phase 8 step 2), `/wrap-up-session` (Phase 4 Step 4b sweep + Phase 6 Step 6b finalize), and `/generate-plan` (Step 0.6 prior-version known-gaps ingest). Per-version, append-only log at `docs/<version>/known-gaps.md` recording NI / DF / BG / WN / MT / QG items. Files flip from `in-progress` to `finalized` on version bump. The next `/generate-plan` ingests open items and seeds them into the discovery interview.
    *   **Stale-sentinel bug in Claude permission installer (caught during v1.1.0 verification)**: real-session test against the v1.1.0 install showed that the user's `~/.claude/settings.json` had received the new PreToolUse hook entries but had ZERO new `PowerShell(...)` allow patterns despite the catalog template carrying ~100 of them. Root cause: the Claude branch of all three permission installers (`scripts/installer.sh` line 433, `scripts/installer.ps1` line 724, `scripts/Install-DevAI-Permissions.ps1` line 120) used a single hard-coded sentinel string (`Bash(gh pr list)` / `WebFetch(domain:api.github.com)` / `WebFetch(domain:github.com)`) to detect "permissions already installed" and skip the entire merge. Any user who installed v0.9.5+ would have one of these sentinels and would never receive any allow-list entry shipped in later versions. Fix: replaced the binary sentinel with a count-based delta - the installer computes how many of the template entries are not already present, skips the file write entirely when the delta is zero, and writes (with a backup) plus reports `(N new entries)` when the delta is positive. The Gemini / Codex / Copilot branches in the same files have the same bug pattern but do not ship new entries in v1.1.0; tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed in this release.
    *   **PowerShell dialog UI doesn't render `updatedInput.command` like Bash does (caught during v1.1.0 verification)**: third real-session test exposed yet another Bash-vs-PowerShell asymmetry. For Bash, the format hook's `updatedInput.command` (with the `# ===== Description ===== #` comment block prepended) renders directly under the dialog header so the user sees what the command does without expanding any panel. For PowerShell, the same `updatedInput.command` is hidden inside a collapsed "Details" panel - the dialog body shows only the generic "Do you want to proceed with PowerShell?" header. Fix: the hook now also writes the model-supplied description into `permissionDecisionReason`, which Claude Code renders in the dialog body for both tools. Auto-approved commands keep the existing reason text ("All pipeline segments match configured allow patterns") so the audit trail still distinguishes them; non-allow-listed commands carry the description verbatim. Two updated regression tests in `test_format_powershell_description.py` assert this. Full hook test suite is still 262 tests passing.
    *   **Extra read-only automatic-variable patterns added to allow-list (caught during v1.1.0 verification)**: same real-session test showed the model reaching for `$PWD.Path` when asked for a read-only command. The cmdlet equivalent `Get-Location` was in the allow-list and auto-approved; the property-access form `$PWD.Path` was not, so the user got an extra approval dialog they did not expect. Added `$PWD`, `$PWD.Path`, `$PWD.ProviderPath`, `$HOME`, `$PROFILE`, `$PID`, `$Host.Version`, `$Host.Name`, `$Host.UI.RawUI.WindowSize`, `$ExecutionContext.SessionState.Path.CurrentLocation` and the verbose forms of `$PSVersionTable` to `configs/permissions/claude-permissions.json`. Skipped `[System.Environment]::*` family because Python's `fnmatch` treats `[...]` as a character class - the literal `[` in a pattern is interpreted as the start of a set match, so a static pattern can never match these expressions. If we ever need to allow them, we would need to either escape the brackets via fnmatch's `[[]` syntax or move the matcher off `fnmatch`. Tracked as a follow-up.
    *   **PowerShell hook now returns `permissionDecision: "ask"` for non-allow-listed commands (caught during v1.1.0 verification)**: same real-session test exposed a more dangerous bug - even after manually verifying the hook ran (transcript showed `PreToolUse:PowerShell hook_success` events with our exact comment-block JSON), Claude Code was executing destructive commands like `Set-Content -Path "hello.txt" -Value "hello world"` without ever showing the approval dialog. Diagnosis by transcript-replay: when a `PreToolUse:PowerShell` hook returns `updatedInput` without an explicit `permissionDecision`, Claude Code's PowerShell tool treats the absence of a decision as approval and runs the command silently. The Bash tool falls through to a default-ask path in the same scenario; the PowerShell tool does not. Fix: when our hook decides NOT to auto-approve, it now explicitly emits `{"permissionDecision": "ask", "permissionDecisionReason": "PowerShell command not in auto-approve allow-list", "updatedInput": {...}}`. The comment-block envelope is still rendered into the script body so the description stays visible in the truncated approval-dialog preview, but the `"ask"` decision forces Claude Code to gate execution on user approval. New regression test in `test_format_powershell_description.py` asserts the `ask` decision is set for any non-allow-listed command; another test asserts the same when the description is already pre-formatted. Full hook test suite is now 262 tests passing.
    *   **Post-install restart reminder** in both `scripts/installer.sh` and `scripts/installer.ps1`. Surfaced after a real test caught the trap: the developer ran the installer, saw the "Installation Complete" banner, but the new PowerShell hook still didn't fire in their already-running Claude Code session. Diagnosis: hook files were copied byte-identical, settings.json was correctly merged with the new PowerShell PreToolUse entries, but Claude Code reads settings.json at session start and does not hot-reload it (upstream blocker tracked at `anthropics/claude-code#17127`). Fix is documentation-only on the catalog side - the installer's "Installation Complete" path now prints a yellow notice telling the user to restart any running Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini / Codex / Copilot sessions. Same notice mirrored in the v1.1.0 CHANGELOG and README "What's New" upgrade-note callout. This same blocker was previously hit during v0.9.7 Phase 5 (effort-level hot-reload) and remained in memory; v1.1.0 makes the limitation visible at install time so future users do not lose 10 minutes diagnosing what looks like a hook bug but is actually a session-cache issue.
*   **Design Rationale**: The single most important judgment call in this release was the conservative-by-default allow-list scope. PowerShell's universal script-block syntax (`{ ... }`) means `Where-Object {$_.Foo -eq 'x'}` (filter, safe) and `ForEach-Object { Remove-Item $_ }` (destructive) look syntactically identical at the regex level. Rather than write a full PowerShell parser into the format hook, the rule blocks ANY `{` outside single-quoted strings and accepts that `Where-Object` and friends only work in their modern comparison-statement form (`Where-Object Name -eq foo`). Same for `ForEach-Object`: rather than try to distinguish property access from method invocation, the cmdlet is excluded from the allow-list entirely. The cost is that some legitimate read-only patterns require manual approval; the benefit is that the safety model is provably correct without parsing PowerShell. The Bash twin's complexity (~860 lines handling shell constructs, env-var prefixes, command unwrapping, output-redirect detection, `bash -c` extraction) was deliberately not ported - the PowerShell hook is one-third the length and a fraction of the surface area for bugs. The 14-file canonical version-bump surface from v0.9.7 / v1.0.0 is reused; no new bump targets needed.
*   **Migration Impact**: NONE for users who only use the Bash tool - the PowerShell hooks are gated by the `"matcher": "PowerShell"` in settings.json. Users who already have the Bash description hooks installed will pick up the PowerShell pair on the next installer run. Users who don't run the installer keep the v1.0.0 behavior (PowerShell calls land in approval dialogs without a description) until they install. No breaking changes; no API changes; no destructive operations.
*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: The format hook only auto-approves single-line PowerShell commands. Multi-line scripts always require manual approval, even when every line is read-only. This is a deliberate scope choice for v1.1.0; a more sophisticated multi-line analyzer (or a "trusted multi-line script template" allow-list) could land in a future release if usage telemetry shows it would meaningfully reduce friction. `ForEach-Object` is also outside the allow-list pending a clean way to distinguish its property-access form from its method-invocation form without parsing PowerShell. The Gemini / Codex / Copilot branches of the permission installers (`scripts/installer.sh`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `scripts/Install-DevAI-Permissions.ps1`) carry the same stale-sentinel bug class as the Claude branch fixed in v1.1.0; not fixed in this release because those branches do not ship new entries in v1.1.0, but tracked as a follow-up. The `[System.Environment]::*` family of read-only patterns can never be added via `fnmatch` because Python interprets `[...]` as a character class - if those patterns ever become important, the matcher would need either fnmatch's `[[]` literal-bracket escape or a different matching engine.

    **Claude Code upstream rendering inconsistency (acknowledged limitation):** the PowerShell approval dialog renders an empty body when a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: "ask"`, while the Bash dialog renders the hook-prepended comment block under the header. Three output surfaces tested (`updatedInput.command`, `updatedInput.description`, `permissionDecisionReason`) - none reach the PowerShell dialog body. The description still reaches the user via the chat IN block, the expanded `Details ▾` panel, and the audit trail, but is one click less prominent than for Bash. v1.1.0 ships with this limitation documented prominently in CHANGELOG and README; the safety guarantee (destructive commands gate on approval) holds regardless. The alternative - dropping `permissionDecision: "ask"` to "make the box visible like Bash" - was rejected because empirical testing shows that without an explicit `ask`, Claude Code's PowerShell tool auto-executes destructive commands without any dialog at all. Better to ship a working safety gate with a UX rough edge than a leaky safety gate with prettier dialogs. Upstream issue to be filed against `anthropics/claude-code`.
*   **Test Posture**: 261 tests passing across `catalog/hooks/tests/` (179 prior + 80 new + 2 from existing parity / smoke suites - net 261). All four quality gates clean: `make validate` JSON integrity (skills.json / templates.json / bundles.json / marketplace.json all parse), `make lint` ShellCheck `--severity=warning` (new `require-powershell-description.sh` clean, installer.sh clean), `python -m py_compile` on `format-powershell-description.py` clean, end-to-end installer dry-run not needed (file copies are additive, settings.json merge is gated on per-hook `grep` checks).
*   **Current Status**: All v1.1.0 surfaces shipped. 14-file version-bump complete (`data/marketplace.json`, `data/templates.json`, `data/bundles.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `catalog/hooks/session-start.sh`, `catalog/skills/README.md`, `guides/reference/SUBAGENTS_GUIDE.md`, `infrastructure/hooks/README.md`, `infrastructure/tools/README.md`). CHANGELOG migrated from `[Unreleased]` to `[1.1.0] - 2026-05-05`. The annotated `v1.1.0` tag is created locally with this release commit; push to origin happens immediately per user direction.

## [2026-04-27] - Release 1.0.0: Reverse-Engineering-First Security Hardening

*   **Goal**: Ship the first stable release of DevAI-Hub. The release theme is "reverse-engineer locally first; trusted vendor wrappers only when reverse-engineering is infeasible AND the feature is extremely worth it." The driving constraint was that the registry's existing third-party MCP entries (search-as-service, embeddings-as-service, scraping-as-service, generation-as-service) caused users' agents to ship proprietary source code, prompts, and queries to external data processors - unacceptable for the regulated-industry / high-trust profile this release primarily targets. The 12-phase plan at [docs/archives/v1/v1.0/plans/security-hardening-v100.md](v1.0.0/plans/security-hardening-v100.md) addresses the policy gap, builds two new internal MCP servers as reverse-engineered replacements, bakes a security-and-RE-assessment section into `/compare-project` so the same mistake cannot recur on future adoption exercises, and ships under v1.0.0 because the breadth of changes (policy + 2 new MCPs + 3 new skills + breaking removals + command-level workflow change) is a major-version event. The version bump skips 0.9.8 entirely - what would have been a patch release accumulated into a major release.
*   **What Changed** (grouped by phase from the security-hardening plan):
    *   **Phase 0 - Revert and abandon the v0.9.8 adoption plan**: removed the `claude-context` registry entry that was added in an aborted Phase 2 of the prior plan; deleted the Phase 2 session-history file (uncommitted, no diff); removed the corresponding DEVLOG entry; prepended an ABANDONED header to `docs/v0.9.7/plans/adoption-claude-context.md` with a forward-link to the v1.0.0 successor plan. Materialized the durable plan via `/generate-plan` to `docs/archive/v1/v1.0/plans/security-hardening-v100.md` (1255 lines, 12 phases). Commit `6d9b696`.
    *   **Phase 1 - MCP Registry Policy with reverse-engineering-first decision tree**: authored `## MCP Registry Policy` in `AGENTS.md` (decision tree: local-only -> LLM-native skill -> reverse-engineered internal MCP -> trusted vendor wrapper -> drop; 5-question audit checklist; hard-no list). Distributed the condensed summary diff-identical to all 7 platform-instruction surfaces (`base-claude.md`, `base-codex.md`, `base-cursor.md`, `base-gemini.md`, `base-opencode.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/devai-hub.mdc`). Commit `112b46a`.
    *   **Phase 2 - Reverse-Engineering Matrix**: authored `docs/policy/mcp-reverse-engineering-matrix.md` - the authoritative classification document for every MCP shipped or considered. 18 rows organized into 5 sections (already-local, dropped, vendor-intrinsic, new-internal, reverted). Each row cites upstream evidence and names its v1.0.0 deliverable. Commit `484e3b4`.
    *   **Phase 3 - Apply matrix to registry + integration docs**: stripped 4 third-party entries from `mcp-servers.json` (`context7`, `exa-web-search`, `firecrawl`, `magic-ui`); inlined the 5-question audit into the `_comment` of every kept vendor-intrinsic entry; rewrote `guides/reference/MCP_DEVELOPMENT_SERVERS.md` and shortened `infrastructure/integrations/README.md` (601 -> 180 lines) for policy-compliance. Commit `6505164`.
    *   **Phase 4 - De-brand Phase 1 skill content**: rewrote four locations in `catalog/skills/ai-development/rag-implementation/SKILL.md` to strip every external-source attribution while preserving the technical patterns. Renamed "Canonical OSS Reference" to "Hybrid Retrieval in Practice"; dropped the `Zilliz Cloud` row; generalized the embedding-provider table; removed upstream file-path citations from the AST and Merkle subsections. Concrete references now point at the internal `devai-code-search` MCP. Commit `7967f44`.
    *   **Phase 5 - `/compare-project` extension with RE-first `/generate-plan` handoff**: inserted a new mandatory Section 9 "Security and Risk Assessment" (4 subsections: threat model, per-item risk scorecard, RE viability, recommendation ordering); renumbered downstream sections; updated Step 8 to always pass `reverse-engineer-first=true`; updated the backing skill's Quality Checklist; added Step 0.5f to `/generate-plan` to handle the RE-first flag. Commit `5bc017a`.
    *   **Phase 6 - Build `devai-code-search` MVP (keyword-only)**: shipped `extensions/devai-code-search/` (~1,000 LOC across 8 source files + 5 test files). Tools: `index_codebase`, `search_code`, `clear_index`, `get_indexing_status`. Inverted index + rapidfuzz keyword retrieval, content-hash incremental indexing, `.gitignore` + `.devaiignore` respect, advisory file-lock for concurrent indexers, recursive character splitter. 35 pytest tests passing in 1.5s. Zero outbound calls. CI extended to install + test the package. Commit `1580524`.
    *   **Phase 7 - Build `devai-web-fetch` + LLM-native skill replacements**: shipped `extensions/devai-web-fetch/` (~300 LOC + 17 tests covering SSRF denylist, redirect handling, three extract modes, fixture HTTP server). Authored two new skills under `catalog/skills/`: `ui-component-generation` (replaces `magic-ui`) and `local-docs-lookup` (partial replacement for `context7`). Registered both in the 3 registry files. Commit `43873be`.
    *   **Phase 8 - Reverse-engineered `code-semantic-search` skill**: authored `catalog/skills/ai-development/code-semantic-search/SKILL.md` (135 lines). All technical content; zero external attribution. References the internal `devai-code-search` MCP throughout. Registered in `data/SKILL_INDEX.md`, `data/skills.json`, `data/marketplace.json`. Skill count moved 186 -> 187. Commit `d85fe1c`.
    *   **Phase 9 - Cross-link context-manager and context-engineering**: added one Related Skills entry in each of the two skills pointing at `code-semantic-search`, framed as the escape valve when the repo exceeds the model's context window. Commit `e6d8343`.
    *   **Phase 10 - Internal MCP benchmark harness**: shipped `scripts/devai_mcp_benchmark.py` (~320 LOC) exercising all 3 internal MCPs through their handler functions. Includes a no-network-guard context manager that monkeypatches `socket.socket.connect` to raise on outbound attempts during the local-only MCP phases. Added `make benchmark` target; pytest coverage with 13 tests; both installers register the script. Commit `ed98b54`.
    *   **Phase 11 (pre-release polish) - security review fixes + style-guide relocation + 14-file version bump**: ran `/security-review` and identified 3 HIGH-severity findings, all fixed in this phase: (a) pickle deserialization RCE in `devai-code-search/store.py` -> replaced with JSON; (b) SSRF via `follow_redirects=True` in `devai-web-fetch/fetcher.py` -> manual redirect loop with per-hop revalidation; (c) SSRF via DNS rebinding in `ssrf_guard.py` -> new `pin_hostname_to_ip` context manager that monkeypatches `socket.getaddrinfo` for the duration of each fetch. Each fix carries regression tests. Separately, both `compile-deep-research-style-guide.md` and `generate-report-style-guide.md` were surfacing as slash commands - relocated to `catalog/style-guides/` (sibling of `catalog/commands/`). Convention updated across `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/devai-hub.mdc`. Both installers now ship `catalog/style-guides/` to `~/.devai-hub/style-guides/`. 14-file version bump (canonical list per MEMORY.md `project_release_v097`) from 0.9.7 -> 1.0.0; CHANGELOG migrated [Unreleased] -> [1.0.0]. Commit `66e3f86`.
    *   **Phase 11 (post-pen-test) - symlink fix**: `/run-penetration-test --depth=deep` against the new attack surface verified the 3 prior HIGH fixes hold and identified one new MEDIUM finding: `walk_files` in `devai-code-search/indexer.py` followed symlinks, which could leak files outside the indexed root when indexing untrusted repositories (e.g., a malicious repo's `keys -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa`). Fixed: added `if entry.is_symlink(): continue` at the entry loop. Regression test added (skipped on Windows where symlink creation requires elevation). Pen test report at [docs/security/penetration-test-2026-04-27.md](security/penetration-test-2026-04-27.md). Commit `2a756e2`.
    *   **Phase 11 (post-tag preparation) - `/run-deep-review` command + workflow documentation**: shipped a new `catalog/commands/run-deep-review.md` slash command authored in a parallel session - a 12-phase pre-release deep-review orchestrator that chains known-gaps collection, health gates, dependency scan, docs/git hygiene, project validators, `/analyze-codebase`, `/run-security-audit`, `/run-penetration-test --depth=deep`, and `/review-codebase` into a single run. Synthesizes findings (P0-P3) into one severity-ranked report with a GO / GO-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-GO verdict, then chains into `/generate-plan` for the remediation roadmap. All artifacts centralized under `docs/<next-version>/review/`. Use this before cutting a major or minor release. Also added two practical workflow sections to `README.md` (English + Chinese): "New Project Workflow" (5 phases: Planning -> Project Setup -> Development -> QA -> Release) and "Inherited Project Workflow" (Primary Analysis & Deep Review -> Making Changes), giving users opinionated end-to-end starting points. Updated CHANGELOG, RELEASE_NOTES, CATALOG-COVERAGE, llms.txt to reflect the new command.
*   **Design Rationale**: The release implements four mutually-reinforcing decisions that together close the data-leak gap: (1) policy text in `AGENTS.md` defines what qualifies an MCP for the registry; (2) the matrix at `docs/policy/mcp-reverse-engineering-matrix.md` is the authoritative classification for every entry past, present, and proposed; (3) the two new internal MCPs (`devai-code-search`, `devai-web-fetch`) demonstrate that reverse-engineering popular third-party services into local-only equivalents is tractable and ships at acceptable cost; (4) the `/compare-project` Section 9 extension forces every future adoption exercise through the same gate, preventing reintroduction of third-party data-processor entries. The "skip 0.9.8" version bump signals that this is not a patch but a major-version security retrofit. The de-branding work (Phase 4) addresses a subtle but important point: even *naming* a third-party project in skill content can be a soft endorsement that conflicts with the no-vendor-attribution clause of the policy.
*   **Migration Impact**: BREAKING for users who relied on the 4 dropped third-party MCP registry entries. Migration path is documented in the `[1.0.0]` CHANGELOG section and in `docs/archive/v1/v1.0/RELEASE_NOTES.md`: users can re-add the snippets to their own `.claude/settings.json` if they accept the data-flow tradeoff; DevAI-Hub no longer ships them. Slash command surface narrows by two: `/compile-deep-research-style-guide` and `/generate-report-style-guide` no longer appear (these were never intended as user-facing slash commands; they are reference content for the agent running the parent commands). 14-file version-bump sweep skipped 0.9.8 cleanly.
*   **Known Issues / Follow-ups**: 3 informational items deferred to v1.0.1: (a) README prompt-injection caveat for tools that return external content (`devai-web-fetch`, `devai-code-search`); (b) port allowlist in `GuardConfig` for `devai-web-fetch` (defense-in-depth, no concrete exploit path); (c) file-lock TOCTOU on networked filesystems (operational reliability, no security boundary crossed). Dense / hybrid retrieval on `devai-code-search` (with local ONNX embeddings via `fastembed` + `sqlite-vec` vector store) is planned for v1.1.0 per the matrix. Vendor-wrapper reverse-engineering (`devai-github`, `devai-supabase`, etc.) is matrixed for v1.1.0+ and gated on demand signal.
*   **Test Posture**: 275+ tests passing across the four test surfaces - skill-server (37), code-search (36 + 1 platform-skip), web-fetch (23), catalog/hooks (179). All 4 quality gates clean: `make validate` JSON integrity, `make lint` ShellCheck, `make test` pytest, `make benchmark` MCP latency. Both installers parse cleanly (`bash -n`, ShellCheck `--severity=warning`, PowerShell AST). Pre-existing PSUseApprovedVerbs warnings in `installer.ps1` predate v1.0.0; no new instances introduced.
*   **Current Status**: All 12 plan phases shipped. Pre-release polish bundle (security review fixes + pen test fix + style-guide relocation + version bump + docs sync) committed across 4 commits (`66e3f86`, `2a756e2`, plus this DEVLOG entry's commit and the final release artifacts commit). The annotated `v1.0.0` tag is created locally by the final release commit; push is gated on user confirmation per the destructive-command rule.

## [2026-04-10] - Release 0.9.5: generate-todos Command and Configurable Extension Thresholds

*   **Goal**: Ship a patch release that adds a new catalog command for project progress bootstrapping and delivers a significant UX upgrade to the claude-usage-monitor VS Code extension -- making thresholds, colors, and metric selection fully user-configurable without editing raw JSON.
*   **What Changed**:
    *   **`generate-todos` Command** (`catalog/commands/generate-todos.md`): New command that analyzes git history, existing docs, and code annotations to bootstrap a structured `docs/todos.md` progress tracker for inherited or under-documented projects. Complements the `dev-progress-tracker` skill added in 0.9.4 by providing the initial population step.
    *   **claude-usage-monitor Settings Panel** (`extensions/claude-usage-monitor/src/settingsPanel.ts`): New `Claude Usage: Settings` command opens a dedicated webview panel with form controls for all configurable urgency thresholds, status bar colors, and the threshold metric. Settings are written directly to the global VS Code configuration without requiring the user to open `settings.json`.
    *   **Configurable Thresholds and Colors** (`extensions/claude-usage-monitor/src/types.ts`, `src/statusBarManager.ts`, `src/recommendations.ts`, `src/extension.ts`): Urgency thresholds (moderate/high/critical percentages) and status bar background colors are now read from VS Code settings (`claudeUsage.thresholds.*`, `claudeUsage.colors.*`) with hardcoded defaults as fallback. Legacy enum values (`"warning"`, `"error"`) stored by older builds are auto-migrated to hex on read.
    *   **`thresholdMetric` Setting**: New `claudeUsage.thresholdMetric` setting (`"highest"` | `"session"` | `"weekly"` | `"sonnet"`) controls which usage metric drives urgency evaluation and threshold notifications. Defaults to `"highest"` (previous hardcoded behavior) for zero-config backwards compatibility.
    *   **Extension Version Bump**: claude-usage-monitor bumped from 0.3.2 to 0.4.0 (minor bump warranted by the addition of the settings panel command and fully configurable threshold/color system).
    *   **CI Fix** (`catalog/hooks/`): Corrected SC2088 tilde-expansion issue and missing trailing newline in hook/CI scripts that caused ShellCheck warnings.
    *   **Main Version Bump**: Updated `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `README.md` from 0.9.4 to 0.9.5.
*   **Design Rationale**: The hardcoded 50/75/90 thresholds and fixed status bar colors were the top friction point for users whose usage patterns didn't align with the defaults. A settings panel was preferred over raw settings.json because it provides immediate color preview and eliminates JSON syntax errors. The `generate-todos` command closes the gap between having the `dev-progress-tracker` skill (which maintains an existing `todos.md`) and having no `todos.md` to start from in an inherited codebase.
*   **Current Status**: Verified. All version references consistent at 0.9.5.

*   **Design Rationale**: The agent-skills comparison (`docs/v0.9.2/comparison-agent-skills.md`) identified three structural gaps in DevAI-Hub: (1) no Define-phase skills (`idea-refine`, `spec-driven-development`), (2) no Ship-phase skills (`shipping-and-launch`), and (3) no session lifecycle management (`wrap-up-session`, SessionStart hook). The 9 new skills and session workflow commands directly address all three gaps. The skill anatomy improvements (Common Rationalizations + Verification) adopt the quality pattern that makes agent-skills skills more reliably executed.

*   **Goal**: Remove the manual `claudeUsage.currentModel` VS Code setting and replace it with automatic detection from Claude Code's own model picker (`claudeCode.selectedModel`), while making the extension forward-compatible with any model ID format including 1M extended-context variants.

## [2026-02-19] - CLI Usage Limits Display (Stop Hook)

*   **Goal**: Address user feedback requesting token limit visibility in the CLI. Users could see tokens consumed but had to navigate to `claude.ai/settings/usage` to see how close they were to their cap.
*   **What Changed**:
    *   **Usage Display Hook**: Created `catalog/hooks/usage-display.sh` (Stop hook, 213 lines) that fetches from the Anthropic OAuth API, caches responses for 5 minutes, and displays a compact color-coded summary to stderr when any metric exceeds 50%. Includes graceful degradation (silent exit) for missing curl/jq, missing credentials, expired tokens, and network errors.
    *   **Hook Config**: Updated `catalog/hooks/settings.json` with Stop hook entry alongside existing PreToolUse.
    *   **Installer Integration**: Added `install_usage_display` (Bash) and `Install-UsageDisplay` (PowerShell) functions to both installers. Installed in both global (Phase 1) and workspace (Phase 2) with idempotent settings.json merge.
    *   **Check-Usage Enhancement**: Added Phase 0 auto-fetch to `catalog/commands/check-usage.md`. The command now reads OAuth credentials and calls the API directly via curl before falling back to manual entry.
    *   **Documentation**: Added "Usage Display (Stop Hook)" section to `infrastructure/hooks/README.md` with configuration, customization, and cross-references to the VS Code extension and `/check-usage` command.
*   **Design Decisions**:
    *   50% smart threshold (silent when healthy, visible when it matters)
    *   5-minute cache TTL to prevent API spam
    *   3-second curl timeout to never block the CLI
    *   Reused the same Anthropic OAuth API endpoint as the VS Code extension (`usageFetcher.ts`)
*   **Current Status**: Implemented. Three complementary usage monitoring features now exist: automatic CLI hook (passive), VS Code extension (visual), and `/check-usage` command (on-demand).

## [2026-02-10 12:00] - Created Claude Usage Monitor VS Code Extension

*   **Goal**: Build a VS Code extension that monitors Claude Code API usage (session and weekly limits) with auto-fetching, a status bar indicator, rich tooltip, and a full dashboard panel.
*   **Attempted Solutions**:
    *   *Icon Font Generation (fantasticon)*:
        *   *Result*: Failed. fantasticon v4.x reported "No SVGs found" regardless of path format, even in a temp directory without spaces. Version self-reported as "0.0.0".
        *   *Analysis*: fantasticon's glob resolution is broken in v4.x on Windows.
        *   *Solution*: Bypassed fantasticon entirely. Wrote custom `scripts/generate-icon-font.js` using `svgpath` + `svg2ttf` + `ttf2woff2`. Key insight: SVG fonts have Y-axis going UP (opposite of regular SVGs), requiring `svgpath(path).scale(64, -64).translate(0, 1024)` for 16px to 1024 unitsPerEm conversion.
    *   *Tooltip Progress Bars (HTML divs)*:
        *   *Result*: Failed. VS Code MarkdownString tooltips do not render `background` CSS on content-less `<div>` elements. `<table>` width attributes are also ignored.
        *   *Analysis*: VS Code's tooltip renderer has a limited CSS subset. Properties like `background`, `color`, `opacity`, and `font-style` on arbitrary HTML elements are unreliable.
        *   *Solution*: Switched to SVG data URI images via `<img src="data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}">`. This renders reliably when `isTrusted` and `supportHtml` are true.
    *   *Percentage Right-Alignment (HTML tables)*:
        *   *Result*: Failed. HTML `<table width="260">` was not respected by VS Code's tooltip. Percentages appeared next to labels instead of at the far right edge.
        *   *Solution*: Baked label, percentage, AND progress bar into a single SVG image using `text-anchor="end"` for guaranteed pixel-perfect right alignment.
    *   *PowerShell Installer Phase 3*:
        *   *Result*: Initially failed. `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` converted npm/npx stderr output into terminating PowerShell exceptions.
        *   *Solution*: Wrap native CLI tool sections with `$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"` and restore afterward. Use `2>$null | Out-Null` instead of `2>&1 | Out-Null` for stderr suppression.
*   **Changes**:
    *   Created `extensions/claude-usage-monitor/` (full extension, 22 files):
        *   `src/usageFetcher.ts`: Reads OAuth token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, calls `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header, maps response to internal types.
        *   `src/statusBarManager.ts`: Status bar with `$(claude-icon)` custom icon, `X% (current) Y% (week)` format, SVG data URI tooltip with theme-aware colors via `activeColorTheme.kind`, auto-refresh timer.
        *   `src/dashboardPanel.ts`: WebviewPanel with full usage breakdown, model recommendations, optimization tips, theme-aware tab icons via `{ light: Uri, dark: Uri }` iconPath.
        *   `src/extension.ts`: Orchestrates auto-fetch on activation, registers commands (`dashboard`, `refresh`, `update`, `reset`), configures auto-refresh interval.
        *   `src/inputCollector.ts`: Manual input fallback (4-step wizard) when API credentials are unavailable.
        *   `src/recommendations.ts`: Usage-based model switching recommendations (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku).
        *   `scripts/generate-icon-font.js`: Custom SVG-to-WOFF2 font generator.
        *   `icons/claude.svg`, `icons/claude-dark.svg`, `icons/claude-light.svg`: Theme-aware icon variants.
        *   `fonts/claude-icons.woff2`: Generated icon font at codepoint U+E101.
    *   Modified `scripts/installer.ps1`: Added Phase 3 (extension build, VSIX packaging, VS Code installation with Node.js detection).
    *   Modified `scripts/installer.sh`: Added Phase 3 (same logic for macOS/Linux with brew/apt detection).
    *   Created `catalog/commands/check-usage.md`: CLI command for checking usage from the terminal.
    *   Added `catalog/claude_icon.svg`, `catalog/claude_logo.png`: Icon assets.
    *   Modified `skills.json`: Registered `check-usage` command.
*   **Lessons Learned**:
    *   VS Code MarkdownString tooltips support `<img>` tags with `data:image/svg+xml` URIs but do NOT reliably support CSS `background`, `color`, `opacity`, or `font-style` on HTML elements. Tables render but ignore width attributes. The most reliable approach for custom graphics in tooltips is inline SVG data URIs.
    *   fantasticon v4.x is unusable on Windows. A custom script with `svgpath` + `svg2ttf` + `ttf2woff2` is more reliable and produces smaller output.
    *   PowerShell `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` must be temporarily disabled when invoking npm, npx, node, or any native CLI tool that writes to stderr as part of normal operation.
    *   The Claude OAuth usage API lives at `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` (not `claude.ai`), requires the `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header, and returns `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_sonnet`, `seven_day_opus`, and `extra_usage` fields each with `utilization` (0-100) and `resets_at` (ISO 8601).
*   **Current Status**: Verified. Extension builds, packages, installs, and runs correctly. Auto-fetch populates status bar on activation. Tooltip shows SVG progress bars with theme-aware colors. Dashboard opens with Claude icon on tab. Manual fallback works when credentials are missing.

        *   `context-analysis`: Added dual-mode support, git-changes preflight, edge case handling (>500 lines batching), critical path identification.
